Economy in 72 hours

Learn every fact the Economy past papers test in 72 hours before 6 December 2026: one hour at a time, in order. Every hour mixes learning, recall and questions from earlier hours, so facts come back just as you start to forget them.

Each learn hour (60 min): read the key facts and the hour's questions with their answers (30) · cover the answers and recall the grey boxes (10) · answer this hour's questions (10) · answer the spaced-review questions from 1, 3, 7, 15 and 30 hours ago and your weak questions (10).
Revise hours: every Must-know fact, then your weak questions, then look-alike traps.
Mock tests: 30 real Uttar Pradesh paper questions in 25 minutes. Review every mistake afterwards.

Hour 1 of 72 · Learn

Nature of Indian Economy

13 facts · 18 questions · 3 Must know

Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
  • Mixed economy means:Where public sector and private sector co-exist in the national economy

Mixed economy → public sector and private sector co-exist in the national economy; blends market economy with planned economy. Must know

Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

  • Indian Economy is:Mixed economy

Indian economy → mixed economy (its main characteristic); combines aspects of capitalism and socialism. Must know

Don't confuse With socialist or Gandhian socialist economy; India is a mixed economy.

Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

  • It will be true to classify India as:A labour-surplus economy

India → labour-surplus economy: large population and unlimited workers willing to work at a subsistence wage.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • An underdeveloped economy is generally characterized by: I. Low per capita income II. Low rate of capital formation III. Low dependency ratio IV. Work force largely in the tertiary sector Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:I and II

Underdeveloped economy → low per capita income and low rate of capital formation; low dependency ratio and tertiary-heavy workforce are not its features.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Which of the following correctly explains that India is an underdeveloped economy?None of these

India underdeveloped → inequitable income distribution, high dependency ratio, slower national income growth; change in banking/financial sector is not a sign. Code: none of these.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Which of the following features indicates that Indian economy is in a developing category? I. Occupation is mainly agriculture II. Disguised unemployment III. Poor quality of human capital IV. High per capita intake ofproteins Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:I, II & III

Developing economy signs → occupation mainly agriculture, disguised unemployment, poor quality of human capital; high per capita protein intake is not one. Must know

Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

  • The Indian Economy is characterised by:I, III & IV only

Indian economy → predominance of agriculture, low per capita income, massive unemployment; predominance of industry marks a developed economy, not India.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Indian Economy is characterized as:Developing Economy

Indian economy → developing economy; at present a middle income developing market economy.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Which of the following is not a characteristics of Indian Economy?Lack of Natural Resources

Not a feature of Indian economy → lack of natural resources; low labour productivity, low per capita income, low capital formation are features.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Which of the following is not an economic activity?Voluntary Social Service

Voluntary social service → not an economic activity; farming, transportation and services are (input of resources → production → output).

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Which of the following is a non-economic element in growth of the country?Social Behaviour

Social behaviour → non-economic factor of growth; natural, energy and capital resources are economic factors.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Which of the following is not part of the 'Second Generation of Economic Reforms' identified by the Government?Legal System Reforms

Second Generation Economic Reforms → oil sector, public sector, government and public institutions reforms; legal (judicial) system reform is not included.

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

  • Indian model of development ensures interest of–State and Person both

Indian model of development (mixed economy) → protects interests of both State (public sector) and Person (private sector).

Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    National Income & Gross Domestic Product + National Income & Gross Domestic Product

    86 facts · 91 questions · 14 Must know

    Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
    • The term National Income represents:Gross National Product at market prices minus depreciation and indirect taxes plus subsidies

    National Income = NNP at factor cost = GNP at market prices – depreciation – indirect taxes + subsidies; NNP at market price = GNP – depreciation. Must know

    Memory aid Market price → factor cost: subtract indirect taxes, add subsidies.

    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

    • Which of the following statement is correct?Both (a) and (b) are correct

    NNP = GNP – Depreciation; GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad; so NNP = GDP + NFIA – Depreciation (both correct).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The National income of a country for a given period is equal to the:money value of final goods and services produced

    National income → money value of all final goods and services produced by normal residents of a country in a period (generally one year).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In an openeconomy, the national income (Y)of the economy is: (C, I, G, X, M stand for Consumption, Investment, Govt. Expenditure, total exports and total imports respectively)Y = C + I + G + (X – M)

    Open economy national income → Y = C + I + G + (X – M); X – M = net exports.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following is not a method to calculate the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?Diminishing cost method

    GDP methods → Product, Income, Expenditure; 'diminishing cost method' is not one.

    Memory aid PIE: Product, Income, Expenditure.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Net National Product (NNP) and Gross National Product (GNP) are -—

    NNP and GNP → both measure the money value of national production, and the two are different.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Nominal (GDP) is:GDP evaluated at current market prices

    Nominal GDP → GDP at current market prices, without inflation adjustment; used to find the GDP deflator and real GDP.

    Don't confuse With real GDP, which is valued at constant prices.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • One of the problems in calculating National Income in India is:non-organized sector

    Main problem in calculating India's national income → non-organized sector (no proper records); also unreliable data and double counting.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Read the following statements and choose the correct option: Statement I: Net Domestic Product = Gross Domestic Product + Depreciation. Statement II: Per Capita Income = Net Domestic Product/ Total Population of the Nation. Statement III: Net Domestic Product is the better metrics than Gross Domestic Product for comparing the economies of the world.None of the above options is true

    NDP = GDP – Depreciation (not plus); none of the three statements (NDP formula, per capita income = NDP/population, NDP better for comparison) is true.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is:PDI = Personal income – Personal tax payments

    Personal Disposable Income (PDI) = Personal income – Personal tax payments (direct taxes); it is spent or saved.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • If over a given period of time both prices and monetary income have been doubled, the real income will be –Unchanged

    Prices and money income both doubled → real income unchanged.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Theoretically, ifeconomic growth is conceptualized, which one of the following is not usually taken into consideration?Growth in financial aid from World Bank

    Economic growth measured by growth in GDP, GNP and per capita GNP; growth in World Bank financial aid is not considered.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Consider the following statements about Amartya Sen’s advices regarding priorities for Indian Economy:2, 3 and 4 are correct

    Amartya Sen's priorities for India → people-oriented (not commodity-oriented), economic security to poorest of the poor, safeguards against integration with world economy.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The view that ‘Planning in India should, in future, pay more attention to the people than to commodities’ was given by:Amartya Sen

    'Planning should pay more attention to people than to commodities' → Amartya Sen (Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, 1998).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The Hindu rate of growth refers to the growth rate of:National Income

    Hindu rate of growth → slow growth of National Income/GDP (about 3.5%, 1950s–1980s); term first used by Prof. Raj Krishna, 1981. Must know

    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

    • Economic growth is usually coupled with:Inflation

    Economic growth → usually coupled with inflation (rising income raises demand for goods).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The proportion of labour in GNP (Gross National Product) becomes low due to the following reason:Wages lag behind prices

    Labour's share in GNP becomes low when wages lag behind prices.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.4 1 2 3

    Economic development → constructive change; economic growth → GDP; sustainable development → environment; quality of life → health.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • With reference to Indian economy, consider the following statements:2 only

    Last decade: public sector's share in GDP declined (private sector's rose) → true; GDP increased four times in 10 years → false.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:1 2 3 4

    Boom → high business activity, rising income, output, employment; recession → gradual fall, business in low gear; depression → unprecedented unemployment, drastic fall; then recovery.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In the context of Indian economy, consider the following pairs:1 only

    Meltdown → steep fall in stock prices (only correct pair); recession → massive contraction of economic activity; slowdown → decrease in economic activity.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Given below are two statements:Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A.

    New Economic Policy 1991 (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) is criticised by insiders and outsiders, largely on ideological grounds → A and R true, R explains A. Must know

    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

    • Economic liberalization in India started with:substantial changes in industrial licensing policy

    Liberalisation began with changes in industrial licensing → New Industrial Policy, 24 July 1991 (Narsimha Rao govt); all except 18 industries freed from licence.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which one of the following is correct regarding stabilization and structural adjustment as two components of the new economic policy adopted in India?Structural adjustment is a gradual multi-step process, while stabilization is a quick adaptation process.

    NEP: stabilisation → quick, demand-side (inflation, fiscal, balance of payments); structural adjustment → gradual multi-step, supply-side (trade, capital flow, industrial reforms).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Who is called the pioneer of liberalization of Indian Economy?Dr. Manmohan Singh

    Pioneer of liberalisation of Indian economy → Dr. Manmohan Singh, Finance Minister in 1991.

    Don't confuse Don't pick P.V. Narsimha Rao; the 'pioneer' title goes to Finance Minister Manmohan Singh.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • One of the reasons for India's occupational structure remaining more or less the same over the years has been that:investment pattern has been directed towards capital intensive industries

    India's occupational structure stayed nearly the same → investment pattern directed towards capital-intensive industries.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following activities constitute real sector in the economy?1 and 2 only

    Real sector (production and flow of goods) → farmers harvesting crops, textile mills making fabric; bank lending and overseas rupee bonds → financial sector.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which among the following is NOT a major factor of economic growth?Technocrats and Bureaucrats

    Major growth factors → natural resources, physical capital, population/labour, human capital, technology, law; technocrats and bureaucrats are not.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which one of the following is a sign of economic growth?A sustained increase in real Per Capita Income.

    Sign of economic growth and best index of development → sustained increase in real per capita income (year to year).

    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

    • The most appropriate measure of a country’s economic growth is its –Per Capita Product (PCP)

    Most appropriate measure of economic growth and of standard of living → per capita real income (Per Capita Product / per capita NNP). Must know

    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

    • Increase in absolute and per capita real GNP do not connote a higher level of economic development, if:poverty and unemployment increase

    Higher absolute and per capita real GNP is not higher development if poverty and unemployment increase; development = growth + better living standards.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The growth rate of Per Capita Income at current prices is higher than that of Per Capita Income at constant prices, because the latter takes into account the rate of:increase in price level

    Per capita income grows faster at current prices than at constant prices → constant prices remove the increase in price level (inflation).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • That the Per Capita Income in India was Rs. 20 in 1867-68, was ascertained for the first time by:Dadabhai Naoroji

    First estimate of India's national income → Dadabhai Naoroji, 1867-68; per capita income Rs. 20. Must know

    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

    • Who was the chairman of National Income Committee appointed by the Government of India in 1949?P.C. Mahalanobis

    National Income Committee, 1949 → chairman P.C. Mahalanobis; members D.R. Gadgil and V.K.R.V. Rao.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The economist who for the first time scientifically determined National Income in India:V.K.R.V.Rao

    First scientific estimate of national income → Dr. V.K.R.V. Rao (1931-32); first attempt → Dadabhai Naoroji (1867-68).

    Don't confuse The first attempt (Naoroji) with the first scientific estimate (V.K.R.V. Rao).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following offices or institutes releases data of the National Income in India?None of the above / More than one of the above

    National Income data → earlier CSO (set up 1951); now National Statistical Office (NSO), formed by merging CSO and NSSO. Must know

    Full question and explanation · 10 paper(s)

    • In India which agency is entrusted with the collection of data of capital formation?RBI and Central Statistical Organisation

    Capital formation data → RBI and Central Statistical Organisation (now NSO); roles set by K.N. Raj Committee (1981) on saving and investment estimates.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • 'Base year' in National Income accounting means:The year whose prices are being used to calculate the real GDP

    Base year → the year whose prices are used to calculate real GDP (constant prices); present base year 2011-12.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Indicate the vital change in the measurement of National Income of India recently:Both the base year and calculation method have changed.

    2015: CSO changed both base year (2004-05 → 2011-12) and method (GVA at basic prices replaced GDP at factor cost). Must know

    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

    • In India for estimation of GDP at constant prices, at present the base year is:—

    GDP base year at constant prices → 1999-2000 when this was asked; now 2011-12.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following is the correct base year for measuring National Income in India?—

    National income base year → 2004-05 when this was asked; now 2011-12.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The new GDP series released by the CSO in February, 1999 is with reference to base prices of:1993-94

    CSO's new GDP series, February 1999 → base prices of 1993-94 (present base year 2011-12). Must know

    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

    • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:(A) is true, but (R) is false

    Economic development needs a multi-dimensional approach (A true); government focuses on both micro and macro issues, not mainly micro (R false).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • As per data released by Government of India in March 2011, the Per Capita Income of Indians rose by 14.5% in 2009-10. What is the Per Capita Income figure (in nearest hundred)?Rs. 46,500

    Per capita income 2009-10 (rose 14.5%) → about Rs. 46,500 (Economic Survey: Rs. 46249 at current prices).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In year 2013-14 in India, Per Capita Net National Income at current prices and factor cost was -None of these

    Per capita NNI 2013-14 (current prices, factor cost) → Rs. 79118 (new series), so none of the options.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In which year the rate of growth of India's Per Capita Income at constant prices was the highest during the period 1951-52 to 2015-16?2007-08

    Highest per capita income growth at constant prices (2004-05 series), 1951-52 to 2015-16 → 2007-08 (8.6%).

    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

    • In the year 2010-11 (at 2004-05 prices), which of the following is the Per Capita Income in India?Rs. 35,993

    Per capita income 2010-11 at 2004-05 prices (Quick Estimates) → Rs. 35,993.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In the year, 1991-92, the Per Capita Annual Income in India was about:7,500

    Per capita annual income 1991-92 → about Rs. 7,500 (nearest option; Economic Survey 2022-23 gives Rs. 6835 at current prices).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In the gone by decade of90s the highest rate of growth of GDP was obtained in which of the following year:1999-2000

    Highest GDP growth in the 1990s → 1999-2000 (GNI growth 8.8%, 2011-12 series); 1996-97 had 7.7%. Must know

    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

    • Indian Economy has witnessed highest growth rate in the year:2006-07

    Highest growth rate among the options → 2006-07 (as per 2011-12 series, Economic Survey 2022-23). Must know

    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

    • In the context of Indian Economy, consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

    Five years to 2010-11: GDP and per capita income growth did not rise steadily (2008-09 dip: GNI 2.9%, PCI 0.8%) → neither statement correct.

    Economic Survey 2020-21 (IMF estimate) → India's real GDP growth 11.5% in 2021-22 (financial year 2022) and 6.8% in 2022-23.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The annual growth rate of the Indian Economy at 1999- 2000 prices during 2005-2006 has been estimated between:8 to 9 percent

    GDP growth 2005-06 at 1999-2000 prices → 8.4% (CSO revised estimate, 31 May 2006) = 8 to 9 per cent; later revised to 9.5%. Must know

    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

    • The expected GDP growth rate for 1998-99 is:6.5%

    GDP growth 1998-99 → 6.5% (base year 1993-94); revised to 6.7% (base year 2004-05). Must know

    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

    • In India Gross Domestic Product growth rate increased from 4.5 percent in 2012-13 to 4.7 percent in 2013-14, because of–High growth rate in agriculture & allied sector

    GDP growth up from 4.5% (2012-13) to 4.7% (2013-14) → high agriculture & allied growth (4.7% vs 1.4%) due to a favourable monsoon.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following sub-sectors has experienced negative growth rate in 2009-10 over 2008-09?—

    Economic Survey 2009-10 showed agriculture & allied with negative growth in 2009-10 over 2008-09; revised data show positive growth in every sub-sector.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • As per recent estimates of the Reserve Bank of India growth rate in 2002-2003 will be –5-5.5%

    RBI's contemporary estimate of growth for 2002-03 → about 5-5.5%.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • According to Asian Development Report 2004, growth rate of India in 2005 will be –6.9%

    Asian Development Report 2004 (released 28 April 2004) → India's growth for 2005 estimated at 6.9%.

    • Assertion (A): The Indian Economy has experienced recession in the fiscal year 1997-98.Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of(A)

    Per capita NSDP (descending): question period → Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka (option d); 2021-22 → Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra.

    Don't confuse Haryana is a very close second now and was first earlier; the book's current answer is Karnataka.

    Highest GSDP growth in 2010-11 among options → Bihar; in 2021-22 Chhattisgarh (11.71%) led these, Manipur (13.51%) highest overall.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Assertion (A): Economic growth in India has generally remained stagnant for the last ten years.—

    1990s: effective growth till 1996-97 (not stagnant); foodgrains rose 176.4 → 212.9 million tonnes (1990-91 to 2001-02) → both A and R false.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R).(A) is false, but (R) is true

    Book answer: A false (per capita income has improved along with national income since 1947); R true (sizeable population still below poverty line).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In India, rural incomes are generally lower than the urban incomes. Which of the following reasons account for this?1,2 and 3

    Rural incomes lower than urban → farmers lack scientific-agriculture knowledge, primary products priced below manufactured goods, low investment in agriculture (all three).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • With reference to the 'Capital formation' which of the statements is/are correct?Both 1 and 2

    Capital formation → depends on savings and effective financial institutions; investment is its essential factor (both true).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • The main reason for low growth rate in India, inspite of high rate of savings and capital formation is:high capital-output ratio

    Low growth despite high savings and capital formation → high capital-output ratio (capital needed for one unit of output).

    Memory aid High COR = more capital for the same output = slower growth.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Despite being a high saving economy, capital formation may not result in significant increase in output due to:high capital-output ratio

    High saving economy but output rises little → high capital-output ratio; lower COR means higher productivity of capital and faster growth.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following are the main causes of slow rate of growth of Per Capita Income in India –1 and 2

    Slow growth of per capita income in India → high capital-output ratio and high population growth (not capital formation or fiscal deficits).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Consider the following statements about the reasons behind the low level of Per Capita Income in Uttar Pradesh:1, 2 and 3

    Low per capita income in Uttar Pradesh → fast-growing population, lack of entrepreneurship, inadequate infrastructure; modernization of agriculture is not a cause.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Economic growth in country X will necessarily have to occur if –there is capital formation in X

    Economic growth must occur with capital formation (saving part of income and investing it) → the most important factor of growth.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which factor can be highly supportive in achieving economic growth rate of 8% or more in the near future in India?Implementation of all stalled productive projects.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which of the following reasons are mainly responsible for slow growth of Real Per Capita Income in India -1, 2 and 3 only

    Slow growth of real per capita income → rapid population growth, high price rise, slow agricultural and industrial growth; foreign exchange is now sufficient.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In the 2001-2010 decade, the highest rate of gross domestic savings was achieved in the year –2007-08

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • In year 2012-13, India's gross domestic savings rate was-None of these

    Gross domestic savings rate 2012-13 → 33.9% of GDP, so none of the options.

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    Savings ratio 2006-07 → above 32% of GDP (34.9% at current market prices).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    • Which has the highest share in the household savings of India?Physical assets

    Highest share in household savings → physical assets (more than deposits, currency, shares and debentures).

    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

    Share in savings (descending) → household sector > private corporate sector > public corporations/enterprises > government.

          Limits to Growth (Meadows, 1972) → limits reached in the next 100 years if trends continue unchanged; in 2004 Meadows cut it to 30 years.

          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

          • The Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) shows the relationship between per capita GDP and environmental loss. What is the shape of Environmental Kuznets Curve?Inverted ‘U’ shaped

          Environmental Kuznets Curve → inverted 'U': environment worsens with early growth, then improves after a certain level of per capita GDP.

          • When did the term 'Sustainable Development' come into existence?1980

          • Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and other as the Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A)

          • ‘Saving energy and other resources for the future without sacrificing people’s comfort in the present’ is the definition of which of the following concepts?Sustainable development

          Base of sustainable development → environmental approach (outlook).

                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                      • India’s main agricultural import item is:Edible oil

                      India's main agricultural import → edible oil (more than 50% of value of agri-imports).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Consider the following statements:1 only

                      Edible oil imports exceed domestic production (2020-21: 133.52 vs 122.89 lakh tonnes) → true; customs duty on edible oils is reviewed and recently reduced, not nil → false.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Niger crops is a oil seed crop. What is the content of oil in its seeds?37 – 47%

                      Niger (minor rainfed oilseed) → seeds contain about 37-47% oil.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • The leading mulberry silk producing Indian State is:Karnataka

                      Leading mulberry silk producer (2022-23) → Karnataka; then Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Consider the following statements:1 only

                      India → only country producing all five commercial silks (Mulberry, Tropical Tasar, Oak Tasar, Eri, Muga); China largest silk producer, India second. Sugar 2022-23: Brazil first, India second.

                      Don't confuse India was the largest sugar producer in 2021-22, but in 2022-23 (USDA) Brazil is first.

                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                      • Which one of the following is the pathway to increase productivity in agriculture?None of the above/More than one of the above

                      Raising farm productivity → efficient irrigation, quality seeds, pesticides and fertilizers (all; 'more than one of the above').

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the following is not the reason for low productivity in Indian agriculture?Co-operative farming

                      Low farm productivity causes → population pressure, small holdings, disguised unemployment, uncertain monsoon; co-operative farming is not (it raises productivity). Must know

                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                      • The importance of agriculture in Indian economy is indicated by its contribution to which of the following?All of the above

                      Agriculture's importance → national income, employment, industry, international trade, foodgrain supply (all); 17.6% of GVA, employs about half the workforce.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the following pairs about India's economic indicator and agricultural production (all in rounded figures) are correctly matched?1 and 3 only

                      2006-07: per capita GDP about Rs. 37,000 and wheat 75.8 MT (correct pairs); rice was 93.4 MT, not 180 MT.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Agriculture income tax in India can be levied by:State Governments

                      Agricultural income tax → only State Governments (item 46, State List, Seventh Schedule); exempt from Union income tax.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • What percentage of labour force is provided direct employment by the agriculture sector in India?—

                      Workforce in agriculture → 58.2% (Census 2001); about 55% (Census 2011).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • In Uttar Pradesh maximum percentage of workers are engaged in:Agriculture sector

                      Uttar Pradesh → most workers (59.3%) engaged in agriculture sector (Census 2011).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • What approximate percentage of India's labour force at present depends on agriculture for their livelihood?—

                      Labour force dependent on agriculture → about 65% at question time; about 55% as per Census 2011.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the followings is not a cash crop?Jowar

                      Not a cash crop → Jowar (a coarse foodgrain); jute, groundnut, sugarcane are cash crops.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • The main objective of Vishesh Krishi and Gram Udyog Yojna is:Promotion of agricultural export

                      Vishesh Krishi and Gram Udyog Yojana (VKGUY) → promote agricultural exports by offsetting high transport costs to port/airport.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Kissan Bahi Yojana was started in Uttar Pradesh in:1992

                      Kisan Bahi Yojana in Uttar Pradesh → started 1992.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Consider following statements about Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana and state which one of them is incorrect?Additional Central Assistance under the scheme would be available as 80% grant to the States

                      Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana → launched August 2007; Rs. 25000 crore for 11th Plan; given as 100% central assistance (ACA), not 80% grant. Must know

                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                      • Which is not included in 'National Agricultural Development Yojna'?None of these

                      RKVY (2007 umbrella scheme) includes soil test labs, fertilizer quality control labs, farm tools test labs, agricultural engineering → none excluded.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • P. Sengupta and G. Sdasyuk (1968) had divided India into how many micro agricultural regions?60

                      Sengupta and Sdasyuk (1968) → 4 macro (climate), 11 meso (physiography), 60 micro agricultural regions (crop combinations).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • For the 8th Plan, India was divided into how many agro-climatic zones by the Planning Commission?15

                      Planning Commission (1988, for 8th Plan) → India divided into 15 agro-climatic zones.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • National Horticulture Mission was launched in which of the following Five Year Plans?Tenth Five Year Plan

                      National Horticulture Mission → started May 2005, in the 10th Five Year Plan; now a sub-scheme of MIDH (launched 2014-15). Must know

                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                      • Which of the following States is covered under the National Horticulture Mission (NHM)?Uttar Pradesh

                      NHM covers Uttar Pradesh; North Eastern and Himalayan States (J&K, Arunachal, Himachal) are under a separate mission, HMNEH.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which one of the followings is not the objectives of 'National Horticulture Mission'?Providing financial assistance

                      NHM objectives → higher horticulture growth, post-harvest management, human resource development; 'providing financial assistance' is not one.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Krishi Shramik Samajik Suraksha Yojna provides –Benefits of pension and insurance

                      Krishi Shramik Samajik Suraksha Yojana (1 July 2001) → life insurance, survival benefit and pension for agricultural workers.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • 'Small Farmers Development Programme' was started in the year:—

                      Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA) programme → started 1971 for small, marginal farmers and agricultural labourers.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the followings is not true for National Food Security Act?It has only two schedules which prescribes for issue of price and nutritional standards of food

                      NFSA → 67% of population (75% rural, 50% urban); has four schedules, not two (I subsidised prices, II nutritional standards, III advancing food security).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • With reference to the National Food Security Act, which of the following statements is/are correct? I. It will cover upto 75 percent rural and 50 percent urban population. II. Special focus on nutritional support to women and children. III. Eldest woman of above 18 years age will be head of household. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:I, II and III are correct

                      NFSA 2013 → up to 75% rural, 50% urban; nutritional support to women and children; eldest woman (18+) is household head (all correct).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • With reference to the provisions made under the National Food Security Act, 2013, consider the following statements:2 only

                      NFSA 2013 → not BPL-only (SECC method, non-BPL also benefit); eldest woman aged 18 or above is household head for ration card (only 2 true).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Under which law, the State Food Commission is established?National Food Security Act, 2013

                      State Food Commission → Section 16, National Food Security Act, 2013; Chairperson, five other Members and a Member-Secretary.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • The Food Preservation Commission is a statutory body established under which of the following Acts?National Food Security Act, 2013

                      Commission for food under NFSA 2013 → the Act names it 'State Food Commission' (asked as 'Food Preservation Commission').

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the following States started E-ration Card Service in first time?Delhi

                      First to launch E-ration Card Service → Delhi (March 2015).

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Consider the following statements:1 only

                      FSS Act 2006 replaced Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954; FSSAI has an independent Chairperson (Secretary rank) under Health Ministry's administrative control, not under DG Health Services.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the followings is not an objective of National Food Security Mission (NFSM)?Strengthening credit facilities

                      NFSM (October 2007) → raise rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals output, restore soil fertility, boost farm economy; strengthening credit facilities is not an objective.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Which of the following crops is not covered under the National Food Security Mission?—

                      NFSM → October 2007 (from Rabi 2007-08); target rice +10, wheat +8, pulses +2 million tons by 2011-12; coarse cereals not covered then. Must know

                      Full question and explanation · 9 paper(s)

                      • The reason for increase in price of foodgrains distributed through public distribution system is to:Lesson the burden of subsidy involved in scheme

                      PDS foodgrain prices raised → to lessen the subsidy burden of the scheme.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Operation Flood is related to which of the following –Milk production

                      Operation Flood (1970, NDDB) → milk production / White Revolution; Dr. Verghese Kurien → father of White Revolution. Must know

                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                      • As per Economic Survey 2020-21, arrange the following States in decreasing order of milk production:Madhya Pradesh > Gujarat > Punjab > Haryana

                      Milk production 2019-20 (Economic Survey 2020-21) → UP, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra, Punjab, Maharashtra, Haryana; so MP > Gujarat > Punjab > Haryana.

                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                      • Consider the following statements with reference to 'Nandini Krishak Samriddhi Yojana':Only 1

                      Nandini Krishak Samriddhi Yojana (UP, Nand Baba Mission) → only Sahiwal, Gir, Tharparkar, Gangatiri cows (true); 'one year experience' claim false.

                      Wrong pair → Sheep – Tharparkar (Tharparkar is a cow breed, Gujarat and Rajasthan); Bhadawari → buffalo; Sindhi → cow; Jamunapari → goat.

                            Hunger persists despite three-fold rise in foodgrains (1950-1990) → Green Revolution limited to small pockets, food costly versus earnings of poor, wheat/paddy favoured over coarse grains.

                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                            • The Second Green Revolution proposed by the Prime Minister does not include:encourage foreign direct investment in agriculture

                            • Which one of the following agriculture practices is eco-friendly?Organic farming

                            • With reference to 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana', consider the following statements:2 only

                            Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana → boost export of fruits, vegetables, flowers, minor forest produce, dairy, poultry; exporters get duty credit scrip (5 percent of FOB). Must know

                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                  • Consider the following statements:All three

                                  Niger (ramtil, Guizotia abyssinica) → Kharif crop with MSP (one of 14 kharif MSP crops); some tribal people cook with its oil (all three true).

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Since 1997-98, which statement is correct regarding Minimum Support Price (MSP)?MSP > C2 costs

                                  Since 1997-98 → MSP > C2 cost (C2 = actual paid costs + imputed family labour + interest on owned capital + rental value of owned land).

                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                  • Who determines the minimum support price in India?The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices

                                  MSP recommended by Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP): set up January 1965 as Agricultural Prices Commission, renamed CACP in 1985. Must know

                                  Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                  • Which of the followings are the objectives of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)?1, 2 and 3

                                  CACP objectives → stabilise farm prices, meaningful real income for farmers, protect consumers through PDS at reasonable rates; not 'maximum price for farmers'.

                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                  • Consider the following statements regarding the Minimum Support Price: I. If the market price is high, then farmers will sell their produce to the government. II. This ensures minimum fixed prices for the farmers' yields. III. It is helpful in Food Security Mission. IV. It is highly profitable for the farmers as they earn immense profit on their yields. Among these –II and III are correct

                                  MSP → ensures minimum fixed price for farmers and helps food security; farmers sell to government only when market price is below MSP; not for profit.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • The Minimum Support Price fixed by the Government for the purchase of wheat in 2013 is:Rs. 1350/quintal

                                  Wheat MSP when asked (2013) → Rs. 1350/quintal; RMS 2024-25 → Rs. 2275 (Rs. 150 above 2023-24's Rs. 2125).

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • From 4th July, 2018 the Minimum Support Price (MSP) during 2018-19 for paddy per quintal is:Rs. 1,750

                                  Paddy (common) MSP 2018-19 → Rs. 1,750/quintal (Grade A Rs. 1770); 2024-25 → Rs. 2300 (up Rs. 117).

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which State of India has recently decided tofix a Minimum Support Price (MSP) for fruits and vegetables?Kerala

                                  First State with MSP for fruits and vegetables → Kerala (decided October 2020, effective November 1, 2020; 16 commodities).

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Minimum Support Price for groundnut announced by the Government of India for 1995-96 is –900 Rs/quintal

                                  Groundnut MSP 1995-96 → Rs. 900/quintal; 2024-25 → Rs. 6783 per quintal.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • The price at which the Government purchases foodgrains, is:Procurement Price

                                  Government buys foodgrains (for PDS and buffer stock) at Procurement Price, generally higher than MSP. Must know

                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                  • Which one among the followings is not a cash crop?Soyabean

                                  Not a cash crop among options → Soyabean; tobacco, cotton and rubber are cash crops.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • In the Union Budget 2011-2012, the effective rate of interest for farmers on timely repayment of bank loan is:4 percent

                                  Union Budget 2011-12 → prompt-repayment subvention raised from 2% to 3%, so farm loans (up to Rs. 3 lakh at 7%) effectively cost 4%.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which of the followings is not included in running cost capital of a farm?Land revenue

                                  Running cost capital of a farm → seeds, fertilizer, irrigation water (inputs); land revenue is not included.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which One of the followings does not contribute to the rural economy?Practice of lending personal money

                                  Limited contribution to rural economy → practice of lending personal money; pastoralism, cottage industry and good tools contribute.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which of the following is the main principle of agriculture finance?All of the above

                                  Principles of agricultural finance → purpose, person and productivity planning (all of the above).

                                  Memory aid Three Ps: Purpose, Person, Productivity planning.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which is not a source of agricultural finance in India?None of these

                                  Institutional farm credit → cooperative societies/banks, commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks, government; non-institutional → moneylenders, relatives. All options are sources → 'none of these'.

                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                  • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                  Agri credit share 2022-23: Commercial Banks 76.86%, RRBs 12.34%, all cooperatives only 10.80%, so DCCBs don't lead; DCCBs fund and guide Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS).

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Long-term agricultural credit is provided by:Land Development Bank

                                  Long-term agricultural credit → Land Development Banks (earlier called Land Mortgage Banks).

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which one of the followings is the largest source of agricultural credit in India in recent years?Commercial Banks

                                  Largest source of farm credit → Commercial Banks (about three-fourth; 53.7% in 1999-2000 → 76.86% in 2022-23); co-operatives fell from 39.5% to 10.80%. Must know

                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                  • Which among the followings is providing least institutional credit to agriculture and allied activities in recent years?Foreign Private Banks

                                  Least institutional credit to agriculture → Foreign Private Banks (negligible); main sources are Commercial, Cooperative and Regional Rural Banks.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • To improve institutional agricultural credit flow, what credit target for 2020-21 has been fixed in the Union Budget of India?Rs. 15 lakh crore

                                  Agricultural credit target: 2020-21 → Rs. 15 lakh crore; 2021-22 → 16.5; 2022-23 → 18; 2023-24 → 20 lakh crore.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Under the Kisan Credit Card scheme, short-term credit support is given to farmers for which of the following purposes?1, 3 and 4 only

                                  Kisan Credit Card (1998; NABARD model, R.V. Gupta Committee) → short-term credit for farm-asset working capital, household consumption, post-harvest expenses; not tractors, houses, cold storage. Must know

                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                  • Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order:4, 1, 2, 3

                                  Chronology → Regional Rural Banks (1975), NABARD (1982), SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (1992-93), Kisan Credit Card (1998). Must know

                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                  • The New Package for Agriculture announced by the UPA Government does not provide:Concession in loan payment

                                  UPA's New Package for Agriculture → bank loans to landless farmers, NABARD proposal for them, credit to 50 lakh new farmers; no loan waiver or repayment concession.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Government of India has taken a decision to set up a Price Stabilisation Fund for the growers of:Potato and Onion

                                  Price Stabilisation Fund Scheme (1 April 2003 – 30 September 2013) → small coffee, tea, rubber, tobacco growers (up to four hectares); book answer: potato and onion.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • Which of the following crop is covered for price control under the price stabilization fund of the Government of India?Potato

                                  Price Stabilization Fund (2014-15) → curbs price volatility of onions and potatoes (pulses added later) through a strategic buffer; discourages hoarding.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                  • With reference to the management of minor minerals in India, consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                  Sand → 'minor mineral' under MMDR Act, 1957 (true); States grant minor mineral leases and also frame their rules, not the Centre → 1 and 3 correct.

                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        54 facts · 64 questions · 8 Must know

                                        Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                        • Which was the first Indian Private Sector Company to find place in Global 500 list of ‘Fortune Magazine’?Reliance Industries Ltd.

                                        First Indian private company in Fortune Global 500 → Reliance Industries (284th, list of 24 July 2006); 2023: Reliance 88th, Indian Oil 94th, LIC 107th.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • According to Fortune India List of 500 Companies/ Corporations, the biggest Company/Corporation in 2019 was:Reliance Industries Ltd.

                                        Biggest company in Fortune India 500 list (2019 to 2023) → Reliance Industries; 2023: Indian Oil 2nd, LIC 3rd. Must know

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements:2 and 3 only

                                        PNGRB (2006) → not India's first regulator (Forward Market Commission 1952, SEBI, IRDA earlier); ensures competitive gas markets; appeals go to Appellate Tribunal for Electricity.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With reference to the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), which of the statements is/are correct?Neither 1 nor 2

                                        CSR made mandatory from April 1, 2014 (India first in world) by Section 135, Companies Act 2013 → two percent of average net profit of past three years. Must know

                                        Don't confuse Both statements wrong: the Act is of 2013 (not 2014) and the spend is two percent (not one).

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • Which of the following statements is incorrect about Uday Kotak Committee?It recommends that the post of chairman and managing director must remain the same.

                                        Uday Kotak Committee (SEBI, June 2017) → corporate governance: at least half board independent, minimum 6 members, one woman independent director; chairman and MD posts not same.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which of the following statement/s is/are correct with reference to Indian Railways?Both 1 and 2

                                        Indian Railways targets → 100% electrification by 2023 (about 95% broad gauge done by FY 2023-24) and 'net zero' carbon emission network by 2030 (both correct).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Where in India, the first rubber based tyre Metro is being built?Nashik

                                        India's first rubber-tyred Metro → Nashik, Maharashtra (cleared by State Cabinet, August 2019); rubber tyres run on concrete or steel rollways.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • The first showroom in India of the retail furniture giant 'Ikea' was opened in which city in 2018?Hyderabad

                                        IKEA's first showroom in India → Hyderabad, 9 August 2018 (13 acres, about 7500 products).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • In which district of Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Centre Banmore is situated?Morena

                                        Industrial Development Centre Banmore → Morena district, Madhya Pradesh.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which two cities of Madhya Pradesh included in 'town of export excellence'?Dewas-Indore

                                        Madhya Pradesh 'towns of export excellence' → Dewas (pharmaceuticals) and Indore (soya meal and soya products).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Who was the chairman of the committee on revisiting and revitalizing the PPPmodel of Infrastructure development?V. Kelkar

                                        Committee on revisiting and revitalising PPP model of infrastructure → Dr. Vijay Kelkar (announced in Budget 2015-16; report 19 November 2015).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which of the following infrastructure sectors of India is related with Bharatmala Project?Road infrastructure

                                        Bharatmala Project → road and highways infrastructure (economic corridors, inter corridors, feeder routes).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R):(A) is false but (R) is true

                                        National Infrastructure Pipeline → first made public in PM's 2019 Independence Day speech; aims at equitable infrastructure access (R true); '2020-30 period' is false (A false).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With reference to 'PM Gati Shakti Scheme', which of the following statement/s is/are correct?Only 2

                                        PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan → launched 13 October 2021 (not 2022); seven engines: roads, railways, airports, ports, mass transport, waterways, logistics; NIP aligned to it.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which one of the following industrial/economic corridors of India is being developed in collaboration with Japan?Delhi-Mumbai

                                        Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor → developed with Japan (MoU 2006); Japan also assists Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Among other things, which one of the following was the purpose for which the Deepak Parekh Committee was constituted?To suggest measures for financing the development of infrastructure

                                        Deepak Parekh Committee (Finance Ministry, December 26, 2006) → financing infrastructure development; report May 2007; headed infrastructure financing committee again July 2012.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • According to recent data released by Indian Cellular Association (ICA), India has acquired what position in the world in producing mobile phones?Second

                                        India → second largest mobile phone producer after China (ICA data, 2017); retained in 2023-24.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With reference to ‘National Investment and Infrastructure Fund’, which of the following statements is/are correct?Neither 1 nor 2

                                        National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (2015) → India's first infrastructure-specific fund; not a NITI Aayog organ; proposed corpus Rs. 40,000 crore, not Rs. 4,00,000 crore.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements about the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme:2 and 3

                                        PLI for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (notified 1 April 2020) → boosts mobile phone and specified component manufacturing (incl. ATMP units); 4% to 6% incentive on incremental sales.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • When was the National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) released by the Government of India?4 November, 2011

                                        National Manufacturing Policy → 4 November 2011; manufacturing to 25% of GDP within a decade, 100 million jobs, 12-14% sector growth. Must know

                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                        • What is/are the recent policy initiative(s) of Government of India to promote the growth of manufacturing sector?1, 2 and 3

                                        NMP initiatives for manufacturing → National Investment and Manufacturing Zones, single window clearance, Technology Acquisition and Development Fund (all three).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Recently, India’s first ‘National Investment and Manufacturing Zone’ was proposed to be set up in:Andhra Pradesh

                                        First National Investment and Manufacturing Zone proposed → Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh; NIMZs are tools of National Manufacturing Policy, 2011. Must know

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • The Government policy ‘Make in India’ aims at:None of the above/More than one of the above

                                        Make in India (25 September 2014) → facilitate investment, innovation, skills, IP protection, best manufacturing infrastructure; aims cover more than one option.

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • Logo of'Make in India' is:Lion

                                        Make in India logo → silhouette of a lion on the move; initiative launched September 2014. Must know

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • Which one of the following is not an initiative for industrial development?Digital India

                                        Not an industrial development initiative → Digital India (digitally empowered society, knowledge economy); Make in India, Ease of Doing Business, Start-up India are.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • The specific requirements of the ‘start-ups’ can be fulfilled through:All the above

                                        Start-up funding → bootstrapping, crowd funding, angel investors, venture capital, incubators, bank loans, MUDRA (all the above).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • "Initially the specific requirements of the Start-up can be fulfilled through the new age financing alternatives " has been suggested by:Pranab Mukherjee

                                        'New age financing can meet start-up needs' (angel investors, venture capital, crowd funding) → President Pranab Mukherjee, 17th March 2016.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which Indian State has launched the Student Startup and Innovation Policy (SSIP) 2.0 in January 2022?Gujarat

                                        Student Startup and Innovation Policy (SSIP) 2.0 → Gujarat, January 2022 (for 11 January 2022 to 31 March 2027).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With reference to 'Stand-Up India Scheme', which of the following statements is/are correct?Both 1 and 2

                                        Stand-Up India → promotes entrepreneurship among SC/ST and women; refinance through SIDBI; anchored by Department of Financial Services (both true).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • ‘Stand-up India’Scheme’s purpose is:To encourage entrepreneurship among the SC/STs and women entrepreneur

                                        Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) → bank loans of 10 lakh to 1 crore to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per branch for a greenfield enterprise. Must know

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • Pradhan Mantri Mudra Scheme is aimed at:bringing the small entrepreneurs into formal financial system

                                        PM MUDRA Yojana (April 8, 2015) → brings small entrepreneurs into formal finance; loans up to 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm micro enterprises.

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • How much loan amount will be granted by banks under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana for industry, business and services under Kishor Enterprise?More than Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5,00,000

                                        MUDRA loan types → Shishu up to Rs. 50,000; Kishor more than Rs. 50,000 up to Rs. 5,00,000.

                                        Memory aid Shishu (child) gets the smallest loan; Kishor (teen) the next size.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With reference to ‘Quality Council of India (QCI)’, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                        Quality Council of India (1997) → set up jointly by Government and Indian industry; chairman appointed by PM on industry's recommendation (both true); under DPIIT.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • What is the correct chronological sequence of the following enactments in India?4, 2, 1, 3

                                        Chronology → Minimum Wages Act (1948), Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (1951), MRTP Act (1969), FERA (1973).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements:Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A)

                                        Post-1991 reforms and dilution of MRTP Act provisions → mergers and acquisitions became common → A and R true, R explains A.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • In India, which one of the following compiles information on industrial disputes, closures, retrenchments and lay-offs in factories employing workers?Labour Bureau

                                        Data on industrial disputes, closures, retrenchments, lay-offs → Labour Bureau (established 1920).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • The Trade Disputes Act of1929 provided for:a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes

                                        Trade Disputes Act 1929 → Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation; banned strikes/lock-outs without notice in public utility services.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements: As per the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules, 2018Both 1 and 2

                                        Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules 2018 → fixed-term employment eases lay-offs; no termination notice for temporary workmen (both true).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                        Factories Act 1881 → better working conditions (no child labour under seven); did not fix wages or allow trade unions; N.M. Lokhande → pioneer of labour movement.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which of the following labour related Acts have been amalgamated into the 'Code on Wages, 2019'? I. Minimum Wages Act II. Payment of Bonus Act III. The Contract Labour Act IV. Equal RemunerationAct Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes:I, II and IV only

                                        Code on Wages 2019 replaced → Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Payment of Bonus Act 1965, Equal Remuneration Act 1976; not Contract Labour Act.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With reference to casual workers employed in India, consider the following statements:1, 2 and 3

                                        Casual workers → entitled to EPF (Supreme Court, Pawan Hans case, January 2020), regular hours and overtime; government can mandate wages only by bank account (all three).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • With effect from 1 April, 2017 the minimum wage for unskilled labour in Uttar Pradesh has been fixed at:Rs. 7400 per month

                                        UP minimum wage for unskilled labour from 1 April 2017 → Rs. 7400 per month; from 1 April 2024 → Rs. 10648.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • The share of industry in GDP of India in 2006-07 was:Between 25-30 percent

                                        Industry's share in GDP 2006-07 → 25-30%; was 16.6% in 1950-51; averaged 31 percent during 2011-12 to 2020-21.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • What was the industrial growth rate of India during 2013-14 with 2011-12 as the base year?3.5 percent

                                        Industrial growth 2013-14 (constant 2011-12 prices) → about 3.5%.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Assertion (A): There was an increase in industrial production during 1999-2000.Both (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of(A)

                                        1999-2000: industrial production rose, helped by stable exchange rate and better business sentiment after South-East Asian crisis → A, R true; R explains A.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which of the following activities has not been included in the Industrial Production Index of India?Construction

                                        IIP (by NSO, monthly) covers mining, manufacturing, electricity; construction is not included (nor gas and water supply). Must know

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • Which of the following agencies releases the Index of Industrial Production to measure industrial performance in India?None of the above / More than one of the above

                                        Index of Industrial Production → earlier released by CSO, now by National Statistical Office (NSO), monthly; base year 2011-12.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • The new series for the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), which was released by Government of India on 10th June 2011, has changed the base year from 1993-94 to:2004-05

                                        IIP base year 1993-94 → 2004-05 (10th June 2011) → 2011-12 (May 12, 2017); weights: manufacturing 77.63%, mining 14.37%, electricity 7.99%.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • In India, in the overall Index of Industrial Production, the Indices of Eight Core Industries have a combined weight of37.90%. Which of the following are among those Eight Core Industries?1, 2, 3 and 4

                                        Eight core industries → coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity (not textiles or chemicals); 40.27% of IIP weight (earlier 37.90%).

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                        • In the 'Index of Eight Core Industries', which one of the following is given the highest weight?Electricity generation

                                        Highest weight in Index of Eight Core Industries → electricity generation; eight core industries = 40.27 percent of IIP weight (base 2011-12).

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • During the year 2000-01, which one of the following industries recorded the highest growth rate in India?Steel

                                        Highest growth in 2000-01 among options → steel; in 2023-24 steel (12.3%) again led cement, coal and electricity.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                        Coal nationalised by Indira Gandhi government (Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973) (true); coal blocks now auctioned, not by lottery (Act of 2015); self-sufficiency claim false.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Which is not included in manufacturing sector?Construction Industry

                                        Manufacturing sector includes large, small scale, micro and medium industries; construction industry is not part of the manufacturing sector.

                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                        • Consider the following statements about Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)Act, 2020:1 and 3 only

                                        MSME revised definition: announced in Atmanirbhar Bharat Package 13th May 2020; notified 1st June 2020; effective 1st July 2020; one composite formula for manufacturing and service units. Must know

                                        Don't confuse Notification date (1st June 2020) with the date it came into effect (1st July 2020).

                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                              Hour 9 →
