                                              Industrial Sector · part 2 of 2

                                              48 facts · 54 questions · 6 Must know

                                              Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                              • In Industrial Policy of 1991, the investment amount for small scale industries approved for general and auxiliary units was:Rs. 60 lakh, Rs. 75 lakh

                                              1991 Policy: SSI limit Rs. 60 lakh (was 35), ancillary Rs. 75 lakh (was 45); MSMED Act 2006; micro now: investment ≤ Rs. 1 crore, turnover ≤ Rs. 5 crore. Must know

                                              Memory aid 60-75: small 60, ancillary 75 in 1991.

                                              Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                              • Investment in Plant and Machinery in a small scale manufacturing unit should be:Above Rs. 25 lakhs but not more than Rs. 5 crore

                                              MSMED Act 2006, old manufacturing limits (plant and machinery): micro up to Rs. 25 lakh; small Rs. 25 lakh to 5 crore; medium Rs. 5 to 10 crore. Must know

                                              Don't confuse These are the old 2006 limits; the revised definition uses a composite investment-plus-turnover formula.

                                              Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                              • Consider the following statements with reference to India:2 only

                                              Medium enterprise (w.e.f. 1st July 2020): investment up to Rs. 50 crore, turnover up to Rs. 250 crore (not Rs. 15-25 crore); all MSME bank loans are priority sector.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • As on March 31, 2011, which one of the following States had the largest number of registered factories?Tamil Nadu

                                              Most registered factories → Tamil Nadu (ASI 2021-22: 39667), then Gujarat, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Consider the following statements: Small-scale industries are, in most cases, not as efficient and competitive as the large-scale ones. Yet the Government provides preferential treatment and reservations in a range of products to the small firms because small-scale industries:1 and 2

                                              SSIs get preference and reservation because they give higher employment per unit of capital and promote regional dispersion of industries.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • For a developing country like India small scale and cottage industries should be encouraged primarily because they:Generate large employment opportunities

                                              Small scale and cottage industries are encouraged in India mainly because they generate large employment opportunities.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Small Scale and Cottage Industries are important, because:they provide more employment

                                              Small scale and cottage industries are important because they provide more employment.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The most important small scale industry in India is the:Handloom

                                              Most important small scale industry of India → Handloom (unorganised sector); fourth Handloom Census 2019-20: about 35.23 lakh workers.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The largest industry of Uttar Pradesh in terms of employment is:Handloom

                                              Largest industry of Uttar Pradesh by employment → Handloom (not cotton mills, leather or cement).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which ofthefollowing is aproblemofsmallscaleindustries?All of the above

                                              SSI problems: lack of capital, marketing experience and raw material; also old technology, power shortage, labour problems and industrial sickness.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which one of the following is not the problem of Small Scale Industries (SSIs)?Strikes and lockouts

                                              Strikes and lockouts are a problem of large scale industries, not SSIs; SSIs face finance (working capital), marketing and raw material problems.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Arrange the following Committees formed for small scale sector in a chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below: I. Nayak Committee II. Abid Hussain Committee III. S.S. Kohli Committee IV. Karve Committee Codes:—

                                              SSI committees in order: Karve 1955 → Nayak 1991 → Abid Hussain 1995 → S.S. Kohli 2000 (order IV, I, II, III).

                                              Memory aid K-N-A-K: Karve, Nayak, Abid, Kohli.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Nayak committee is related:to small industries

                                              Nayak Committee (RBI, 9 December 1991, P.R. Nayak) → finance problems of small scale industries; report September 1992.

                                              Don't confuse With P.J. Nayak Committee (RBI, January 2014) on governance of bank boards.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which one of the following committees recommended the abolition of reservation of items for the small scale sector in industry?Abid Hussian Committee

                                              Abid Hussain Committee (Expert Committee on Small Enterprises, 1995) → total abolition of reservation of items for small scale industries; report 1997. Must know

                                              Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                              • The contribution of India's small scale sector to the gross turnover in the manufacturing sector since 1992 has been of the order of:40%

                                              Small scale sector's share in manufacturing gross turnover (since 1992) → about 40%; MSME share in manufacturing GVA 40.83% in 2021-22.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which sector got high rate of growth in its cooperative units?Cotton textile

                                              Cotton textile → high growth in cooperative units (14.8% yearly growth, 1999-2000 to 2005-06).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • In India, maximum number of workers are employed in:Textile Industry

                                              Textile industry → largest employer after agriculture: about 45 million direct and 60 million indirect jobs.

                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                              • From which sector of the following, largest quantity of cotton textile is produced in the country?Powerloom

                                              Largest quantity of cotton textile in India is produced by the powerloom sector (not mill, handloom or hosiery).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The largest centre of textile industry in India at present is:Mumbai

                                              Largest textile centre in India (among Ahmedabad, Kanpur, Mumbai, Surat) → Mumbai.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which Indian State has the largest number of Cotton Textile Mills?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                              Most cotton textile mills → Tamil Nadu (then Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh); Tamil Nadu has almost half of India's cotton spinning capacity.

                                              Don't confuse Most mills = Tamil Nadu; most mill-made cotton cloth = Gujarat.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • In India, the highest production of mill-made cotton cloth comes from:Gujarat

                                              Highest mill-made cotton cloth production → Gujarat (2016-17), then Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. Must know

                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                              • The oldest large scale industry of India is:Cotton textiles

                                              Oldest large scale industry of India → cotton textiles; first cotton mill set up in 1818 at Fort Gloster near Kolkata.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The first industry to develop in India was the:Cottage industry

                                              First industry to develop in India → cottage industry (since ancient times; declined under British rule).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which one of the following industries is regarded as the most basic for our modern civilization?Iron and Steel

                                              Iron and steel → most basic industry of modern civilisation; backbone of the modern industrial economy.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The industry for which Nepanagar is known is:Newsprint paper

                                              Nepanagar (Burhanpur, Madhya Pradesh) → newsprint paper; Nepa Mills pioneered newsprint in India, production from April 1956. Must know

                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                              • Which of the following places are known for paper manufacturing industry?1, 2 and 4

                                              Paper industry centres: Yamunanagar (Haryana), Guwahati (Assam), Ballarpur (Maharashtra); Shahabad is not known for paper.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The Hazira Fertilizer Factory is based on:Natural Gas

                                              Hazira (Surat, Gujarat) KRIBHCO fertilizer complex → based on natural gas.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which statement is not correct about the fertilizer industry of India?—

                                              India not self-reliant in fertilizers: urea above 85%, phosphatic above 50% self-sufficient, potash fully imported; India is second in nitrogenous fertilizers; fertilizer is second industry after iron and steel.

                                              Don't confuse At question time only (c) was wrong; by present data (b) 'third largest in nitrogen' is also wrong (India is second).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Though a few (gas-based) industries have already been established, good reserves of natural gas in India remain unutilized. This vast resource of natural gas can be used in the production of:Fertilizer

                                              Unused natural gas → best used for fertilizers; natural gas is main feedstock for ammonia (Haber process).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The Oil and Natural Gas Commission (ONGC) was set up in:1956

                                              ONGC → set up 14 August 1956 as a Commission; statutory body October 1959; became Corporation in 1994.

                                              Don't confuse 1956 (set up) with 1959 (statutory body by Act).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • OIL is an enterprise involved in:Oil exploration

                                              Oil India Limited (OIL) → exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas (not import or marketing).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • With reference to the Public Sector Undertakings in India, consider the following statements:1 and 2

                                              MMTC → largest non-oil importer; PEC Ltd (STC subsidiary, 1971) → Ministry of Commerce & Industry; enforcing quality control is not an ECGC objective.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                              MMTC → India's largest international trading organisation and government trading company; Neelachal Ispat Nigam (1982, Kalinga Nagar, Odisha) promoted by MMTC with Odisha government (IPICOL). Must know

                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                              • With reference to the functions of Public Sector in India, which of the following statements is/are correct?I, II, III and IV are correct

                                              Public sector functions: provide public utilities, build social and economic overhead capital, ensure balanced regional and sectoral growth, pursue egalitarian goals.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Read the following statements carefully:1 and 3 are true

                                              Public sector in India has basic and heavy industries and secure jobs; not all its industries are profit-oriented.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Assertion (A): In recent times, the growth in the public sector employment has been very sluggish in India.Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A

                                              Public sector employment growth became sluggish because the NEP 1991 reassessed the State's role in development (A and R true; R explains A).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • In India the Public Sector is most dominant in:commercial banking

                                              Public sector is most dominant in commercial banking in India (among steel, term-lending institutions and transport).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which of the following is not a public sector undertaking/ enterprise?T.I.S.C.O.

                                              TISCO (Tata Steel, Jamshedpur, 1907) → private sector; NTPC, SAIL and BHEL → Maharatna CPSEs.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which is not a Public enterprise?Leather Factory, Gwalior

                                              Not a public enterprise → Leather Factory, Gwalior; BHEL Bhopal, Ordnance Factory Jabalpur and Alkaloid Factory Neemuch are public enterprises.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which one of the following is not of the same category:ESSAR OIL

                                              Odd one out → Essar Oil (private; now Nayara Energy); SAIL, BHEL and ONGC are public sector undertakings.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The Government holding in BPCL is:between 50% and 60%

                                              Government holding in BPCL → between 50% and 60% (present 52.98%; it was 66.2% in the question period).

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which of the following are the public sector undertakings of the Government of India?1 and 3 only

                                              Balmer Lawrie (Ministry of Petroleum) and EdCIL (Ministry of Education) → Miniratna-I PSUs; Dredging Corporation (1976) handed to 4 major ports in 2018, so now only 1 and 3.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which among the following are in the Private Sector?—

                                              Private sector refinery now → Essar Oil (Nayara Energy); Bongaigaon, Haldia and Mangalore (MRPL, ONGC subsidiary since March 2003) are public sector.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which of the following oil refinery is in the private sector?—

                                              Digboi, Barauni, Noonmati and Mathura refineries → all public sector; India has 23 refineries: 19 public, 3 private, 1 joint venture.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • HAL is related to manufacturing of:Aircrafts

                                              HAL (Bengaluru) → aircraft; founded 23 December 1940 as Hindustan Aircraft Ltd by Walchand Hirachand; management passed to Government of India in 1947.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • Which of the following is related with the field of electricity generation?N.H.P.C.

                                              Electricity generation → NHPC (erstwhile National Hydroelectric Corporation), Miniratna Category-I CPSE and India's largest hydropower organisation.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • The development of tourism and hotel industry in India is the function of:I.T.D.C.

                                              Tourism and hotel industry development → ITDC (India Tourism Development Corporation, October 1966); Government holds 87.03%.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                              • In which of the following years was the BSNL established?2000

                                              BSNL → formed in 2000 by corporatisation of the Department of Telecom Services.

                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                    • In which one of the following Public Sector Enterprises the Government has 100% equity?BSNL

                                                    100% Government of India owned enterprise (among BSNL, NTPC, BHEL, SBI) → BSNL.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which among the following was not the profit making central public sector enterprise during 2013-14?BSNL

                                                    Loss-making CPSE among ONGC, NTPC, IOC and BSNL → BSNL (in 2013-14 and also in 2022-23).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which Central Public Enterprise has borne loss in India in the year 2014-15?Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd.

                                                    Top loss-making CPSEs 2014-15: BSNL, Air India, MTNL; in 2022-23 the top loss-maker was HPCL, then BSNL.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The Gas Authority of India Ltd. has planned to invest Rs. 8,000 crores for laying pipelines from:Vijayawada to Vijaipur

                                                    GAIL (2009) planned Rs. 8000 crore, 1,100 km gas pipeline from Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh) to Vijaipur (Madhya Pradesh).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which amongst the following now decide the oil-prices in India?Oil companies

                                                    Petrol and diesel prices → decided by oil marketing companies; market-determined from 26 June 2010 (petrol) and 19 October 2014 (diesel).

                                                    Don't confuse Petrol was freed first (2010); diesel later (2014).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The concept of 'Navratna' is associated with:selected Public Sector Enterprises

                                                    Navratna → status for selected Central Public Sector Enterprises; first given to 9 CPSEs in 1997; three categories: Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following does not enjoy ‘Maharatna’ status(as on February 2013)?Oil India Limited

                                                    Not Maharatna (February 2013) → Oil India (then Navratna; Maharatna in 2023) and BEL; Maharatna scheme 2010-11; now 13 Maharatna, 20 Navratna, 65 Miniratna. Must know

                                                    Memory aid 13-20-65 = Maha, Nav, Mini (as on 30 April 2024).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                    • In which year Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) was received the status of Maharatna Company?2013

                                                    BHEL → got Maharatna status in 2013.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • As on October 2019, how many Maharatna Companies are in India?10

                                                    Maharatna companies → 10 in October 2019; 13 as on 30 April 2024.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following is included in ‘Navratna’?Bharat Electronics Limited

                                                    Navratna (among Coal India, BHEL, BEL, GAIL) → Bharat Electronics Ltd; other Navratnas include CONCOR, EIL, HAL, MTNL, NALCO, NBCC, NMDC.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The Public Sector undertaking included in ‘Navratna’ isMTNL

                                                    MTNL → Navratna; SAIL and GAIL → Maharatna.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following public sector undertakings has not been accorded status of ‘Navratna’?Indian Aluminium Company Limited

                                                    Not Navratna → Indian Aluminium Company (private, not a CPSE); SAIL, Power Grid and REC were Navratna then, now Maharatna.

                                                    Don't confuse Private Indian Aluminium Company with NALCO, the Navratna aluminium CPSE.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following Aluminium Companies has been given'Navaratna Status' by the Government of India?NALCO

                                                    NALCO (1981, Bhubaneswar, Ministry of Mines) → Navratna aluminium company; Government holds 51.28% (not BALCO, HINDALCO or MALCO).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • What was the maximum amount which has been provided as financial autonomy by the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises of Union Government to the 'Mini Ratna', Category-I?Rs. 500 crore

                                                    Miniratna Category-I → investment autonomy up to Rs. 500 crore or net worth, whichever lower; needs three years' profit, Rs.30 crore pre-tax profit once, positive net worth.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Six more Public Sector Undertakings have been accorded status of Miniratna by the Government of India (September 2006). Choose the one which is not included amongst them from the following:Indian Telephone Industries

                                                    Miniratna (19 September 2006) to six CPSEs: BSNL, BEML, Hindustan Latex, Engineering Projects, Rashtriya Ispat, Garden Reach; Indian Telephone Industries not included.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Match the following:(i) (iv) (ii) (iii)

                                                    Rajasthan policies: IT Policy → 2000; Mineral Policy → 2011; Hotel Policy → 2006; Industrial & Investment Promotion Policy → 2010.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Helpline 'Udyami' is meant for:Micro, small and medium enterprises

                                                    Udyami Helpline → call centre of Ministry of MSME; inaugurated 21st August 2010 by Dr. Manmohan Singh; toll-free 1800-180-6763.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Headquarter of Madhya Pradesh Finance Corporation is:Indore

                                                    Madhya Pradesh Financial Corporation (1955) → headquarters at Indore; finances small and medium industries.

                                                    Don't confuse Headquarters is Indore, not the capital Bhopal.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Long term credit to small and medium enterprises is provided in Uttar Pradesh through:All of the above

                                                    Long-term credit to small and medium enterprises in UP → UP Small Industries Corporation, UPSIDC (now UPSIDA) and UP Financial Corporation: all of these.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The U.P. Financial Corporation does not finance:Tourism related industries

                                                    UP Financial Corporation (1954, under SFCs Act 1951) → does not finance tourism related industries.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • 'Udyog Bandhu' is a/an:organization to assist industrial units in solving time-bound establishment and investment related problems

                                                    Udyog Bandhu (now Invest UP) → UP government society that facilitates investment and solves establishment and investment problems of industrial units.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which region of the Uttar Pradesh has developed most from the industrial point of view?Western

                                                    Most industrially developed region of Uttar Pradesh → Western UP (more urbanised, more workers in registered factories).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • BIFR is related to:Reconstruction and financing of sick units

                                                    BIFR (Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction, Ministry of Finance) → revival or closure of sick industrial units; dissolved 1 December 2016, cases sent to NCLT/NCLAT under IBC.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Mega Food Parks scheme has been initiated by the Government of India with the objective:To improve infrastructure facilities for food processing industries

                                                    Mega Food Parks → better infrastructure for food processing; cluster approach linking farmers, processors and retailers to cut wastage and raise farmers' income. Must know

                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following is a benefit of industrial development and foreign trade?Increased competition

                                                    Benefit of industrial development and foreign trade → increased competition (also more goods, higher growth, lower unemployment).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following is a social objective of business?Employment generation

                                                    Social objective of business → employment generation (also supply of quality goods); profit earning is an economic objective.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Why companies go for business process re-engineering with the help of technology?All of these

                                                    Business process re-engineering with technology: rising customer demands, IT gives competitive edge at lower cost, faster change after liberalisation → all of these.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:4 3 2 1

                                                    Sole trader → unlimited liability; Partnership → contractual relationship; Co-operatives → betterment of weaker sections; Public Limited Company → large number of risk bearers.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • With reference to the expenditure madeby an organisation or a company, which of the following statements is/are correct?1 only

                                                    Acquiring new technology → capital expenditure (buy, upgrade or extend life of assets); debt and equity financing are both capital receipts, not capital vs revenue expenditure.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • What does venture capital mean?A long-term start-up capital provided to new entrepreneurs

                                                    Venture capital → long-term start-up capital (private equity) for new entrepreneurs and small businesses with growth potential.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The first Industrial Policy of the free India was announced in:1948

                                                    First Industrial Policy of free India → April 1948, by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee (Industry Minister); set a mixed economy model.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Concept of 'Joint Sector' for industrial development of India was envisaged in Industrial Policy Resolution of:1956

                                                    Joint Sector concept → Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (second policy, placed by Nehru, April 1956; expand public and co-operative sectors). Must know

                                                    Don't confuse 1948 = first policy (mixed economy); 1956 = Industrial Policy Resolution; 1991 = liberalised policy.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                    • The licensing policy for the industries drew strength from:Industries Act 1951

                                                    Industrial licensing policy drew strength from the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • In India, liberal Industrial Policy was adopted in the year:1991

                                                    Liberal Industrial Policy adopted → 1991 (amid severe economic instability) to raise efficiency and growth.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Assertion (A): Many industries in India have obtained ISO 9001 and ISO 9002 certification in the recent past.Both A and Rare true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

                                                    Many Indian firms got ISO 9001/9002 certification (BIS) and licensing was liberalised (24 July 1991), but liberalisation does not explain ISO certification.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • According to 1991 Industrial Policy, the number of industries for which licensing was necessary, were:18

                                                    1991 Industrial Policy (24 July 1991, P.V. Narasimha Rao) → licence needed only for 18 industries; now only four need compulsory licensing.

                                                    Memory aid 18 in 1991 → four today.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The number of industries for which industrial licensing is required has now been reduced to:—

                                                    Industries needing compulsory licence: 15 at question time (option a); now only four (environmental, safety and strategic reasons).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The Policy of liberalization, privatization and globalization was announced as New Economic Policy by Prime Minister:Narsimha Rao

                                                    LPG New Economic Policy (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) → announced in 1991 under PM P.V. Narasimha Rao.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The Industrial Policy, 1991 was criticized on a number of poinsts. Which of the following was not one of them?Neglect of agriculture sector

                                                    Criticisms of Industrial Policy 1991: erratic growth, threat from foreign competition, misplaced faith in foreign investment; neglect of agriculture was not one.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Some time back, the Government of India, decided to delicense 'white goods' industry. 'White goods' include:items purchased for conspicuous consumption

                                                    White goods → home appliances (AC, refrigerator, washing machine) bought as conspicuous consumption items; industry delicensed in 1993.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • With reference to India, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?IPCL is India's largest petrochemicals company.; MTNL is listed in NYSE.

                                                    Not correct: 'IPCL is India's largest petrochemicals company' (second in 2002-03; merged with RIL in 2007); MTNL listed on NYSE November 2001.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following groups of goods is not included in FMCG (Fast Moving Consumer Goods)?Automobile (Car and Motor Cycle)

                                                    FMCG = quick-selling, low-cost non-durable goods (toiletries, dairy, bakery); automobiles (car, motorcycle) are not FMCG.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below in the lists:2 1 4 3

                                                    Pearl fishing → Tuticorin; Automobiles → Pune; Shipbuilding → Mormugao; Engineering goods → Pinjore.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following modes of privatization is the most comprehensive and complete?Transferring ownership and management to the private sector.

                                                    Most complete mode of privatisation → transfer of ownership and management to the private sector (divestment).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Why is the Government of India disinvesting its equity in the Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)?Neither 1 nor 2

                                                    Disinvestment aims: citizen participation, better governance, lower fiscal burden; Government keeps management control (at least 51%); not mainly to repay external debt.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • With reference to the National Investment Fund to which the disinvestment proceeds are routed, consider the following statements:3 and 4

                                                    National Investment Fund (November 2005, disinvestment proceeds) → managed by UTI, SBI and LIC mutual funds; 75% income for social sector schemes, 25% for CPSE capital; a Public Account.

                                                    Don't confuse NIF is a Public Account, not part of the Consolidated Fund; it is not managed by the Finance Ministry.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Assertion (A): Disinvestment is an integral part of liberalization of economy in India.BothAand Rare true, but R is not a correct explanation of A

                                                    Disinvestment is integral to liberalisation (cuts fiscal burden); proceeds used as per stated policy (NIF, November 2005), but R does not explain A.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Assertion (A): The Government is resorting to disinvestment of some of the public sector units (PSUs).A is true, but R is false

                                                    Disinvestment is done to cut fiscal burden and revenue shortfall, not because PSUs failed to create jobs (A true, R false).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Disinvestment in Public Enterprises started from which financial year?1991-92

                                                    Disinvestment began in 1991-92: minority stakes in 31 PSUs sold for Rs. 3038 crore.

                                                    • Which of the following Iron and Steel Plant is not located on a riverside?Bhilai

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following are the purposes to which the National Renewal Fund has been set up?1 and 2

                                                    National Renewal Fund (February 1992) → safety net for workers hit by modernisation, restructuring or closure of sick units; funded VRS and retraining; not for refugees. Must know

                                                    Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following is referred to as the ‘Golden Handshake’:Voluntary Retirement Scheme

                                                    Golden Handshake → Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS), used to cut surplus staff in public and private companies. Must know

                                                    Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                    • Korean multinational company POSCO wants to invest Rs. 52,000 crore in:Odisha

                                                    POSCO (South Korea, steel) → MoU with Odisha on June 22, 2005 for a 12 billion USD (Rs. 52,000 crore) plant near Paradip.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Kandla, situated in the Gulf of Kutch, is well known for which of the following industries?Export processing zone

                                                    Kandla (Gulf of Kutch) → Asia's first Export Processing Zone, 1965; now India's largest multi-product SEZ (KASEZ). Must know

                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                    • Consider the following statements: Industrial development in India, to anextent, is constrained by2, 3 and 4

                                                    Industrial development constrained by: lack of savings to invest, lack of technology, skills and infrastructure, low purchasing power of masses; not lack of entrepreneurship.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • A labour intensive industry is one that:employs more hands

                                                    Labour intensive industry → employs more hands (labour costs outweigh capital costs), e.g. hotels, agriculture, mining.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following groups is not co-partner of Industrial Relation?Consumers and their organizations

                                                    Co-partners of industrial relations: workers, managers and Central/State Governments (with their organisations); consumers are not co-partners.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The largest producer of sugar in India is:Uttar Pradesh

                                                    Largest sugar producer → Uttar Pradesh (119.9 lakh tonnes, 2023-24, ISMA), then Maharashtra (99.9) and Karnataka (49.7).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following statement/s is/are correct? I. The sugar industry was initially located in Uttar Pradesh. II. The low yield of sugarcane, short crushing seasons, unsatisfactory location of industries created problems in producing sugar. Code:Both I and II

                                                    Sugar industry began in UP (first mill Pratappur, Deoria, 1903); low cane yield, short crushing season, poor location caused problems; UP lost lead to Maharashtra in 1960s.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Sugar industry is mostly developed in which State?Uttar Pradesh

                                                    Sugar industry most developed → Uttar Pradesh (leading sugarcane and sugar producing State).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The President of Sugar De-control Committee was:C. Rangarajan

                                                    Sugar de-regulation committee → Dr. C. Rangarajan; levy obligation ended for sugar after September 2012, regulated release abolished; 2013-14 a watershed.

                                                    Don't confuse Cane area reservation, minimum distance and cane price formula were left to State Governments.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which pair is not correctly matched?Katni - Paper

                                                    Not matched: Katni – Paper; Katni (MP) is known for cement, limestone and fireclay; Surat → cotton textiles; Churk → cement; Ludhiana → hosiery.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below:4 3 2 1

                                                    Jute products → Titagarh; silk textile → Bangalore (Bengaluru); woollen hosiery → Ludhiana; woollen carpet → Bhadohi.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • HINDALCO, an aluminium factory located at Renukoot owes its site basically to:abundant supply of electricity

                                                    HINDALCO Renukoot (1962) sited for abundant electricity: Renusagar captive power plant (840 MW, 1967), first for aluminium in India.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?Madras Aluminium Company – Chennai Limited (MALCO)

                                                    MALCO → Mettur (Salem, Tamil Nadu), not Chennai; BALCO → Korba; INDAL → Hirakud (now part of HINDALCO); HINDALCO → Renukoot.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following States enjoys ideal conditions for the development ofpetrochemical industries:Gujarat

                                                    Ideal for petrochemicals → Gujarat (infrastructure, strategic location, skilled labour, raw material; leader in chemicals).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Assertion (A): Coastal Gujarat has been called an industrial workshop.Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A.

                                                    Coastal Gujarat → 'industrial workshop' because it is dotted with textile, pharmaceutical and petrochemical units (A and R true; R explains A).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Participation of labourers in management means:Participation in policy-decision making

                                                    Workers' participation in management → participation of non-managerial employees in policy decision-making.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following industrial towns is located on the Chota Nagpur plateau?Ranchi

                                                    Industrial town on the Chota Nagpur plateau ('Ruhr of India') → Ranchi (HEC, mineral based industries).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Dewas is famous for its:Printing of currency notes

                                                    Dewas (Madhya Pradesh) → Government currency note printing press.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Consider the following factors regarding an industry:1, 3 and 4

                                                    Nature and size of an industry → capital investment, labour force and power consumption (book: turnover also counts today).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following are correctly matched?2 and 3 only

                                                    First machine-made paper → 1870, Bally near Calcutta; first cement factory → 1904 near Madras; first cotton mill → 1818 Fort Gloster, not 1854 Bombay (second).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Consider the following events and arrange these in chronological order: I. Development of sugar industry by Indians II. Starting of first jute mill in Rishra III. Production of steel in India for the first time IV. Starting of first textile mill in Bombay Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code:I, II, IV and III

                                                    First steel attempt Porto Novo (J.M. Heath) 1830; first Bombay textile mill (Davar) 7 July 1854; first jute mill Rishra 1855; first sugar mill Pratappur 1903.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which pairs are correctly matched?2, 3 and 4

                                                    Mundra SEZ → Adani; CMC Ltd → Tata; IPCL → Reliance; VSNL → Tata (Tata Communications, February 2008), not Bharti.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which among the following multinational companies are functioning in India?2 and 4 only

                                                    Multinationals in India (book): Samsung and LG; Hindustan Unilever is an Indian subsidiary of Unilever and GKW is not a multinational.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Consider the following pairs:3 and 4

                                                    Renault SA → France; Volkswagen AG → Germany; BMW AG → Munich, Germany (not USA); Daimler AG → not Sweden.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The All India Khadi and Village Industries Board was set up during the:1st Plan

                                                    All India Khadi and Village Industries Board → January 1953 (First Plan, 1951-56); KVIC statutory body under KVIC Act 1956, took over in April 1957.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The head office of Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) is located at:Mumbai

                                                    KVIC (statutory commission, Ministry of MSME) → head office at Mumbai.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?Tarapore Committee - Customer Services in Banks

                                                    Not matched: Tarapore Committee → full capital account convertibility of rupee, not bank customer services; Goswami → industrial sickness; Janakiraman → share scam; Malhotra → insurance reforms.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Meera Seth committee was related to:Development of Handlooms

                                                    Meera Seth Committee (12 members, 1995) → handloom development; recommended National Handloom Fund of Rs. 500 crore.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Sathyam Committee deals with:Textile policy

                                                    Sathyam Committee (July 1998, report August 1999) → textile policy; basis of National Textile Policy 2000.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • The Chairman of the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganized Sector is:Arjun Sengupta

                                                    National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS) → chairman Dr. Arjun Sengupta; set up 20.09.2004; term ended 30.04.2009.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation established in 1969 under the Companies Act 1956 helps to:all the above

                                                    RIICO (Rajasthan; began 28th March 1969 as RSIMDC, split 1st January 1980) → sets up industrial areas, social infrastructure, project reports and managerial services: all these.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation (RIICO) has signed a MOU with a Japanese company for establishment of Japanese units in Neemrana Industrial Area. That Japanese company is:Jetro

                                                    RIICO signed MoU with JETRO (Japan External Trade Organization) in July 2008 to bring Japanese units to Neemrana Industrial Area.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • In the States of India, the State Finance Corporations have given assistance mainly to develop:Medium and Small Scale Industry

                                                    State Finance Corporations → mainly finance medium and small scale industries (supplementing Industrial Finance Corporation, IFC Act 1948).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following pairs (industry and industrialist) is not properly matched?Wipro – R. Krishnamurthy

                                                    Not matched: Wipro – R. Krishnamurthy; Wipro's founder chairman is Azim Premji (Rishad Premji chairman from 2019); Reliance – Mukesh Ambani; Airtel – Bharti Mittal.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • 'e-Biz' refer to:single window for approach to government services

                                                    E-Biz portal (Ministry of Commerce and Industry, 28.01.2013) → single window for business access to government services (ease of doing business).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • E-Commerce means:Trade on Internet

                                                    E-commerce → buying and selling goods over the internet (through computers, tablets, smartphones).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which dimension of e-commerce enables commerce beyond the boundaries of the country?Global reach

                                                    E-commerce dimension for trade beyond national boundaries → global reach (others: richness, interactivity, ubiquity).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which one of the following is largest e-commerce company of India?M-junction

                                                    Largest e-commerce company of India (book) → M-junction (SAIL–Tata Steel 50:50 venture, February 2001); world's largest e-marketplace for steel.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Assertion (A): Information technology is fast becoming a very important field of activity in India.A is true, but R is false

                                                    IT is a fast-growing field and software is a major export, but India does not have a strong hardware base (A true, R false).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which among the following is the largest software company in India?TCS

                                                    Largest software company in India (by market capitalisation) → TCS (Tata Consultancy Services).

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following statement related to automobile sector is not correct?It generated direct and indirect employment of5.3 crore at the end of2021.

                                                    Automobile sector (Economic Survey 2022-23): 7.1% of GDP, 49% of manufacturing GDP, 3.7 crore jobs (not 5.3 crore) end-2021; largest two/three-wheeler maker, fourth in cars.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • Which of the following statement, related to Pharmaceutical sector is not correct?India has 80 percent market share of global vaccine manufacturing.

                                                    Pharma (Economic Survey 2022-23): 3rd by volume, 14th by value; largest generic supplier (20% of global volume); vaccine market share 60%, not 80%.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                    • What is/are the purpose/purposes of 'District Mineral Foundations' in India?2 only

                                                    District Mineral Foundation → non-profit trust in mining-affected districts for benefit of affected persons; funded by miners; mandated by MMDR Amendment Act 2015.

                                                    Don't confuse DMF does not promote exploration or issue licences.

                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          Tertiary Sector

                                                          18 facts · 23 questions · 3 Must know

                                                          Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                          • In India Tertiary Sector includes:1 and 2 only

                                                          Tertiary (services) sector: trade, transport, hotels, communication, finance, real estate; forestry, fishing and mining are not services; services share 54.9% of GVA (2023-24). Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                          • Which one of the following is a tertiary activity?Marketing

                                                          Marketing → tertiary activity; farming and forestry → primary; manufacturing → secondary; agriculture is the primary sector. Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                          • Transport, Communication, Commerce come under the:Tertiary activities

                                                          Transport, communication and commerce → tertiary (services) activities.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • The largest source of National Income in India is:Service Sector

                                                          Largest source of National Income → services sector: 54.9% of nominal GVA (Rs. 146.35 lakh crore of Rs. 266.78 lakh crore, 2023-24).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • The share of Tertiary Sector in Indian economy during 2016-17 was:—

                                                          Services share 2016-17 → 52.6% of GVA (Rs. 73.49 lakh crore of Rs. 139.65 lakh crore).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following activities?1, 3, 2, 4

                                                          Sector shares at question time (2000-01 prices): Agriculture > Trade-hotels-transport > Manufacturing > Finance-real estate; now services 54.9%, industry 27.6%, agriculture 17.6% (2023-24).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • During 2006-2010, which of the following service sectors registered fastest growth in India?Communication

                                                          Fastest growing service sector in India during 2006-2010 → communication.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Among the services sector, which has the highest share in the India’s GDP in 2006?Trade, Hotels, Transport and Communication

                                                          Highest services sub-sector share in GDP (2006-07) → Trade, Hotels, Transport and Communication; this group is 17.6% of GVA in 2023-24.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • The largest share of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in India comes from:Services sector

                                                          Largest share of India's GDP/GVA → services (tertiary) sector; order: Services > Industry > Agriculture. Must know

                                                          Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                          • The share of services in India's GDP and total employment in 2012-13 respectively are approximately57% and 28%

                                                          Services share 2012-13 → about 57% of GDP (56.9%) and 28% of employment (28.1%); 2018-19: 54.3% of GVA, 34% of employment.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • For which of the following States the share of services sector in State GDP has been largest in 2008-09?Delhi

                                                          Highest services share in State GDP (2008-09) → Delhi, then Chandigarh, Kerala, Maharashtra; in 2019-20 Chandigarh (74.00%) and Delhi (68.22%) top.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Which of the following statements is not true about the Indian Economy?The share of services sector in India’s GDP is only 25%

                                                          Wrong statement: 'services share of India's GDP only 25%' (it was 57.09% in 2009-10); 58.2% workforce in agriculture (Census 2001).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • What was the rank of growth rate of services sector of India in world during the period 2001 to 2012?Second

                                                          Services growth 2001-2012 → India second fastest (CAGR 9.0%) after China (10.9%) (Economic Survey 2013-14).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • Since 1980, the share of the tertiary sector in the total GDP of India has:shown an increasing trend

                                                          Tertiary share in India's GDP since 1980 → increasing trend (about 49.0% in 2011-12; 54.9% now).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • In India, between 2001 to 2005, growth rate of which sector has consistently increased?Services

                                                          Sector whose growth rate rose steadily 2001-2005 → services (5.6% to 9.9%).

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • As the economy develops, the share of the tertiary sector in the GDP:Increases

                                                          As an economy develops, the tertiary sector's share in GDP increases (India: 30.3% in 1950-51 → 50.37% in 2000-01).

                                                          Memory aid Clark-type shift: farm → factory → services as income grows.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • During 2011-12 to 2015-16, the contribution of Services Sector in the growth rate of Indian economy is:69.0 percent

                                                          Services' contribution to GVA growth during 2011-12 to 2015-16 → about 69.0%; in 2017-18 about 72.5%.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                          • According to Economic Survey 2023 about services, which statement among the following is not correct?Fashion, grocery and general merchandise will be captured nearly two-third of the Indian e-commerce market by 2030.

                                                          Economic Survey 2023: fashion, grocery and general merchandise to capture nearly two-thirds of e-commerce by 2027 (not 2030); 75 digital banking units; services credit growth above 16%.

                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                Hour 12 →
