                                                                Fiscal Policy & Revenue · part 1 of 5

                                                                50 facts · 56 questions · 7 Must know

                                                                Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                • Along with the Budget, the Finance Minister also places other documents before the Parliament which include 'The Macro Economic Framework Statement'. The aforesaid document is presented because this is mandated by:Provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003

                                                                Macro-Economic Framework Statement → mandated by Section 3(5) of FRBM Act, 2003; presented with the Budget (overview of GDP growth, fiscal and external balance).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • When was gender budgeting initiated in India?Union Budget, 2005-06

                                                                Gender budgeting → first introduced in Union Budget 2005-06 (4.8% of total outlay then).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which among the following is not included in the ten main themes of the Union Budget for the financial year 2017-18?Export performance

                                                                Union Budget 2017-18 had 10 themes: farmers, rural population, youth, poor, infrastructure, financial sector, digital economy, public services, fiscal management, tax administration; not export performance.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following is not included in the priorities of India Budget 2022-23?Disinvestment

                                                                Budget 2022-23 four priorities: PM GatiShakti; Inclusive Development; Productivity, Investment, Energy Transition and Climate Action; Financing of Investments; disinvestment not one.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following was not included in the intended objectives of the Union Budget, 2017-18?Educate India

                                                                Budget 2017-18 (Arun Jaitley, 1st February 2017) agenda → TEC India: Transform, Energise, Clean India; not 'Educate India'.

                                                                Memory aid TEC = Transform, Energise, Clean.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • According to the Union Budget 2021-22, Finance Minister proposed a new levy Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess. This cess will be levied on how many products?29

                                                                Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess (Budget 2021-22) → levied on 29 products to fund agriculture infrastructure.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • As per the Economic Survey 2015-16, which one of the following has been constructed as the Chakravyuha Challenge of the Indian economy?Movement of Indian economy from socialism with limited entry to marketism without exit

                                                                Chakravyuha Challenge (Economic Survey 2015-16) → economy moved from 'socialism with limited entry' to 'marketism without exit' (easy entry, hard exit).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which statement is true for Finance Sector (Fiscal Management) in the Union Budget, 2023?Fiscal Deficit of3.5% of GSDP allowed for States.

                                                                Budget 2023-24: States allowed fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GSDP (0.5% tied to power reforms); total expenditure about Rs. 45 lakh crore; 2025-26 deficit target below 4.5%.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Consider the following statements:Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A).

                                                                Fiscal deficit 2017-18 → 3.5% of GDP vs 3.2% budgeted, as indirect tax growth slowed with GST (A and R true; R explains A).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                Gross tax/GDP (10.1% in 2010-11, 11.2% in 2017-18) fluctuated; fiscal deficit/GDP (5.9% in 2011-12, 3.5% in 2017-18) fell overall → neither rose steadily.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Consider the following items:1, 2 and 4 only

                                                                GST exempt (0%): hulled cereal grains, cooked chicken eggs in shell, newspapers (even with ads); processed and canned fish taxed at 5%.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The ‘Goods and Services Tax’ was proposed by a task force, whose President was:Vijay Kelkar

                                                                GST was proposed by the Vijay Kelkar Task Force (on FRBM, formed 2003; recommended GST in 2004).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • What is/are the most likely advantages of implementing ‘Goods and Services Tax’(GST)?1 only

                                                                GST's main advantage → replaces multiple taxes of multiple authorities, creating a single market; claims of 'drastically' cutting CAD or 'enormously' raising growth are overstated.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • What kind of tax is GST?Indirect Tax

                                                                GST → single, comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax (from 1 July 2017); subsumed Service Tax, Central Excise and State VAT. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following Constitution (Amendment) Act provides for Goods and Services Tax (G.S.T.)?The Constitution (One Hundred and First) Amendment Act, 2016

                                                                GST → Constitution (One Hundred and First) Amendment Act, 2016; GST in force from 1 July 2017. Must know

                                                                Don't confuse Act number (101st) differs from its Bill number (One Hundred and Twenty Second Amendment Bill).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • GST (Goods and Services Tax) is now proposed to be introduced in India from:—

                                                                GST was then proposed from April 01, 2012 (option b); it actually came into effect on 1 July 2017 via the 101st Amendment (2016).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The introduction of Goods and Services Tax from July 2017 is expected to create:Both (a) and (b) above

                                                                GST (July 2017) → uniform common national market and better tax compliance; ends cascading (double) taxation.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Consider the following statements:Only 1 and 2 are correct

                                                                GST Council (Article 279A) → chaired by Union Finance Minister, MoS Revenue/Finance a member; decides rates, exemptions, threshold; States cannot levy VAT after GST.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following tax is not included in Goods and Services Tax (GST)?Custom Duty

                                                                Not under GST → customs duty; also outside GST: alcohol for human consumption, petroleum products and electricity.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • What has been kept under the purview of Goods and Services Tax (GST)?Ghee

                                                                Under GST → ghee; outside GST → alcohol for human consumption, electricity and petroleum products.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The collection of 'Goods and Service Tax' in Indian economy in October, 2020 has been:More than Rs. One lakh crore

                                                                Gross GST collection October 2020 → Rs. 105,155 crore (above Rs. one lakh crore); record Rs. 210,267 crore in April 2024.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The term 'Revenue Neutral Rate' was in news recently is related to:Goods and Service Tax (GST)

                                                                Revenue Neutral Rate → GST rate that keeps government revenue equal to revenue under the old tax system.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?Only 1

                                                                Input Tax Credit (ITC) → credit of input tax on goods/services received by a registered person; allowed for taxable and zero-rated supplies, not non-taxable, exempt or nil-rated.

                                                                Don't confuse Zero-rated (exports, SEZ supplies; ITC allowed) is not nil-rated (0% GST; no ITC).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Saksham project approved by Govt. of India is related to:A new indirect tax network

                                                                Project Saksham (CCEA, September 2016) → new indirect tax IT network of CBEC for GST; cost Rs. 2256 crore over seven years.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • In India, which one among the following formulates the fiscal policy?Ministry of Finance

                                                                Fiscal policy → formulated by Ministry of Finance; monetary policy → RBI; Finance Commission (Article 280) → tax sharing between Union and States. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Long-term fiscal policy was announced by which finance minister of India?V.P. Singh

                                                                Long-term fiscal policy → announced by Finance Minister V.P. Singh in his Budget Speech 1985-86.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The controlling authority of government expenditure is:The Ministry of Finance

                                                                Government expenditure is controlled by the Ministry of Finance; its six Departments: Economic Affairs, Expenditure, Revenue, DIPAM, Financial Services, Public Enterprises (no 'Banking Division').

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • The following table shows the percentage distribution of revenue expenditure of Government of India in 1989-90 and 1994-95: Expenditure Head (Percent of Total)spend more and more on interest payments

                                                                Revenue expenditure 1989-90 vs 1994-95: interest payments share rose (27.7% → 38.7%), so the Union is under pressure to spend more on interest.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following is not an objective of fiscal policy of Government of India?Regulation of inter-state trade

                                                                Fiscal policy objectives: growth, full employment, price stability, equitable distribution of income and wealth; regulating inter-state trade is not one.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Fiscal policy is concerned with which of the following?The policy regarding taxation and government expenditure

                                                                Fiscal policy → government policy on taxation and expenditure (to influence the economy).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following is a part of fiscal policy?Tax policy

                                                                Fiscal policy instruments → taxation, public expenditure and public debt; so tax policy is part of fiscal policy.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following is NOT a tool of fiscal policy?Interest rate

                                                                Fiscal tools: public expenditure, taxation, deficit financing; interest rate is a monetary policy tool.

                                                                Don't confuse Interest rate = monetary policy (RBI); taxes and spending = fiscal policy (Finance Ministry).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following economists, introduced fiscal policy as a tool to rectify the Great Depression of 1929- 30?Prof. Keynes

                                                                Fiscal policy as remedy for the Great Depression (1929-30) → J.M. Keynes, 'General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money' (1936): raise government spending.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following statements appropriately describes the 'fiscal stimulus'?It is an intense affirmative action of the Government to boost economic activity in the country.

                                                                Fiscal stimulus → intense government action (tax rebates, incentives, spending) to boost economic activity.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which among the following steps is most likely to be taken at the time of an economic recession?Increase in expenditure on public projects

                                                                In a recession → increase expenditure on public projects; recession = real GDP contracts for at least two consecutive quarters.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • The revenue estimates of the Budget in India are prepared by:The Ministry of Finance

                                                                Budget revenue estimates → Ministry of Finance; Union Budget prepared and presented by its Department of Economic Affairs; revenue control via CBDT (Department of Revenue).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Economic Survey of India is related to:Ministry of Finance

                                                                Economic Survey → Ministry of Finance (prepared by Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser); presented before the Union Budget. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Economic Survey of India is published officially, every year by the:Ministry of Finance, Govt. of India

                                                                Economic Survey → published every year by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; reviews the past financial year; tabled before the Budget. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                • Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes below the lists:3 4 1 2

                                                                Wholesale Price Index → Ministry of Commerce & Industry; National Accounts Statistics → CSO (now NSO); Report on Currency and Finance → RBI; Economic Survey → Ministry of Finance.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • 'Budget' is an instrument of-fiscal policy of the government

                                                                Budget → instrument of fiscal policy; Article 112 'Annual Financial Statement' laid before both Houses every year.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • In which of the following countries, zero-based budgeting was first adopted?U.S.A.

                                                                Zero-based budgeting (Peter Pyhrr, 1970s) → first adopted in USA (Jimmy Carter, Georgia, 1973); India: DST 1983, Government 1986; every scheme reviewed from zero. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                • Which of the following (Union Budget Departments 2023- 24 –Allocation amount approx. Rs.) is correctly matched?Ministry of Health – Rs. 89,155 Crore

                                                                Budget 2023-24: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare → Rs. 89,155 crore; Dept of Health and Family Welfare Rs. 86175 crore; PMJAY Rs. 7200 crore; Health Research Rs. 2980 crore.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • In the Union Budget for 2011-12, which one of the following sectors has been allocated largest outlay?Energy

                                                                Largest sector outlay in Union Budget 2011-12 → Energy (by 2024-25 data, Transport is far larger).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • As per Budget Estimates 2010-11, presented to the Parliament on 2016-02-10, arrange the following sectors in descending order as per their Central Plan outlay.2, 4, 3, 1

                                                                Central Plan outlay 2010-11, descending: Energy > Social Services > Transport > Rural Development. Must know

                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                • As per Union Budget 2018-19, match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the lists:4 3 2 1

                                                                Budget 2018-19 allocations: Defence Rs. 2.82 lakh crore; Agriculture Rs. 0.63; Food subsidy Rs. 1.69; Rural development Rs. 1.38 lakh crore.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following is not true about the total outlay in the Union Budget 2023-24?Subsidies (9%)

                                                                Budget 2023-24 outlay shares: interest 20%, States' share of taxes 18%, subsidies 7% (not 9%), defence 8%.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • In the Union Budget for 2010-11, capital receipts:are less than revenue receipts

                                                                Capital receipts are less than revenue receipts (2010-11 and now; 2024-25 interim: 37.02% vs 62.98%).

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following is not a source of Public revenue?Subsidy

                                                                Subsidy → public expenditure, not public revenue; income tax, VAT and public borrowing are sources of public revenue.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which among the following are the sources of income in current account of the Central Government? I. Corporation Tax II. Profit from Public Enterprises III. Sale of National Savings Certificates IV. Loans received from the World Bank V. Excise duties Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:I, II and V

                                                                Current (revenue) account income: corporation tax, profits of public enterprises, excise duties; NSC sales and World Bank loans are capital receipts.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                • Which one of the following is not included in the revenue account of Union Budget?Small Savings

                                                                Revenue account: interest receipts, tax receipts, profits and dividends of PSUs; small savings → debt receipts in the capital account.

                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following is/are included in the Capital Budget of the Government of India?1, 2 and 3

                                                                      Capital budget includes: asset creation (roads, buildings, machinery), loans from foreign governments, loans and advances to States and UTs: all three.

                                                                      • Which of the following come under Non-Plan Expenditure?1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                      Non-Plan expenditure (before Budget 2017-18): subsidies, interest payments, defence, maintenance of past-plan assets, salaries, pensions, statutory transfers to States. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                      • In the Union Budgets in India, which one of the following is the largest in amount?Revenue expenditure

                                                                      Largest in Union Budget → revenue expenditure; Plan/Non-Plan classification was removed from Budget 2017-18.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following did not take place in the Union Budget for 2017-18?Increase in the number of centrally sponsored schemes.

                                                                      Budget 2017-18 reforms: presented 1 February (a month earlier), Railway Budget merged, Plan/Non-Plan ended; no increase in centrally sponsored schemes. Must know

                                                                      • There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which action/actions of the following can be taken by the Government to reduce the deficit?1 and 3 only

                                                                      To cut a persistent deficit: reduce revenue expenditure and rationalise subsidies; new welfare schemes and lower import duties would widen it.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which among the following is the most important item of revenue expenditure of the Union Government?Interest Payment

                                                                      Largest item of revenue (and total) expenditure of the Union → interest payments (2024-25: 32.57% of revenue expenditure). Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 8 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which among the following is the largest item of current revenue expenditure of Central Government in the year 2008-10?Interest Payments

                                                                      Largest current revenue expenditure item of the Centre in 2008-10 → interest payments; still the largest (Interim Budget 2024-25).

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following is the most important item of Non-Plan expenditure of the Central Government during 2015-16 budget?Interest payments

                                                                      Largest Non-Plan expenditure item (2015-16) → interest payments; Plan/Non-Plan classification ended in Budget 2017-18. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                      • In the context of governance, consider the following:3 and 4 only

                                                                      Fiscal deficit control: downsizing bureaucracy (less spending) and selling PSU shares (more receipts); encouraging FDI or privatising higher education does not directly help.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which one of the following statements is/are correct with reference to India?1 and 2 only

                                                                      Fiscal deficit: 2017-18 raised to 3.5% (from 3.2%); 2018-19 target 3.3%; 2020-21 projected 3.0% (not 3.1%); 2021-22 estimated 6.8%. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      • Consider the following statements about the latest developments in the Union Government finances:Only 1

                                                                      Union fiscal deficit: 9.2% of GDP in FY21 (pandemic); 6.7% in FY22 (not 7.7%); revenue receipts fell only in FY21.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • For the Financial Year 2019-20 the Union Government aims to restrict the fiscal deficit at:3.3 percent of GDP

                                                                      Fiscal deficit target 2019-20 → 3.3% of GDP; 2020-21 target 3.5%; actuals 4.6% and 9.2% (Covid-19).

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • In the Union Budget 2000-2001 the fiscal deficit has been pegged at:5.1 percent

                                                                      Fiscal deficit target in Union Budget 2000-01 → 5.1% of GDP; 2024-25 interim target is also 5.1%.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Fiscal deficit/GDP ratio has been maximumin the financial year:2011-2012

                                                                      Highest fiscal deficit/GDP among 2011-2012 to 2014-2015 → 2011-12 (5.9%); 1990-91 was 8.4%; 2020-21 hit 9.2%, highest since 1990-91. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      • In the Union Budget of 1996-97, the target level offiscal deficit is:5.0 percent of GDP

                                                                      Fiscal deficit target in Union Budget 1996-97 → 5.0% of GDP.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • As per the Budget 2001-2002 the current fiscal deficit of India is:4.7 percent

                                                                      Fiscal deficit as per Budget 2001-2002 → 4.7% of GDP; 2024-25 interim → 5.1% (Rs. 1685494 crore). Must know

                                                                      • In the Budget 2009-10 the fiscal deficit is placed at:6.8%

                                                                      Fiscal deficit in Union Budget 2009-10 → 6.8% of GDP.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • In the Union Budget 2010-11, fiscal deficit is estimated at:5.5% of GDP

                                                                      Fiscal deficit estimate in Union Budget 2010-11 → 5.5% of GDP (actual 4.9%).

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • What is the fiscal deficit target of India for the financial year 2016-17?3.5% of GDP

                                                                      Fiscal deficit target for 2016-17 → 3.5% of GDP.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • What was the most important reason for the popularity of the National Budget of February 1997?Reduction in almost every tax

                                                                      Budget 1997-98 (P. Chidambaram) popular for cutting almost every tax: income tax 10, 20, 30% (from 15, 30, 40%); corporate tax 48% → 35%.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • The present fiscal deficit of States has touched a record of:—

                                                                      States' record fiscal deficit at question time → Rs. 1,00,000 crore (option d); States' combined GFD 2023-24 (B.E.) Rs. 9.48 lakh crore (3.1% of GDP).

                                                                      • Consider the following statements with reference to Uttar Pradesh Budget, 2023-24:Only 2

                                                                      • With reference to the Indian Public Finance, consider the following statements:2, 3 and 4

                                                                      Budget external liabilities use current exchange rates, not historical; high borrowing keeps real interest rates high; rising fiscal deficit hurts private investment; interest is largest non-plan revenue item.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Consider the following budget deficits of Central Government:2, 3, 1

                                                                      Descending order of deficits: Fiscal > Revenue > Primary; fiscal deficit is always higher than revenue deficit. Must know

                                                                      Memory aid F-R-P: Fiscal is Fattest, Primary is Puniest.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                      • Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:3 1 2 4

                                                                      Budget deficit = total expenditure – total receipts (dropped from 1997-98); Revenue = revenue expenditure – revenue receipts; Fiscal = budget deficit + borrowings; Primary = fiscal – interest payments. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                      • Fiscal deficit implies:Total expenditure – (Revenue receipts + recovery of loans + receipts from disinvestment)

                                                                      Fiscal deficit = total expenditure – (revenue receipts + recovery of loans + disinvestment receipts), i.e. minus non-debt capital receipts.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Which of the following expression shows the formula of Gross Fiscal Deficit?Gross Fiscal Deficit Net borrowing at home + Borrowing from RBI + Borrowing from abroad

                                                                      Gross Fiscal Deficit (financing side) = net borrowing at home + borrowing from RBI + borrowing from abroad; it shows total borrowing need.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • In India's Union Budget, Fiscal deficit means:The difference between total revenue and total expenditure of the government

                                                                      Fiscal deficit → gap between government's total expenditure and total income (revenue plus non-debt capital receipts); also shown as % of GDP.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Assertion (A): Fiscal deficit is greater than budgetary deficit.Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A

                                                                      Fiscal deficit > budgetary deficit because borrowings and liabilities are receipts but not income; fiscal deficit = RBI borrowing plus other liabilities (A and R true; R explains A).

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • If interest payments are subtracted from gross fiscal deficit, the remainder will be:Gross primary deficit

                                                                      Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments; so primary deficit + interest = fiscal deficit. Must know

                                                                      Memory aid Primary deficit = today's gap without the burden of past debt's interest.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                      • Ifprimary deficit is zero, then the amount of borrowing will be:just equal to the interest payment

                                                                      If primary deficit is zero → fiscal deficit equals interest payments, so borrowing is just equal to interest payment.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Primary deficit in the Union Budget for2010-11 is estimated at:below 2.0 percent of the GDP

                                                                      Primary deficit estimate in Budget 2010-11 → below 2.0% of GDP; 2023-24 → 2.3%; 2024-25 interim target 1.5%.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • Revenue deficit in India implies that:the Indian Government needs to borrow in order to finance its expenses which do not create capital assets

                                                                      Revenue deficit → Government borrows to finance expenses that do not create capital assets (day-to-day spending).

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                      • After deducting grants for the creation of capital assets from revenue deficit, we arrive at:Effective Revenue Deficit

                                                                      Effective Revenue Deficit = revenue deficit – grants for creation of capital assets; introduced in Union Budget 2011-12; added to FRBM Act in 2012. Must know

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                      Part of household financial savings goes to government borrowing; dated securities issued at market-related rates in auctions form a large part of internal debt: both correct.

                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                            • A larger part of the fiscal deficit in Union Government Budget is filled by:Domestic borrowings

                                                                            Larger part of fiscal deficit → financed by domestic borrowings (about 98-99%), mainly market borrowings (G-secs).

                                                                            • Assertion (A): Deficit financing leads to inflation.Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of(A)

                                                                            Deficit financing (new currency) raises money supply relative to goods and services → inflation (A and R true; R explains A). Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following is likely to be the most inflationary in its effects?Creation of new money to finance a budget deficit

                                                                            Most inflationary → creating new money to finance a budget deficit; borrowing from public or banks does not add money supply.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • In India, deficit financing is used for raising resources for:economic development

                                                                            Deficit financing in India → used for raising resources for economic development.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The Budget for 2012-13 sought to restrict expenditure on subsidies to:3.5 percent of GDP

                                                                            Budget 2012-13 sought to restrict subsidies to 3.5% of GDP (2024-25 interim: about 1.25% of GDP).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Statement (A): Abig source of deficit in the Government’s budget is the financial subsidy.A is true, but R is false

                                                                            Subsidy is a big source of budget deficit (about 12% of spending then), but Indian farm subsidy is lower than in developed countries (A true, R false).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Consider the following statements:(A) is true, but (R) is false

                                                                            India has a history of fiscal deficits, but Indian agriculture gets far lower subsidies than Western countries (A true, R false).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statements is not correct?A Money Bill is concerned with appropriation of money out of the Contingency Fund of India.

                                                                            Money Bill (Article 110) → appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India, not the Contingency Fund; also covers taxes, custody of funds, borrowing.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • With respect to the procedure of Budget in the Parliament, "the amount of demand be reduced to Re 1" is called:Policy Cut Motion

                                                                            Cut motions: Policy Cut → demand reduced to Re 1 (disapproval of policy); Economy Cut → by a specific amount; Token Cut → by Rs. 100. Must know

                                                                            Memory aid Policy = Re 1; Token = Rs. 100; Economy = specific amount.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following is not correctly matched?Vote on Account – Parliamentary sanction of all budgetary demands for grants in a financial year

                                                                            Vote on Account → advance grant from Consolidated Fund for short-term spending until the Budget is passed; not sanction of all demands for the year. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • The Finance Ministry (Government of India) has introduced the concept of 'Outcome Budget' from 2005. Under this, the monitoring of the outcomes will be the responsibility of:Finance Ministry and Planning Commission jointly

                                                                            Outcome Budget (from 2005) → outcomes monitored jointly by Finance Ministry and Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The concept of Performance Budget has been borrowed from:U.S.A.

                                                                            Performance Budget → first introduced in USA on Hoover Commission recommendation (1949).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Ad hoc Treasury bill system of meeting budget deficit in India was abolished on:31st March, 1997

                                                                            Ad hoc Treasury Bills (from mid-1950s) abolished 31 March 1997; replaced by Ways and Means Advances (WMA) from 1st April 1997.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The Indian Parliament exercises control on the audit of the Budget through its:Public Accounts Committee

                                                                            Parliament's audit control over Budget → Public Accounts Committee (22 members: 15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha; examines CAG reports; opposition chairman since 1967).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                                                            FRBM Review Committee (N.K. Singh, January 2017): debt-GDP 60% by 2023 (Centre 40%, States 20%); Article 293(3): indebted State needs Centre's consent for loans.

                                                                            Don't confuse Statement 2 reverses it: Centre's liabilities were 49.4% of GDP and States' 21%.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in India in the year:2003

                                                                            FRBM Act → enacted August 2003; in force from 5 July 2004; aims at fiscal discipline and lower deficits.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • According to FRBM Bill, the target for achieving the tax-GDP ratio by 2008-09 is:12 percent

                                                                            FRBM target for tax-GDP ratio by 2008-09 → 12%.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following was not stipulated in the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003?Elimination of primary deficit by the end of the fiscal year 2008-09

                                                                            FRBM Act 2003 did not stipulate eliminating primary deficit by 2008-09; it aimed to eliminate revenue deficit by 2007-08, limit RBI borrowing, cap guarantees.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 is adopted in Rajasthan with objectives to:Ensure financial discipline in Government

                                                                            Rajasthan FRBM Act 2005 → ensure financial discipline (fiscal prudence, lower revenue deficit, transparency).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • What was the disinvestment target for Public Sector Banks and Financial Institutions in the Union Budget 2020-21?Rs. 90,000 Crore

                                                                            Budget 2020-21 disinvestment target Rs. 2.1 lakh crore, including Rs. 90,000 crore from public sector banks and financial institutions.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which amount has been targeted in the Union Budget 2019-20 from the disinvestment of Public Sector Enterprises including AIR INDIA?Rs. 1,05,000 Crores

                                                                            Budget 2019-20 disinvestment target (including Air India) → Rs. 1,05,000 crore; actual realisation only Rs. 50,304 crore.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • As against the target of Rs. 10,000 crore from disinvestment by the Government of India for 2000-2001, there was a realisation of only:Rs. 1,829 crore

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The Railway Budget 2013-14 has approved to introduce a new hyper luxury class. It is to be called –Anubhuti

                                                                            Railway Budget 2013-14 → 'Anubhuti' hyper-luxury coaches in selected Rajdhani and Shatabdi trains.

                                                                            • Direct Tax Code in India is related to which of the following?Income Tax

                                                                            • Who had suggested the imposition of‘expenditure tax’ in India for the first time?Kaldor

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following situations best reflects ‘Indirect Transfers’often talked about in media recently with reference to India?A foreign company transfers shares and such shares derive their substantial value from assets located in India

                                                                            Indirect transfer → a foreign company transfers shares that derive substantial value from assets located in India (taxability of such gains).

                                                                            • Tax on sale of inherited property is:Capital Gain Tax

                                                                            Selling inherited property → capital gains tax; inheritance itself is not taxed in India (no inheritance tax).

                                                                            • Under which of the following circumstances may ‘capital gains’ arise?2 and 3 only

                                                                            Capital gain → rise in value of a capital asset above purchase price (property, painting); higher sales of a product is not a capital gain.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • At present, share of direct taxes in Gross National Product (GNP) in India is about –5%

                                                                            Direct taxes share of GNP at question time → about 5%; 2024-25 (B.E.): direct taxes 6.7%, indirect 4.9% of GDP.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The tax-GDP ratio in India is nearly:—

                                                                            Tax-GDP ratio (Centre + States) at question time → about 15%; Centre's gross tax-GDP: 11.5% in 2021-22, 11.7% in 2024-25 (B.E.). Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • Tax-GDP ratio in India in 2008-09 was estimated at:16.39 percent

                                                                            Tax-GDP ratio (Centre + States) in 2008-09 → 16.39% (about 16.5%).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • A decrease in tax to-GDP ratio of a country indicates which of the following?Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                            Falling tax-GDP ratio does not by itself show slowing growth or less equitable income distribution (book: neither statement).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • A redistribution of income in a country can be best brought about through:progressive taxation combined with progressive expenditure

                                                                            Best way to redistribute income → progressive taxation combined with progressive expenditure.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • What kind of Tax System is found in India?Degressive

                                                                            India's tax system → degressive: progressive up to a limit (slabs nil, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30%), then flat at the top.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Why the indirect taxes are termed regressive taxing mechanism?They are charged the same rates for all income groups

                                                                            Indirect taxes are regressive because all income groups pay the same rate on consumption.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which of the following statements are true for the Income Tax in India? I. It is a progressive tax II. It is a direct tax III. It is collected by the State Governments IV. It is a proportional tax Code:only I and II are correct

                                                                            Income tax in India → direct and progressive; levied and collected by the Union, not States; not proportional. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • According to the Union Budget 2016-17, a surcharge of 15% is payable if the income is:Above Rs. 1 Crore

                                                                            Budget 2016-17 → 15% surcharge on individual income above Rs. 1 crore.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • In the Central Government budget 2011-12, a new category of 'Very Senior Citizens' has been created for the purpose of Income Tax. This category covers the persons of age80 years and above

                                                                            Budget 2011-12 created 'Very Senior Citizen' category → 80 years and above; Senior Citizen = 60 to below 80 years.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • As per the Union Budget 2005-2006, the senior citizens have not to pay income tax upto an income of:Rs 1.50 lakh

                                                                            Budget 2005-06 → senior citizens exempt from income tax up to Rs. 1.50 lakh; now (old regime) Rs. 3.00 lakh senior, Rs. 5.00 lakh very senior.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which among the following is true for Central Sales Tax?Only (i) and (ii)

                                                                            Central Sales Tax → levied on inter-state trade and in Union Territories; SEZs exempt; now subsumed in GST (July 1, 2017).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Growth in Gross Tax Revenue in the case of Central Government was highest in the year:2016-17

                                                                            Highest growth in Centre's Gross Tax Revenue (2013-14 to 2016-17) → 2016-17 (17.9%); 2015-16 was 16.9%.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Two largest sources of tax revenue to the Central Government of India are:—

                                                                            Two largest Central tax sources at question time → Union excise and customs duties (option c); now Income Tax (19%), GST (18%), Corporation Tax (17%).

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • The contribution of customs and excise duties in the Central Government revenue in 1995-96 was:—

                                                                            Customs plus excise share of Centre's revenue receipts in 1995-96 (B.E.) → 45.01%; in 2024-25 interim customs 7.7%, excise 10.6%.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Consider the following important sources of tax revenue for the Central Government in India: I. Union Excise Duty II. Corporation Tax—

                                                                            Gross tax revenue order at question time: Corporation Tax > Income Tax > Union Excise > Service Tax (option c); now Income Tax > GST > Corporation Tax.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • Following are the estimated source of revenue of the Union Budget 2020-21. Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below:2 1 4 3

                                                                            Budget 2020-21 share of receipts: Corporation Tax 18%, Income Tax 17%, Customs 4%, Central Excise 7%.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Consider the following important sources of tax revenue for the Central Government:—

                                                                            Order at question time: corporation tax > other income tax > customs > Union excise (option b); 2024-25: taxes on income 30.18%, GST 27.87%, corporation tax 27.22%.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                            • Which one of the following has been the most important source of the tax revenue of the Union Government in 2009-10?Corporation Tax

                                                                            Most important Union tax source in 2009-10 → Corporation Tax. Must know

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                            • In the year 2013-14, largest source of tax revenue of the Union Government was:Corporation Tax

                                                                            Largest Union tax source 2013-14 → Corporation Tax; 2024-25 interim: Income Tax Rs. 1156000 crore, GST Rs. 1067650 crore, Corporation Tax Rs. 1042830 crore.

                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
