                                                                                                          56 facts · 65 questions · 9 Must know

                                                                                                          Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements: Statement-I: Interest income from the deposits in Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) distributed to their investors is exempted from tax, but the dividend is taxable. Statement-II: InvITs are recognized as borrowers under the 'Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002'. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

                                                                                                          InvITs: dividend and interest income fully taxable at investor's slab (Statement-I wrong); InvITs recognised as borrowers under SARFAESI Act, 2002 (Statement-II correct).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • What is the importance of the term ‘Interest Coverage Ratio’ of a firm in India?1 and 2 only

                                                                                                          Interest Coverage Ratio → how easily a firm pays interest on its debt; helps judge present and emerging lending risk; higher ICR is better.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Higher ICR means stronger debt-servicing ability; 'higher is worse' is the trap.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements regarding insolvency and bankruptcy:Only 4

                                                                                                          Insolvency → state of being unable to pay debts; bankruptcy → legal process (conclusion) liquidating assets; IBBI (1 October 2016) regulates under IBC, 2016.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Statements swap them: insolvency is the state, bankruptcy the legal outcome.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • What was the purpose of Inter-Creditor Agreement signed by Indian banks and financial institutions recently?To aim at faster resolution of stressed assets of Rs. 50 crore or more which are-under consortium lending.

                                                                                                          Inter-Creditor Agreement (Project Sashakt, Sunil Mehta Committee, 23 July 2018) → faster resolution of stressed assets of Rs. 50 crore+ under consortium lending; binding if 66% lenders agree.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following statements best describes the term ‘Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A)’, recently seen in the news?It is a scheme of RBI for reworking the financial structure of big corporate entities facing genuine difficulties.

                                                                                                          S4A (Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets) → RBI scheme, 13 June 2016, for deep restructuring of large corporate borrowers facing genuine difficulties.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements: The Reserve Bank of India’s recent directives relating to ‘Storage of Payment System Data’, popularly known as data diktat, command the payment system providers that1 only

                                                                                                          RBI 'Storage of Payment System Data' (6 April 2018) → all payment data stored only in India; no public-sector ownership rule; audit report goes to RBI, not CAG.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which committee has been constituted by the Government of India to boost cashless transaction?Neeraj Kumar Gupta Committee

                                                                                                          Committee to boost cashless transactions → Neeraj Kumar Gupta Committee (April 2016); after demonetisation, Amitabh Kant committee on cashless economy.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following best describes the term ‘Merchant Discount Rate’ sometimes seen in news?The charge to a merchant by a bank for accepting payments from his customers through the bank’s debit cards.

                                                                                                          Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) → fee a bank charges a merchant for accepting customers' card payments; compensates card issuer, PoS bank and gateways.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following links all the ATMs in India?National Payments Corporation of India

                                                                                                          All ATMs linked by National Financial Switch (NFS) → built by RBI's IDRBT in 2004; taken over by NPCI in December 2009.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                          NPCI (set up with RBI's help) → promotes financial inclusion; launched RuPay, a domestic card payment system, in 2012. Both statements correct.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following is a most likely consequence of implementing the ‘Unified Payments Interface (UPI)’?Mobile wallets will not be necessary for online payments.

                                                                                                          UPI (developed by NPCI) → instant inter-bank payments by mobile; likely result: mobile wallets not needed for online payments.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • With reference to Central Bank digital currencies, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                          CBDC → payments possible without US dollar or SWIFT; can carry programmed conditions like a spending time-frame (China's digital yuan expiry).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • With reference to ‘Bitcoins’, sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is / are correct?2 and 3 only

                                                                                                          Bitcoin (January 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto) → not tracked or issued by central banks; peer-to-peer between Bitcoin addresses; parties can stay anonymous.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • With reference to Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs), consider the following statements:1 and 2 only

                                                                                                          NFTs → unique cryptographic tokens on blockchain; digitally represent physical assets; cannot be exchanged at equivalency, so not a medium of commercial transactions.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Fungible cryptocurrencies swap one-for-one; non-fungible tokens cannot.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                          Broad Money (M3) = currency with public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with RBI + time deposits with banks. Must know

                                                                                                          Memory aid M3 = M1 + time deposits with banks.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Ifyou withdraw Rs. 1,00,000 in cash from your Demand Deposit Account at your bank, the immediate effect on aggregate money supply in the economy will be:to leave it unchanged

                                                                                                          Withdrawing Rs. 1,00,000 cash → demand deposits fall and currency with public rises equally; aggregate money supply (M3) unchanged.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following liquid assets:4-1-3-2

                                                                                                          Liquidity, highest to lowest → currency, demand deposits, savings deposits, time deposits.

                                                                                                          Memory aid C-D-S-T: Cash, Demand, Savings, Time, from instant to locked.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The money multiplier in an economy increases with which one of the following?Increase in the banking habit of the people

                                                                                                          Money multiplier rises with more banking habit (more deposits to lend); higher CRR or SLR lowers it; population rise need not raise it.

                                                                                                          Memory aid More deposits → bigger multiplier; higher reserve ratios → smaller.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Money multiplier in India is defined as:Base Money Reserve Money Reserve Money Base Money

                                                                                                          Money multiplier in India = Broad Money (M3) ÷ Reserve Money (high-powered money, M0 or R). Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • What is black money?It is an illegal income upon which income tax is not paid

                                                                                                          Black money → illegal income, or legal income hidden from tax, on which income tax is not paid; curbs include Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following effects of creation of black money in India has been the main cause of worry to the Government of India?Loss of revenue to the State Exchequer due to tax evasion

                                                                                                          Main worry from black money → loss of revenue to the State Exchequer through tax evasion, cutting funds for welfare schemes.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following was not the stated objective of demonetization in India?Increasing the growth rate of G.D.P.

                                                                                                          Demonetisation (8 November 2016, Rs. 500 and Rs. 1000 notes) → aims: curb black money and fake notes, less cash, more digital, wider tax base; not GDP growth.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Paper currency was first started in India in:1862

                                                                                                          Paper Currency Act 1861 gave Government monopoly of note issue; first Government paper currency issued in 1862.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Earlier notes came from private and Presidency banks (e.g. Bank of Hindustan, 1770-1832).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • When did the ‘Naya paisa’ introduced with the decimal system of coinage become, paisa?June 1, 1964

                                                                                                          Decimal coinage → 1 April 1957 ('Naya paisa'); 'Naya' dropped from 1 June 1964, becoming just 'paisa'. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following statements correctly describes the meaning of legal tender money?The money which a creditor is under compulsion to accept in settlement of his claims

                                                                                                          Legal tender money → money a creditor is legally bound to accept in settlement of claims (banknotes; coins within set limits).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The Reserve Bank of India has the power to print currency notes of Rupees upto:Rs. 10,000

                                                                                                          RBI can print notes up to Rs. 10,000 (Section 24, RBI Act 1934); Rs. 10,000 note issued 1938, demonetised 1946; reissued 1954, demonetised 1978.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Note issuing department of RBI should always possess the minimum gold stock of worth:Rs 115 crore

                                                                                                          Note issue → Minimum Reserve System (1956, amended 1957): gold plus foreign securities at least Rs. 200 crore, gold at least Rs. 115 crore. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Reserve Bank of India issues currency notes against which of the following?All of the above

                                                                                                          RBI notes are backed by gold coin and bullion, rupee coin, Government of India securities and foreign securities (Section 33, RBI Act 1934).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who is authorized to issue coins in India?Ministry of Finance

                                                                                                          Coins issued by Government of India (Ministry of Finance), circulated by RBI; four mints: Mumbai, Noida, Kolkata, Hyderabad. Must know

                                                                                                          Don't confuse RBI issues notes; Ministry of Finance issues coins.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Currency expansion can be best described –Higher prices

                                                                                                          Currency expansion → more money supply, lower value of money, higher prices.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • With reference to Indian economy, demand-pull inflation can be caused/increased by which of the following?1, 2 and 4 only

                                                                                                          Demand-pull inflation causes → expansionary policies, fiscal stimulus, higher purchasing power; not inflation-indexed wages or rising interest rates.

                                                                                                          Memory aid Demand-pull: more money and demand chasing the same output.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Due to inflation:Above (a) and (b)

                                                                                                          Inflation → prices of goods rise and value of money falls; exchange rate does not improve (rupee also weakens).

                                                                                                          Memory aid Inflation is a seesaw: prices go up, money's value goes down.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following is/are definite implication(s) of a fall in inflation rate:II only

                                                                                                          Fall in inflation rate → prices rising more slowly than before; it does not mean prices have fallen.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Falling inflation is not falling prices; falling prices is deflation.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Who amongst the following benefits most from inflation:Debtors

                                                                                                          Inflation benefits debtors, producers, traders, farmers; hurts creditors, moneylenders, pensioners, fixed-income groups, savings account holders.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Inflation is beneficial to which of the following section of economy?Debtors

                                                                                                          Inflation helps debtors (repay with cheaper money); creditors, fixed-interest bond investors, consumers and pensioners lose in real terms. Must know

                                                                                                          Memory aid Inflation is the borrower's friend, the lender's enemy.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • A zero rate of inflation obtains necessarily in a year where the annual rate of inflation:in every week of the year is zero

                                                                                                          Zero inflation for a year needs the annual inflation rate to be zero in every week of the year (inflation measured week by week).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Assertion (A): The rate of inflation in India has come down in the last three years.A is true, but R is false

                                                                                                          Inflation fell from 10.9% (1994-95) to 4.8% (1997-98): A true; foreign investment rose only slightly (4807 to 5353 million US $): R false.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following statements is an appropriate description of deflation?It is a persistent fall in the general price level of goods and services.

                                                                                                          Deflation → persistent fall in general price level of goods and services; opposite of inflation.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse A fall in the rate of inflation is not deflation.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • A rapid increase in the rate of inflation is sometimes attributed to the 'base effect'. What is 'base effect'?It is the impact of the price levels of previous year on the calculation of inflation rate

                                                                                                          Base effect → impact of previous year's price level on current inflation rate; a low base shows a high rate.

                                                                                                          Memory aid Low base → high inflation rate; high base → low rate.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which one of the following governmental steps has proved relatively effective in controlling the double digit rate of inflation in the Indian economy in the recent years?Containing budgetary deficit and unproductive expenditure

                                                                                                          Double-digit inflation curbed by containing budgetary deficit and unproductive expenditure; revenue deficit fell from 3.3% of GDP (1990-91) to 2.5% (1992-93).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following factors could potentially contribute to stagflation in the Indian Economy?1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                                                          Stagflation → high inflation, slow growth, high unemployment; causes: spending-led inflation, falling industrial output, weak demand, currency appreciation hurting exports.

                                                                                                          Memory aid Stagflation = stagnation + inflation.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Given below are two statements one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R):Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of(A)

                                                                                                          Bottleneck inflation → supply falls sharply while demand stays same, due to supply bottlenecks or inefficient distribution; tough for government (A, R true; R explains A).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements regarding inflation: Statement (A): Headline inflation refers to the rate of change in the Consumer Price Index Number, a measure of the average price of a standard basket of goods and services consumed by a typical family. Statement (B): Core inflation measures the change in average consumer prices after excluding from the Consumer Price Index certain items of volatile prices such as food and fuel.Both (A) and (B) are correct.

                                                                                                          Headline inflation → change in CPI for a typical household basket; core inflation → CPI change excluding volatile food and fuel. Both correct.

                                                                                                          Memory aid Core = headline minus the shaky items (food and fuel).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Core inflation is defined as:Headline inflation excluding both food inflation and fuel inflation.

                                                                                                          Core inflation = headline inflation excluding both food and fuel inflation; shows the long-run price trend.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Tick mark which is incorrect about inflation:The inflation rate in India is calculated on the basis of the wholesale price index.

                                                                                                          Inflation now measured by CPI (Combined); WPI was main index till April 2014, so 'calculated on WPI' is now incorrect.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • On what basis is the inflation rate measured in India?All of the above

                                                                                                          Inflation in India measured by CPI, WPI and Labour Cost of Living Index; RBI's key measure now CPI (Combined).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The most common measure of estimating inflation in India is:Consumer Price Index

                                                                                                          Headline inflation → CPI (Combined), base 2012 = 100; RBI adopted it as key measure in April 2014, replacing WPI. Must know

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Old answers say WPI; since April 2014 the answer is CPI-Combined.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • In India, inflation is measured by the:Wholesale Price Index Number

                                                                                                          At question time → inflation in India measured by Wholesale Price Index (WPI); later replaced by CPI (Combined).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following fixed the four percent inflation target in India with tolerance level of + / – 2 percent for the period 2016 to 2021?Government of India

                                                                                                          Inflation target (4% CPI, ±2%, 5 August 2016 to 31 March 2021) set by Government of India with RBI, under RBI Act amended May 2016.

                                                                                                          Memory aid 4 ± 2: the band runs from 2 to 6 percent.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The annual rate of inflation in India during the 1991 calendar year based on the monthly average of the Wholesale Price Index was:12.7

                                                                                                          Annual inflation in 1991 (calendar year, monthly average WPI) → about 12.7%.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:1 and 2 only

                                                                                                          Food weight higher in CPI (45.9%) than WPI (24.4%); WPI excludes services, CPI includes them; RBI uses CPI (Combined), not WPI, since April 1, 2014.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements with respect to Consumer Price Index and select the correct answer from the codes given below:1 and 3

                                                                                                          CPI → covers goods and services; RBI uses CPI (Combined) for monetary policy; compiled by NSO and Labour Bureau, not Office of Economic Adviser.

                                                                                                          Don't confuse Office of Economic Adviser (Commerce Ministry) compiles WPI, not CPI.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Consider the following consumer price index: I. Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers. II. Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers. III. Consumer Price Index for Rural Workers. IV. Consumer Price Index for Urban Non-Manual Employees. In the given indexes, which is/are compiled by Central Statistics Office (CSO)?—

                                                                                                          CPI-IW, CPI-AL, CPI-RL → Labour Bureau; CPI-UNME → CSO (discontinued April 2008); CPI-Urban, Rural, Combined → NSO.

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The base of Consumer Price Index for industrial workers has been shifted from 1982 to:2001

                                                                                                          CPI-IW base years → 1960 → 1982 (from 1988) → 2001 (from 2006) → 2016 (from September 2020); compiled by Labour Bureau. Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • Which of the following price index is used to compensate the wages of Central Government employees?Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers

                                                                                                          Wage compensation (dearness allowance) of Central Government employees → Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW).

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                          • The basis of determining dearness allowances to employees of India is:Consumer Price Index

                                                                                                          Dearness allowance of employees fixed using Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW). Must know

                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following Institution/Office bring out the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) data in India?The Ministry of Commerce and Industry

                                                                                                                WPI compiled by Office of Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry; current base year 2011-12.

                                                                                                                Memory aid Wholesale is trade, so WPI sits with the Commerce Ministry.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference to the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), consider the following statements:2 and 3

                                                                                                                WPI base 1993-94 = 100 came in April 2000, not 1998; it cut primary articles' weight, raised electricity's. Base 2011-12: manufactured 64.23%, primary 22.62%, fuel 13.15%. Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The new WPI series was introduced on:14 September, 2010

                                                                                                                WPI with base 2004-05 → released 14 September 2010; base revised to 2011-12 on 12 May 2017 (effective April 2017). Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The new series of Wholesale Price Index (WPI) released by the Government of India is with reference to the base prices of:1993-94

                                                                                                                WPI base years → 1981-82, then 1993-94 (question period), now 2011-12.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • In October 2009, a decision has been taken that the base year of Wholesale Price Index (WPI) has been shifted from 1993-94 to:2004-2005

                                                                                                                CCEA (19 October 2009) shifted WPI base from 1993-94 to 2004-05 with monthly release; new series from September 2010 (Abhijit Sen Committee).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference to India, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                WPI now released monthly only (all groups since February 2012; weekly release cut from October 2009); WPI gives less weight to food than CPI-IW.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The current price index (base 1960) is nearly 330. This means that:weighted mean of prices of certain items has increased 3.3 times

                                                                                                                Price index 330 (base 1960 = 100) → weighted mean of prices of selected items rose 3.3 times, not every item.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Producer Price Index measures:the average change in the prices of produced goods and services.

                                                                                                                Producer Price Index → average change in prices producers receive; output PPI (goods leaving production) and input PPI (goods entering production).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Assertion (a): Cost push inflation is caused by shift in aggregate supply curve.Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A).

                                                                                                                Cost-push inflation → leftward shift (decrease) of aggregate supply curve, caused by rise in wages (A and R true, R explains A).

                                                                                                                Memory aid Cost-push: costs (wages) push prices up from the supply side.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements: Statement-I: In the post-pandemic recent past, many Central Banks worldwide had carried out interest rate hikes. Statement-II: Central Banks generally assume that they have the ability to counteract the rising consumer prices via monetary policy means. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I

                                                                                                                Post-pandemic, central banks hiked interest rates to curb inflation, assuming monetary policy can counter rising prices (both true; II explains I); World Bank (2022) warned of recession.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which one of the following is NOT a method to control inflation?Reducing the rate of interest

                                                                                                                Reducing interest rate is expansionary, not anti-inflation; inflation is controlled by raising interest rates, credit control, cutting money supply, controlling demand, rationing.

                                                                                                                Memory aid To cool prices, raise rates (contractionary policy).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference to inflation in India, which of the following statements is correct?Decreased money circulation helps in controlling the inflation.

                                                                                                                Decreased money circulation (liquidity) helps control inflation; RBI uses monetary policy for this, so it is not only the Government's job.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • India has experienced persistent and high food inflation in the recent past. What could be the reasons?2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                Food inflation reasons → changed consumption patterns with rising incomes; structural constraints in food supply chain. Foodgrain area had not fallen steadily by 30%.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Assertion (A): Between October 2009 and February 2010 the inflation rate in India was negative.Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of(A).

                                                                                                                Book: global petrol price fell from 140 $ to 30 $ a barrel, so India's inflation was negative from October 2009 to February 2010 (A, R true; R explains A).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • In India, the first Bank of limited liability managed by Indians and founded in 1881 was:Oudh Commercial Bank

                                                                                                                Oudh Commercial Bank (Faizabad, 1881) → first limited-liability bank with all-Indian board; Punjab National Bank (founded 1894, Lahore) → first Swadeshi bank.

                                                                                                                Don't confuse First Indian-managed limited bank → Oudh Commercial; first Swadeshi bank → PNB.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference to India, consider the following:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                Financial inclusion steps → bank nationalisation, Regional Rural Banks, village adoption by bank branches (all three); also Lead Bank Scheme.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • In the context of independent India’s economy, which one of the following was the earliest event to take place?Enactment of Banking Regulation Act

                                                                                                                Earliest → Banking Regulation Act (10 March 1949); then First Plan (1951), SBI (July 1955), life insurance nationalised (1956), general insurance (1972). Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The Government of India has nationalized 14 banks of the country in:July, 1969

                                                                                                                Bank nationalisation → 14 major banks (assets above Rs. 50 crore) in July 1969; six more on 15 April 1980. Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order with the help of code given below: I. First phase of Bank Nationalization II. Second phase of Bank Nationalization III. Establishment of Regional Rural Banks IV. Establishment of NABARD Code:I, III, II, IV

                                                                                                                Chronology → first bank nationalisation (1969) → Regional Rural Banks (1975) → second nationalisation (1980) → NABARD (1982).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Arrange the following in chronological order:3, 2, 4, 1

                                                                                                                Nationalisation order → RBI (1949) → SBI (1955) → LIC (1956) → 14 major banks (1969).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                Gorewala Committee (All-India Rural Credit Survey) → SBI formed by merging Imperial Bank of India with State-associated banks; six commercial banks nationalised on April 15, 1980.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The number of public sector banks in India (excluding State Bank of India Group) is presently:—

                                                                                                                Public sector banks excluding SBI Group → 20 at question time; after mergers (April 1, 2020), now 12 public sector banks including SBI.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The recent amalgamation of public sector banks in India is aimed at multiple gains.1, 2, 3 and 4 all

                                                                                                                PSB amalgamation (announced August 2019; 10 banks into 4 from April 1, 2020; 12 PSBs left) → economies of scale, capital access, wider reach, global-size banks.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference tothe governance ofpublic sector banking in India,consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                Capital infusion into PSBs (Rs. 1,18,724 crore, 2008-09 to 2016-17) did not rise steadily; five SBI Associate Banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into SBI (2017).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • With reference to ‘EASE-Index’, which of the following statements is/are correct?Only 1

                                                                                                                EASE Index (Enhanced Access and Service Excellence) → measures performance of public sector banks; not ease of doing business for MSMEs.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Consider the following statements: The functions of commercial banks in India includeBoth 1 and 2

                                                                                                                Commercial bank functions include buying and selling shares and securities for customers, and acting as executors and trustees of wills.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following is the commercial bank of public sector?Indian Overseas Bank

                                                                                                                Public sector bank → Government holds at least 51% stake; e.g. Indian Overseas Bank, SBI, PNB; now 12 PSBs including SBI.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following is a private bank?Bank of Punjab

                                                                                                                Bank of Punjab was a private bank; merged with Centurion Bank in 2005 to form Centurion Bank of Punjab.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which one of the following is not a nationalized bank?ICICI Bank

                                                                                                                ICICI Bank is private, not nationalised; ICICI formed 1955 (World Bank initiative) as development financial institution; ICICI Bank incorporated 1994.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which one of the following Indian Banks is not a nationalized bank?ICICI Bank

                                                                                                                ICICI Bank is not nationalised; Dena and Vijaya Banks merged into Bank of Baroda, Corporation Bank into Union Bank of India.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • When was the State Bank of India established?1955

                                                                                                                State Bank of India → 1 July 1955, by nationalising Imperial Bank of India (RBI took 60% stake).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The largest commercial bank of India is:State Bank of India

                                                                                                                Largest commercial bank in India → State Bank of India (HQ Mumbai; 22,406 branches, 65,627 ATMs/CRMs as on 31 March 2023). Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following commercial banks of India comes in top 100 global banks?SBI; HDFC Bank

                                                                                                                Only Indian bank in global top 100 (S & P, April 2020) → SBI (55th); April 2024: SBI 47th, HDFC Bank new entrant at 74th.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which one of the following bank has formed ‘farmers clubs’ to reach out to the farmers easily?State Bank of India

                                                                                                                SBI with NABARD formed 'Farmers Club' (Kishan club) in Uttar Pradesh to reach farmers and raise their bargaining power. Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Since April, 2011, the SBI’s Chairman has been:Pratip Chaudhuri

                                                                                                                SBI Chairman from 7 April 2011 → Pratip Chaudhuri (till 30 September 2013); Dinesh Kumar Khara from October 2020; Challa Sreenivasulu Setty selected 29 June 2024. Must know

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The Chairman of public sector banks are selected by the:Banks Board Bureau

                                                                                                                PSB chairmen selected by Banks Board Bureau (from April 01, 2016), replaced by Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) from 1 July 2022.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following banks has started the ‘Simply Click’ credit card scheme?S.B.I.

                                                                                                                'Simply Click' credit card → SBI (15 September 2015) with seven e-commerce partners like Amazon India, BookMyShow, Ola Cabs.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which bank became the first bank to open its branch in China?State Bank of India

                                                                                                                First Indian bank to open a branch in China → State Bank of India (2006). Must know

                                                                                                                Don't confuse First Indian private bank branch in China → Axis Bank (Shanghai).

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which of the following Private Bank for the first time did set up its branch in China?Axis Bank

                                                                                                                First Indian private bank branch in China → Axis Bank, Shanghai (January 2014), after Chinese regulator's nod in September 2013.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • Which Indian commercial bank started the first ever moving ATM Services?ICICI

                                                                                                                First moving ATM in India → ICICI (private bank), Mumbai, 12 December 2002.

                                                                                                                • Which private sector bank has launched 'e-Kisaan Dhan' app for farmers?HDFC Bank

                                                                                                                'e-Kisaan Dhan' app for farmers → HDFC Bank (June 2020): mandi prices, farming news, weather, seed information plus banking services.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                • The Commercial Bank which has been merged with the Punjab National Bank is:New Bank of India; Oriental Bank of Commerce

                                                                                                                New Bank of India merged with Punjab National Bank (1993); Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India merged into PNB from 1 April 2020.

                                                                                                                Bank of Rajasthan merged with ICICI Bank on 13 August 2010.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                Bank of Karad → closed after the securities scam; merged with Bank of India in 1994.

                                                                                                                Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
