                                                                                                                      • The percentage of rural branches of all kinds of private, public sector commercial Banks including Regional Rural Banks as on 30.06.2012, according to RBI, was approximately:37%

                                                                                                                      Rural branches of all commercial banks including RRBs → about 37% (30 June 2012); about 36% at end-March 2023.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The 'Lead Bank' Scheme was launched in:December, 1969

                                                                                                                      Lead Bank Scheme → RBI, December 1969, from Gadgil Study Group and Nariman Committee; a designated bank leads credit development in each district. Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Service Area Approach was implemented under the purview of:Lead Bank Scheme

                                                                                                                      Service Area Approach (April 1989) → under Lead Bank Scheme; each rural or semi-urban branch served 15 to 25 villages.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • District Credit Planning is done:Under the Lead bank

                                                                                                                      District credit planning → done under the district's Lead Bank.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following banks operates mainly in relation to small industries?SIDBI

                                                                                                                      SIDBI → set up 2 April 1990 by Act of Parliament; HQ Lucknow; principal institution for financing and developing MSME (small industries). Must know

                                                                                                                      Memory aid SIDBI's head office is in Lucknow, UP.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following pairs:2 only

                                                                                                                      SIDBI head office → Lucknow (not Mumbai); Allahabad Bank → Kolkata (merged with Indian Bank, 2020); Indian Overseas Bank → Chennai.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid SIDBI serves MSMEs from UP's capital, Lucknow.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • ‘Financial Inclusion’ can be encouraged:by all of the above.

                                                                                                                      Financial inclusion → banking for all, incl. zero or minimum balance accounts and financial services to low-income groups (all options).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not the objective offinancial inclusion?Shrinking of banking infrastructure.

                                                                                                                      Financial inclusion aims → services to the poor, growth of weaker sections, finance in rural areas, expanding banking infrastructure; shrinking it is not an aim.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is a hindrance in the process of financial inclusion?All of the above

                                                                                                                      Hindrances to financial inclusion → low income, illiteracy and lack of bank branches (all three).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who among the following was the Chairman of the ‘Committee on Financial Inclusion’ constituted in January 2005?C. Rangarajan

                                                                                                                      Committee on Financial Inclusion → Dr. C. Rangarajan (constituted June 26, 2006; final report January 4, 2008). Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • What is the purpose of setting up of Small Finance Banks (SFBs) in India?1 and 2 only

                                                                                                                      Small Finance Banks (RBI guidelines November 2014) → savings vehicles; credit to small businesses, small and marginal farmers, micro and small industries; no young-entrepreneur aim.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The establishment of‘Payment Banks’ is being allowed in India to promote financial inclusion. Which of the following statements is / are correct in this context?1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                      Payments Banks → resident-owned mobile companies and supermarket chains can promote; can issue ATM/debit cards, not credit cards; cannot lend.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid Payments Bank takes deposits but never lends.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • RBI has cleared the resolution to start Payment Banks in India for improving Financial Inclusion. Following committee had recommended the creation of Payment Banks:Nachiket Mor

                                                                                                                      Payments Banks recommended by Nachiket Mor Committee (formed 23 September 2013; report 7 January 2014) on financial services for small businesses and low-income households.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • What is ‘Shadow Banking’?Financial transactions and other activities of non-banking financial intermediary

                                                                                                                      Shadow banking → bank-like lending by lightly regulated non-banking financial intermediaries; term coined by Paul McCulley (2007).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The difference between a bank and a Non-Banking Financial Institution (NBFI) is that:a bank indulges in a number of activities relating to finance with a range of customers, while an NBFI is mainly concerned with the term loan needs of large enterprises

                                                                                                                      Bank → wide range of financial activities for many customers; NBFI (no full banking licence) → mainly term-loan needs of large companies.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • With reference to the Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) in India, consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                      NBFCs can acquire government securities (statement 1 false) but cannot accept demand deposits like savings accounts or issue cheques on themselves (statement 2 true).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • On which date, the Ombudsman Scheme for the Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFC), 2018 was effectively introduced by Reserve Bank of India?23 February, 2018

                                                                                                                      Ombudsman Scheme for NBFCs, 2018 → from February 23, 2018 under Section 45 L, RBI Act 1934; free complaint redressal for NBFC customers.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Microfinance is the provision of financial services to people of low-income groups. This includes both the consumers and the self-employed. The service/services rendered under microfinance is/are:1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                                                                      Microfinance → basic financial services for poor and low-income households: credit, savings, insurance, fund (cash) transfers, leasing (all four given).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • RBI had set up a committee to study and give suggestions on the microfinance sector. Its Chairman was:Y.H. Malegam

                                                                                                                      RBI sub-committee on microfinance → Y.H. Malegam (formed October 15, 2010); recommended a separate NBFC-MFI category.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • On which of the following recommendations, the Microfinance Institutions were set up in 2011?Malegam Committee

                                                                                                                      Malegam Committee recommendation → new NBFC category: NBFC-Microfinance Institution (NBFC-MFI), 2011.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • ‘Gullak Bachcha Bank’ is a bank based in:Patna

                                                                                                                      'Gullak Bachcha Bank' → run by children at Bal Bhavan-Kilkari, Patna; opened November 14, 2009 by Nitish Kumar for thrift education.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which among the following is an asset for a Commercial Bank?Credit to farmers

                                                                                                                      Bank assets → cash, money at call, investments, loans and advances (e.g. credit to farmers); deposits and RBI borrowings are liabilities.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid Bank owes deposits (liability); bank is owed loans (asset).

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Deposits are a bank's liabilities; loans are its assets.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is not included in the assets of a commercial bank in India?Deposits

                                                                                                                      Deposits are a liability (must be repaid), not an asset; bank assets → cash and RBI balances, money at call and short notice, investments, advances.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is the most important component of the liabilities of commercial banks in India?Time deposits

                                                                                                                      Most important liability of commercial banks → time deposits; then savings and demand deposits.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Non-performing assets in commercial banks mean:Loans in which interest or principal amount is not recovered

                                                                                                                      Non-performing asset (NPA) → loan whose interest or principal is overdue for more than 90 days.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid NPA clock = 90 days.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Priority sector lending by banks in India constitutes the lending to:All of the above

                                                                                                                      Priority sector lending (at least 40% of bank credit) → agriculture, MSMEs, weaker sections, education, housing, export credit, renewable energy.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Short Term Loans is of:Maximum 15 months

                                                                                                                      Loan terms → short-term up to 1 year (or 15 months); medium-term up to 3 (or 5) years; long-term beyond that.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Why is the offering of ‘teaser loans’ by commercial banks a cause of economic concern?1 only

                                                                                                                      Teaser loans → housing loans with ultra-low initial fixed rate, then market rates; seen as subprime lending with future default risk; not for new entrepreneurs.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                      Internal debt includes market borrowings, Treasury bills and special securities issued to RBI; public debt = internal + external, contracted against Consolidated Fund of India.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • In the context of the Indian economy, non-financial debt includes which of the following?1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                      Non-financial debt → credit instruments of governments, households, businesses outside financial sector: housing loans, credit card dues, treasury bills (all three).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The term ‘Core Banking Solutions’ is sometimes seen in the news. Which of the following statements best describes / describe this term?1 only

                                                                                                                      Core Banking Solutions → networked branches let customers operate accounts from any branch; not RBI control or takeover of NPA-laden banks.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Government of India has recently acquired the RBI’s stake in:State Bank of India

                                                                                                                      June 2007 → Government of India acquired RBI's 59.7% stake in State Bank of India.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following banks is under the control of the Reserve Bank of India?—

                                                                                                                      NABARD was under RBI control at question time; RBI divested NABARD (2010, 2019) and NHB (2019) stakes; Government now holds 100% of both.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The National Housing Bank was set up in India as a wholly-owned subsidiary of which one of the following?Reserve Bank of India

                                                                                                                      National Housing Bank (July 9, 1988, NHB Act 1987) → apex housing finance body, wholly owned by RBI till March 19, 2019; now 100% Government.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • ‘Basel IIIAccord’ or simply ‘Basel III’, often seen in the news, seeks to:improve banking sector’s ability to deal with financial and economic stress and improve risk management.

                                                                                                                      Basel III → Basel Committee measures after 2007-09 crisis to strengthen bank regulation, supervision, risk management and ability to handle stress.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid Basel I 1988, Basel II 2004, then Basel III after the crisis.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Basel II relates to which one of the following?International standards for measuring the adequacy of a bank's capital

                                                                                                                      Basel II (June 2004) → international bank capital adequacy standards; three pillars: minimum capital, supervisory review, market discipline (disclosure).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                                                      CAR (CRAR) → bank capital vs risk-weighted assets, to absorb losses; fixed by central banks/regulators, not each bank; Basel III 8%; RBI 9% (11.5% with buffer).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • With reference to Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Insurance Corporation, which of the following statements is/are correct?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                      DICGC → wholly owned RBI subsidiary (Act of 1961); insures each depositor up to Rs. 5 lakh per bank (from 4 February 2020; earlier Rs. 1 lakh).

                                                                                                                      Memory aid Deposit cover went from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh in 2020.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • In India, the interest rate on savings accounts in all the Nationalized Commercial Banks is fixed by:None of the above

                                                                                                                      Savings account interest rates → deregulated by RBI in October 2011; now fixed by banks themselves, not Finance Ministry or IBA.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • What is / are the purpose / purposes of the ‘Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate’ (MCLR) announced by RBI?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                      MCLR (from April 1, 2016) → internal minimum lending rate; brings transparency in loan pricing and fair rates for borrowers and banks.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements related to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: I. It is the apex bank. II. It regulates the money supply. III. It provides loan to business families. IV. It monitors the work of NABARD. Codes:I, II and IV

                                                                                                                      RBI → apex bank, regulates money supply, monitors NABARD; does not lend to business families.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements regarding Reserve Bank of India:1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                                                                      RBI (April 1, 1935) → banker to Government, frames monetary policy, Government's agent for IMF membership, manages Government borrowing.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Who is the Fiscal agent and advisor to Government in monetary and financial matters?R.B.I.

                                                                                                                      Fiscal agent and adviser to Government on monetary and financial matters → RBI (RBI Act, 1934).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                      RBI manages both Central securities and State Development Loans (by agreement with States); only Centre issues T-bills, States issue only bonds; T-bills issued at discount, redeemed at face value.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid T-bill: bought at a discount, paid back at full face value.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Treasury bills are sold in India by:Reserve Bank of India

                                                                                                                      Treasury bills → short-term Government of India debt sold by RBI through auction; first issued 1917; tenors 91, 182, 364 days.

                                                                                                                      Memory aid T-bill tenors are about three, six and twelve months.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • With reference to India, consider the following statements:1 and 2

                                                                                                                      Retail investors can buy T-bills and G-Secs in primary market (RBI Retail Direct, November 12, 2021); NDS-OM is RBI's G-Sec trading platform; CDSL promoted by BSE, not RBI.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Reserve Bank of India does not carries out the transactions of which State Government?—

                                                                                                                      RBI is banker to all State Governments (and UTs Puducherry, Jammu & Kashmir) under Section 21A, RBI Act 1934, except Sikkim (limited debt agreement).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • The Reserve Bank of India regulates the commercial banks in matters of:1, 2, 3 and 4

                                                                                                                      RBI regulates banks' liquidity of assets (Repo, SLR, CRR), branch expansion (rural-urban ratio), bank mergers (with Competition Commission) and winding-up (all four).

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following statements is not correct?RBI was established in 1949.

                                                                                                                      RBI → established April 1, 1935 (RBI Act 1934), not 1949; nationalised 1949; HQ Kolkata, moved to Mumbai 1937; Governments' banker, forex custodian. Must know

                                                                                                                      Don't confuse 1935 = founded; 1949 = nationalised. Don't swap them.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • In India, the Central Bank's function as the 'lender of last resort' usually refers to which of the following?2 only

                                                                                                                      Lender of last resort → RBI gives emergency liquidity to solvent banks in temporary crisis; not lending to industry or financing budget deficits.

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                      • Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the Reserve Bank of India?It issues all types of currency notes.

                                                                                                                      RBI does not issue all notes: one rupee note issued by Government of India, signed by Finance Secretary; other notes signed by RBI Governor. Must know

                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            Hour 22 →

                                                                                                                            Hour 22 of 72 · Learn

                                                                                                                            Money and Banking · part 4 of 7

                                                                                                                            43 facts · 55 questions · 9 Must know

                                                                                                                            Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following is not a function of Reserve Bank of India?Credit creation

                                                                                                                            Credit creation → function of commercial banks, not RBI; RBI controls credit, frames monetary policy, is apex of scheduled banks.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is not a function of the Reserve Bank of India?Regulation of foreign trade

                                                                                                                            Foreign trade regulated by Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not RBI; RBI issues currency, banks for banks and government, controls credit, manages forex.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) acts as a bankers’ bank. This would imply which of the following?1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                            RBI as bankers' bank → banks keep deposits with RBI; RBI lends to them in need and advises on monetary matters. RBI is India's central bank (1935).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Monetary Policy is:Complementary to fiscal policy

                                                                                                                            Monetary policy complements fiscal policy; it acts indirectly through credit and money supply, fiscal policy acts directly on demand.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following is not an objective of Monetary Policy?Equitable Distribution of Income and Assets

                                                                                                                            Monetary policy objectives → price stability, economic stability, exchange rate stability; equitable distribution of income and assets is not one.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Who formulates the monetary policy in India?—

                                                                                                                            Monetary policy → formulated by RBI till 2016; now Monetary Policy Committee sets policy rate, aided by RBI's Monetary Policy Department; RBI keeps price stability. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?1 only

                                                                                                                            Monetary Policy Committee → decides RBI benchmark rates; six members (three RBI incl. Governor, three Government nominees for four years); RBI Governor chairs.

                                                                                                                            Memory aid MPC = three RBI + three Government = six; RBI Governor holds the chair.

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse MPC has six members, not 12; chaired by RBI Governor, not Finance Minister.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In India ‘Money and Credit’ is controlled by the:Reserve Bank of India

                                                                                                                            'Money and Credit' in India controlled by RBI, using quantitative and qualitative measures.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following is not an instrument of selective credit control in India?Variable reserve ratios

                                                                                                                            Selective (qualitative) control → margin requirements, consumer credit regulation, credit rationing, moral suasion; quantitative → Bank Rate, OMO (securities sale), Repo, variable CRR/SLR. Must know

                                                                                                                            Memory aid Quantitative = how much credit (rates, ratios, OMO); qualitative = where credit goes (margins, rationing).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • With reference to Indian economy, consider the following:1 and 2

                                                                                                                            Monetary policy tools → Bank Rate, open market operations; public debt and public revenue belong to fiscal policy.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Open market operations of Reserve Bank of India refer to:trading in securities

                                                                                                                            Open market operations → RBI buys government securities and T-bills to raise money supply, sells them to cut it. Must know

                                                                                                                            Memory aid OMO: Buy = boost money supply; Sell = squeeze it.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Variable reserve rates and open market operations are the means of:Monentary Policy

                                                                                                                            Variable reserve ratios and open market operations → tools of RBI's monetary policy to regulate credit and money supply.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following activities of the Reserve Bank of India is considered to be part of 'sterilization'?Conducting 'Open Market Operations'

                                                                                                                            Sterilisation → RBI absorbs fresh money (e.g. capital inflows) to curb inflation or currency appreciation, mainly via open market operations (selling T-bills).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A)

                                                                                                                            Operation Twist → RBI buys long-term and sells short-term securities together to lower long-term rates and promote long-term investment (US Fed first, 1961).

                                                                                                                            Memory aid Twist: buy long, sell short at the same time.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following measures would result in an increase in the money supply in the economy?1 and 3

                                                                                                                            Money supply rises when Central Bank buys government securities from public or Government borrows from it; deposits in banks and securities sales reduce it.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Consider the following measures that RBI uses to control inflation in the economy.Only 1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                            RBI fights inflation by raising Bank Rate, Repo, CRR and SLR and selling government securities; buying securities would add money.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                            High inflation → RBI sells (not buys) government securities; rupee falling fast → RBI sells dollars; lower US/EU rates bring inflows → RBI buys dollars.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In the context of Indian economy, which of the following is/are the purpose / purposes of ‘Statutary Reserve Requirements’?1 only

                                                                                                                            Statutory Reserve Requirement → minimum share of deposits kept as cash, gold or securities; lets Central Bank control advances (credit growth) banks create.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following terms indicates a mechanism used by commercial banks for providing credit to the government?Statutory Liquidity Ratio

                                                                                                                            SLR → way commercial banks provide credit to Government: banks hold reserves mostly in government securities (Section 24 (2A), Banking Regulation Act 1949).

                                                                                                                            Don't confuse CRR is cash kept with RBI (no interest); SLR is liquid assets kept by banks themselves.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • When the Reserve Bank of India reduces the Statutory Liquidity Ratio by 50 basis points, which of the following is likely to happen?Scheduled Commercial banks may cut their lending rates.

                                                                                                                            SLR cut by 50 basis points → banks get more lendable funds and may cut lending rates; SLR = share of deposits kept as cash, gold, securities. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is not determined by Reserve bank of India?P.L.R.

                                                                                                                            Prime Lending Rate (PLR) → set by commercial banks for best corporate borrowers, not by RBI; RBI fixes Bank Rate, CRR, SLR.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The terms ‘Marginal Standing Facility Rate’ and ‘Net Demand and Time Liabilities’, sometimes appearing in news, are used in relation to:banking operations

                                                                                                                            MSF → banks borrow overnight from RBI by dipping into SLR at penal rate; Bank Rate aligned with MSF rate. NDTL → banks' net demand and time liabilities.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • If the RBI decides to adopt an expansionist monetary policy, which of the following would it not do?2 only

                                                                                                                            Expansionary monetary policy → cut SLR, Bank Rate and Repo Rate; RBI would not raise Marginal Standing Facility rate (makes borrowing costlier).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • If the interest rate is decreased in an economy, it will:increase the investment expenditure in the economy

                                                                                                                            Lower interest rate → borrowing easier, so investment (and consumption) expenditure rises.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Financial sector reforms in India consist of:All of the above

                                                                                                                            Financial sector reforms → lower CRR and SLR, deregulated interest rates, private entry into banking and insurance, NPA reforms (all options).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Since the economic reforms were launched in India, which one of the following statements is true for Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) of the commercial banks:Both SLR and CRR have been reduced

                                                                                                                            After reforms (Narsimham Committee) → SLR cut from 38.5% (1991) to 25% (1997); CRR from 13% (1996) to 9% (1999); now CRR 4.50%, SLR 18%.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The mandatory proportion ofthetotaldeposits and reserves of the commercial banks deposited with the Reserve Bank of India is called:Cash Reserve Ratio

                                                                                                                            Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) → mandatory share of banks' deposits kept as cash with RBI. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • An increase in CRR by the Reserve Bank OfIndia results in:reduction in liquidity in the economy

                                                                                                                            Higher CRR → fewer loanable funds → less liquidity (money supply) in the economy.

                                                                                                                            Memory aid CRR up → lending down.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Lowering the Cash Reserve Ratio, it will have the following impact on the economy: I. Banks will have higher leverage to liquidity. II. The economy may see increased investment. III. Supply of currency in the economy may broaden. IV. Real investment rate may decline. Select the correct code:None of the above / More than one of the above

                                                                                                                            Lower CRR → more bank liquidity, more investment, wider money supply, more credit creation (I, II, III true); real investment rate does not decline (IV false).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • When the Reserve Bank of India announces an increase of the Cash Reserve Ratio, what does it mean?The commercial banks will have less money to lend

                                                                                                                            Higher CRR → banks deposit more with RBI and have less money to lend; credit creation and money supply fall, curbing inflation. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Repo Rate comes under purview of:Monetary Policy

                                                                                                                            Repo Rate → key monetary policy rate at which RBI lends short-term money to banks; a monetary (not fiscal) policy tool.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • 'Repurchase Option’ is used:None of the above

                                                                                                                            Repo (Repurchase Option) → used by RBI to regulate money supply and inflation, not to handle rupee sell-off in exchange market. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends to Commercial banks in the short term to maintain liquidity is known as:Repo Rate

                                                                                                                            Repo Rate → rate at which RBI lends short-term (overnight) funds to commercial banks against government securities under LAF. Must know

                                                                                                                            Memory aid Repo: RBI gives money; Reverse Repo: RBI takes money.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The rate at which banks lend to Reserve Bank of India is known as:Reverse Repo Rate

                                                                                                                            Reverse Repo Rate → rate at which banks lend to RBI (RBI borrows), absorbing surplus money overnight against government securities.

                                                                                                                            Memory aid Repo: RBI gives money; Reverse Repo: RBI takes money.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                                                            Repo rate → rate at which RBI lends to banks (banks borrow from RBI); reverse repo → RBI borrows. Gini coefficient 1 = perfect inequality; 0 = perfect equality.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                            Bank Rate → RBI lends to banks for long-term needs (rediscounts bills of exchange); Repo Rate → RBI lends for short term. Both statements swap these, so both incorrect.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Inflation rate based on Consumer Price Index increases if:—

                                                                                                                            CPI inflation rises when Bank Rate or Reverse Repo Rate is cut; raising Repo Rate or SLR reduces inflation.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • An increase in the Bank Rate generally indicates that the:Central Bank is following a tight money policy

                                                                                                                            Higher Bank Rate → costlier borrowing for banks, less money supply; signals tight (contractionary) money policy.

                                                                                                                            Memory aid Bank Rate up = tight (dear) money; down = easy (cheap) money.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The lowering of Bank Rate by the Reserve Bank of India leads to:more liquidity in the market

                                                                                                                            Lower Bank Rate → banks borrow and lend more → more liquidity in the market.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • Bank Rate implies the rate of interest:at which the Reserve Bank of India discounts the Bills of Exchange

                                                                                                                            Bank Rate → rate at which RBI rediscounts bills of exchange, i.e. lends to commercial banks; a monetary policy tool. Must know

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • In the last one year i.e., June 2010 to June 2011, the difference between Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate is in the order of:1.00 percent

                                                                                                                            June 2010 to June 2011 → Repo minus Reverse Repo = 1.00 percent; from 2011-12 Reverse Repo was set 1% below Repo (no longer so).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • The Policy Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate announced by Reserve Bank of India on December 5, 2019 were respectively:5.15% and 4.9%

                                                                                                                            RBI policy, December 5, 2019 → Repo Rate 5.15%, Reverse Repo 4.90%; on 7 June 2024: Repo 6.50%, Bank Rate and MSF 6.75%.

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                            • As on September 30, 2014, Policy Review of Reserve Bank of India Repo Rate Stands at:8.00%

                                                                                                                            Repo Rate on September 30, 2014 → 8.00%; on 7 June 2024 → 6.50% (SDF 6.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 6.75%, CRR 4.50%, SLR 18.00%).

                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  Money and Banking · part 5 of 7
