                                                                                                                                  Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                  • In October 2001, Reserve Bank of India reduced Bank Rate from 7% to:6.50%

                                                                                                                                  October 2001 → RBI cut Bank Rate by 0.5 percent, from 7% to 6.5%; MSF aligned with Bank Rate from February 2012.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • According to the Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Review on 29 September, 2015, Bank Rate was:7.75%

                                                                                                                                  Bank Rate per RBI review of 29 September 2015 → 7.75%; 6.75% as on 7 June 2024.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following Governors of Reserve Bank of India and arrange them in chronological order:II, IV, I and III

                                                                                                                                  RBI Governors in order → I.G. Patel → Manmohan Singh → C. Rangarajan → D. Subbarao.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                  RBI Governor (and up to 4 Deputy Governors) appointed by Central Government; Governor's powers from RBI Act; Centre's power to direct RBI is in RBI Act Section 7, not Constitution.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Who among the following has not been the Governor of Reserve Bank of India?Raja J. Chelliah

                                                                                                                                  Raja J. Chelliah was never RBI Governor; Governors: Manmohan Singh (1982 to 1985), C. Rangarajan (1992 to 1997), Bimal Jalan (1997 to 2003).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • At present, who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                  RBI Governors → Raghuram Rajan (2013–2016), Urjit Patel (2016–2018), Shaktikanta Das (25th Governor, from 12 December 2018). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The Committee on Financial Sector Assessment is co-chaired by whom?Deputy Governor of Reserve Bank of India and Finance Secretary, Government of India

                                                                                                                                  Committee on Financial Sector Assessment (2006) → chaired by RBI Deputy Governor Rakesh Mohan, co-chaired by Finance Secretary; report March 2009.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The accounting year of the Reserve Bank of India is:April - March

                                                                                                                                  RBI accounting year → January–December, then July–June (from 1940), now April–March (from 2020-21, a nine-month transition year). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Negotiable Instruments Act came into effect in:1882

                                                                                                                                  Negotiable Instruments Act → passed December 1881, in force 1 March 1882; 2018 amendment added sections 143A, 148 to protect payees of dishonoured cheques.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is different from others?—

                                                                                                                                  UTI → mutual fund; Canbank Financial Services → Canara Bank subsidiary; SBI → commercial bank; U.P. State Financial Corporation → State Government enterprise.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Meaning of company limited by shares is:Restricted liability of holders

                                                                                                                                  Company limited by shares → members' liability limited to the unpaid amount on their shares (Companies Act 2013).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is not a feature of Limited Liability Partnership firm?Partners should be less than 20

                                                                                                                                  LLP → limited liability with partnership flexibility; minimum two partners, no maximum; perpetual succession; partners may manage and set governance by agreement.

                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse 'Partners should be less than 20' is wrong: LLP has no upper limit.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • An International Financial Services Centre has been set up at:Gandhinagar

                                                                                                                                  International Financial Services Centre → GIFT City, Gandhinagar (Gujarat); IFSCA set up April 27, 2020 under IFSCA Act, 2019.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Industrial Finance Corporation of India works as:A development bank

                                                                                                                                  IFCI (1 July 1948, statutory corporation) → India's first development financial institution, giving medium and long-term finance to industry.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The Apex institution in the field of Industrial finance in India is:Industrial Development Bank of India

                                                                                                                                  Apex institution for industrial finance → IDBI (July 1964), serving medium and large industries.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following:1, 2, 4, 3

                                                                                                                                  Order → IFCI (1948), ICICI (1955), UTI (February 1964), IDBI (July 1964).

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid F-C-U-D: IFCI, ICICI, UTI, IDBI.

                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse UTI (February 1964) came just before IDBI (July 1964).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following financial institutions of India:1, 2, 3, 4

                                                                                                                                  Order → IFCI (1948), ICICI (1955), IDBI (1964), NABARD (1982).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Match the list-I with List-II and using the codes given below the lists, select the correct answer:4 1 2 3

                                                                                                                                  Founding years → IFCI 1948; ICICI 1955; IDBI 1964; SIDBI 1990.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Match the column-A with the column-B and select the correct answer using the codes given below:3 2 1 4

                                                                                                                                  Founding years → ICICI 1955; IDBI 1964; Exim Bank 1982 (Act of 1981); BIFR 1987.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer using the code given below:3 4 2 1

                                                                                                                                  Founding years → Allahabad Bank 1865; Alliance Bank of Shimla 1874; Awadh (Oudh) Commercial Bank 1881; Punjab National Bank 1894.

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Allahabad Bank is the oldest (1865); PNB the youngest (1894).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following is a marketing institution?SAIL

                                                                                                                                  SAIL → marketing institution; SEBI (capital market), SIDBI and NABARD (agricultural credit) → apex institutions in their fields.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is not an apex institution?State Bank of India

                                                                                                                                  SBI is a commercial bank, not an apex institution; NABARD, SIDBI and State Cooperative Bank are apex institutions.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Arrange the following in asscending order of time in relation to their establishment:—

                                                                                                                                  Order → LIC (1956), UTI (February 1964), IDBI (July 1964), SEBI (1988). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was set up in India on:April, 2000

                                                                                                                                  IRDAI → from Malhotra Committee; autonomous body 1999; statutory body from April 2000; regulates insurance companies. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • IRDAI has set up a panel under whose chairmanship to examine need for standard cyber liability insurance product?P. Umesh

                                                                                                                                  IRDAI panel on standard cyber liability insurance product (October 2020) → chaired by P. Umesh.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The word ‘Actuaries’ is related to:Insurance

                                                                                                                                  Actuary → insurance professional who assesses risk and estimates premiums.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • 'Principle of Indemnity' does not apply to:Life Insurance

                                                                                                                                  Principle of Indemnity (restore insured to pre-loss position) applies to fire and marine insurance, not life insurance.

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid No indemnity in life insurance: the loss from a death cannot be valued.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Provident Fund in India is:Contractual savings

                                                                                                                                  Provident Fund → contractual savings: mandatory, government-managed retirement savings from employee and employer contributions.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Money received by the Government under the 'State Provident Funds' is credited to the:Public Accounts Fund

                                                                                                                                  State Provident Fund receipts → credited to Public Account, not Consolidated or Contingency Fund.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Importance of which of the following institution in India has reduced to most:Pension Funds

                                                                                                                                  Among private banks, development banks, Exim Bank and pension funds → pension funds' importance has fallen most.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • In India, which of the following is regulated by the Forward Markets Commission?Commodities Futures Trading

                                                                                                                                  Forward Markets Commission (1953) → regulated commodity futures; merged with SEBI on 28 September 2015.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which among the following agency regulate the mutual funds in India?SEBI

                                                                                                                                  SEBI → regulates mutual funds and stock markets; non-statutory 1988, statutory April 12, 1992 (SEBI Act 1992); HQ Mumbai. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid SEBI: born 1988, made statutory (given teeth) in 1992.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Private Sector Mutual Funds in India were permitted in:1993

                                                                                                                                  Private sector mutual funds allowed in 1993 (first: Kothari Pioneer); UTI began the industry in 1964; SBI Mutual Fund first non-UTI fund (1987).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Recently, Unit Scheme 1964 was in news, because:Its net worth has dropped significantly due to the long slump in the stock market.

                                                                                                                                  UTI's Unit Scheme 1964 (US-64) in news (1998) → net worth fell sharply; redemptions exceeded sales amid long stock market slump.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The objective of Unit Trust of India is:All of the above

                                                                                                                                  UTI (February 1, 1964) → mobilise small savings, share earnings with small investors, invest to promote industrial development; split in two on 1 February 2003.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is the largest mutual fund organization in India?SBI Mutual Fund

                                                                                                                                  Largest mutual fund → UTI at question time; now SBI Mutual Fund (by assets under management).

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The Head Office of National Stock Exchange of India is located at:Mumbai

                                                                                                                                  National Stock Exchange → set up November 1992 on Manohar J. Pherwani Committee's advice; head office Mumbai.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The promoter of National Stock Exchange of India is:All the above

                                                                                                                                  NSE promoters → IDBI, SBI, IFCI, LIC, GIC, IDFC; now (31.03.2024) promoter holding is zero.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                  Sensex → 30 stocks (not 50), market-cap weighted with proportional weightage; oldest stock exchange is Amsterdam, not New York (1792).

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Sensex = 30 stocks, not 50.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • A rise in 'SENSEX' means:an overall rise in prices of shares of group of companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange

                                                                                                                                  Rise in SENSEX → overall rise in share prices of its group of 30 companies on Bombay Stock Exchange (free-float market-weighted). Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • As on March 2014, no. of companies BSE Greenex Index includes was:25

                                                                                                                                  BSE Greenex → 25 top 'green' companies by greenhouse gas emissions, market cap and liquidity. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Among the following major stock exchanges of India, the exchange which recorded highest turnover during the year 2000-01 is:National Stock Exchange

                                                                                                                                  Highest turnover in 2000-01 → National Stock Exchange (8.39 lakh crore); NSE still has the highest turnover.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • The volatility in the Indian share market is due to: A. Inflow and outflow offoreign funds B. Fluctuations in foreign capital markets C. Changes in the monetary policy Which of the above mentioned causes are correct?A, B and C

                                                                                                                                  Share market volatility → foreign fund flows, foreign market swings, monetary policy changes, liquidity, politics, economic outlook, corporate results.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • ‘Dalal Street’ is situated at:Mumbai

                                                                                                                                  Dalal Street → Mumbai, home of Bombay Stock Exchange since 1874.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                  • Terms ‘Bull’and ‘Bear’are associated with which branch of commercial activity:Share Market

                                                                                                                                  'Bull' and 'Bear' → share market terms: bull market = prices rising; bear market = prices falling. Must know

                                                                                                                                  Memory aid A bull tosses up with its horns; a bear swipes down with its paws.

                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        Hour 24 →

                                                                                                                                        Hour 24 of 72 · Learn

                                                                                                                                        Money and Banking · part 6 of 7

                                                                                                                                        39 facts · 56 questions · 9 Must know

                                                                                                                                        Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                        • In the parlance of financial investments, the term ‘bear’ denotes:An investor who feels that the price of a particular security is going to fall

                                                                                                                                        Bear → investor expecting a security's price to fall; sells now, buys back after the fall.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which among the following is not a speculator in the stock exchange?Broker

                                                                                                                                        Stock market speculators → Bulls, Bears, Stags, Lame Ducks; a broker is an authorised member trading for customers, not a speculator. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Insider trading is related to:Share market

                                                                                                                                        Insider trading → share market dealing using non-public material information; illegal. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • In the context of finance, the term 'beta' refers to:a numeric value that measures the fluctuations of a stock to changes in the overall stock market

                                                                                                                                        Beta → numeric measure of a stock's volatility (systematic risk) relative to the overall market.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Capital Market means:Share market

                                                                                                                                        Capital market → share market; trades mostly long-term securities like stocks and bonds.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Consider the following markets:Only two

                                                                                                                                        Capital market → government bond market, stock market; money market → call money market, treasury bill market.

                                                                                                                                        Memory aid Long-term funds = capital market; up to one year = money market.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • The most volatile part of the Organized Money Market in India is:Call Money Market

                                                                                                                                        Most volatile part of organised money market → call money market (funds from overnight to 14 days).

                                                                                                                                        Memory aid Call money: overnight; notice money: 2 to 14 days.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following is not a participant in the India’s money market:RBI

                                                                                                                                        RBI is not a money market participant; it manages liquidity via LAF. Participants: banks, primary dealers, development finance institutions, mutual funds, NBFCs, corporates.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                        Commercial Paper → short-term unsecured promissory note; Call Money → overnight inter-bank funds. CDs are issued by banks, not RBI; zero-coupon bonds pay no interest.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • For which, commercial paper is the source of credit?Corporate Industry

                                                                                                                                        Commercial Paper (CP) → source of credit for corporate industry; introduced in India in 1990; unsecured promissory note; maturity 7 days to one year.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • With reference to Convertible Bonds, consider the following statements:Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                        Convertible Bonds → pay a lower interest rate (option to swap for equity); the equity option gives some indexation to rising consumer prices. Both statements correct.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Indian Government Bond Yields are influenced by which of the following?1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                        Indian Government bond yields are influenced by all three: US Federal Reserve actions, RBI actions (monetary policy), and inflation and short-term interest rates.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • With reference to the Indian economy, what are the advantages of ‘Inflation-Indexed Bonds (IIBs)’?1 and 2 only

                                                                                                                                        Inflation-Indexed Bonds (IIBs) → protect investors from inflation and let Government reduce coupon rates (cost saving); interest and capital gains on IIBs are not tax-free.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Blue Chip means:Shares giving consistent high rate of return.

                                                                                                                                        Blue Chip → shares of large, well-established, financially sound companies with dependable earnings, giving a consistently high rate of return.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Sweat Equity shares are issued to which of the following?Employees of the company

                                                                                                                                        Sweat Equity shares → issued to directors/employees at a discount or for non-cash consideration (know-how, IPR, value addition); a reward for their contribution.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Gilt-edged market means:market of Government securities

                                                                                                                                        Gilt-edged market → market of Government securities (G-secs); called 'gilt-edged' because interest payment and redemption on the due date are certain. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Gilt-edged (Government securities) with bullion market (gold, silver).

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following is irrelevant in the context of share market?SAPs

                                                                                                                                        SAPs (Structural Adjustment Programmes) → World Bank/IMF loan-linked policies for developing countries, not share market; Sensex, BSE, Nifty are share market terms. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • What is ‘NIKKEI’?Share Price Index in Tokyo Stock Exchange.

                                                                                                                                        NIKKEI (Nikkei 225) → share price index of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • What does S & P 500 relate to?An index of stocks of large companies

                                                                                                                                        S&P 500 (Standard and Poor 500) → market-capitalization-weighted stock index of the 500 leading publicly traded companies of the United States.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?1 and 3

                                                                                                                                        Dow Jones → New York; FTSE-100 → London; Hang Seng → Hong Kong (not Seoul); KOSPI → Seoul.

                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Don't pair Hang Seng with Seoul: Hang Seng is Hong Kong, KOSPI is Seoul.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?Singapore: Shcomp

                                                                                                                                        Wrong pair: Singapore–Shcomp. Shcomp = Shanghai index; Singapore's index = STI. Correct: Japan–Nikkei, U.K.–FTSE, U.S.A.–Nasdaq.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following is related to Brent Index?Crude oil prices

                                                                                                                                        Brent Index → crude oil prices; Brent Complex = oil market around the North Sea of Northwest Europe.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following four countries economy has market-cap more than the size of its GDP?India

                                                                                                                                        Among USA, India, China, Japan → India's market-cap exceeded its GDP (2007; all-time high 146.4% of GDP in December 2007).

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • A company declares dividend on:Subscribed Capital

                                                                                                                                        Dividend → declared on Subscribed Capital (the part of issued capital bought by shareholders); dividend = share of company's net profit paid to shareholders.

                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Not Issued or Authorized Capital; dividend goes on the capital actually subscribed by shareholders.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Debenture holders of a company are its:creditors

                                                                                                                                        Debenture holders → creditors of the company; debenture = medium/long-term loan certificate carrying a fixed rate of interest.

                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Shareholders own the company; debenture holders only lend to it.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following is different from the others from the point of view of ownership?Debenture of a Company

                                                                                                                                        Debenture of a company → freely transferable, so ownership can change; LIC Policy, Bank Fixed Deposit, Kisan Vikas Patra → fixed ownership.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • From the balance sheet of a company, it is possible to:determine the size and composition of the assets and liabilities of the company

                                                                                                                                        Balance sheet → snapshot of a company's financial condition at a point in time; shows size and composition of assets, liabilities and equity.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • The first Land Development Bank was established in 1920. It was located in:Jhang

                                                                                                                                        First Land Development Bank → Jhang (Punjab), 1920; gives long-term finance for land development and agricultural production.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Land Development Bank provides loan to farmers for:Long term

                                                                                                                                        Land Development Bank → long-term loans to farmers (land development, higher agricultural production). Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Land Development Banks is a part of:Cooperative Credit Structure

                                                                                                                                        Land Development Bank → part of the Cooperative Credit Structure (quasi-commercial), with State Cooperative Banks and Primary Agricultural Credit Societies.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Central Cooperative Banks work at:District level

                                                                                                                                        Cooperative credit is three-tier: PACS (village level) → Central Cooperative Banks (district level) → State Cooperative Banks (state level). Must know

                                                                                                                                        Memory aid V-D-S ladder: Village PACS, District CCB, State StCB.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • With reference to 'Urban Cooperative Banks' in India, consider the following statements:2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                        Urban Cooperative Banks → can issue equity and preference shares; under Banking Regulation Act, 1949 via 1966 amendment; regulated by RCS/CRCS and RBI, not local boards.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • As on March 2012, the number of Urban Cooperative Banks in India was:—

                                                                                                                                        Urban Cooperative Banks in India: 1645 (end-March 2011); 1618 (end-March 2012); 1502 (end-March 2023); 1483 (December 2023).

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Consumer Cooperative Stores are set up by:by the members

                                                                                                                                        Consumer Cooperative Stores → set up by the members; registered by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following is not a source of direct finance?None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                        All four (NABARD, RRB, SBI, Allahabad Bank) give direct finance; NABARD lends directly to food parks, warehouses, cold chains, not to individuals.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • During which Plan Period was the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) established?Sixth Five Year Plan

                                                                                                                                        NABARD → set up July 1982, during the Sixth Five Year Plan; HQ Mumbai; apex bank for agricultural refinance. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • Only organization to cater to all types of credit requirements of agriculture and rural development activities, is:NABARD

                                                                                                                                        NABARD → apex body for all credit needs of agriculture and rural development; set up 12 July 1982 under Act 61 of 1981; gives refinance. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 9 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • In India, the Bank NABARD does not provide refinance to:Export-Import Bank

                                                                                                                                        NABARD refinances Scheduled Commercial Banks, RRBs and State Land Development Banks; it does not refinance the Export-Import Bank.

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                        • The nodal agency for implementing the ‘Rural Infrastructure Development Fund Programmes’ is:NABARD

                                                                                                                                        NABARD → nodal agency for the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF); RIDF created 1995-96 with initial corpus of Rs. 2000 crore. Must know

                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)
