Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements:Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Madhya Pradesh → 'Ethiopia of India' (India State Hunger Index 2008): excessive malnutrition and infant mortality like Ethiopia and Chad; A and R true, R explains A. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following is a method to eradicate poverty?All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                              Ways to eradicate poverty → population control, increased savings (capital formation) and more investment in productive activities: all of these.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Assertion (A): Presently, there is no clear picture about the extent of poverty in India.Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of(A)

                                                                                                                                                                                              No clear picture of poverty extent (old Planning Commission and Tendulkar estimates differ); anti-poverty programmes restructured in nineties: A and R true, R not explanation.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • How do District Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs) help in the reduction of rural poverty in India?3 and 4 only

                                                                                                                                                                                              DRDAs → secure inter-sectoral and inter-departmental coordination for anti-poverty programmes and watch effective use of their funds; they are not PRIs and do not run studies.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements regarding Public Distribution Systems:1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                              PDS started in the 1960s as a price support programme to give essential commodities at subsidised prices; food subsidy is provided by the Government of India, not States.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Public Distribution System is aimed at -All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                              PDS aims → food security for the poor, prevent hoarding and black marketing, check exploitation by traders; also a tool of price stabilisation: all of the above.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following programme was meant for the eradication of poverty in rural India?All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                              Rural poverty eradication programmes: TRYSEM (15 August 1979), IRDP (2 October 1980), NREP (October 1980): all of the above.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Mitigating Poverty in Western Rajasthan (MPoWR) Programme is supported by:International Fund for Agriculture Development (IFAD) and Ratan Tata Trust

                                                                                                                                                                                              Mitigating Poverty in Western Rajasthan (MPoWR) → financed by IFAD, Government of Rajasthan and Sir Ratan Tata Trust; six poorest blocks of Jodhpur division.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has identified following categories of poverty. Which one is correct?Both (a) and (b)

                                                                                                                                                                                              UNDP's two categories of poverty → Income poverty (lack of material necessities) and Human poverty (denial of opportunity for a decent life).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Human Poverty Index was introduced in the Human Development Report of the year:1997

                                                                                                                                                                                              Human Poverty Index (HPI) → first published by UNDP in Human Development Report 1997; replaced by Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) from 2010. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid HPI born 1997, retired 2010 when MPI took over.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Human Development Report 1997 introduced the concept of Human Poverty Index (HPI) but Human Development Report replaced it with Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) in the year:2010

                                                                                                                                                                                              HPI introduced in HDR 1997; replaced by Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) in 2010; MPI captures deprivations in health, education and living standards. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The Multidimensional Poverty Index of UNDP includes:10 indicators

                                                                                                                                                                                              Multidimensional Poverty Index (OPHI with UNDP, 2010) → 3 dimensions (health, education, living standards) and 10 indicators.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid 3 and 10: Health 2 + Education 2 + Living standards 6 indicators.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Multidimensional Poverty Index includes:(i), (ii) and (iii) are correct

                                                                                                                                                                                              MPI dimensions → Health, Education and Living Standard (all three); developed in 2010 by OPHI and UNDP.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which one of the following indices is most suitable to assess the intensity of poverty in India?Multi-dimensional Poverty Index

                                                                                                                                                                                              Best index to assess intensity of poverty in India → Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (first in HDR 2010), not HDI, GII or HPI.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The Multi-dimensional Poverty Indexdeveloped by Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative with UNDP support covers which of the following?1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                              MPI (OPHI with UNDP) covers household-level deprivation in education, health, assets and services; it does not cover PPP, budget deficit or GDP growth.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to HDR 2013, the percentage of population suffering form multidimensional poverty in India is:53.7%

                                                                                                                                                                                              HDR 2013 → 53.7% of Indians in multidimensional poverty; HDR 2023/2024 → 16.4% (230.74 million, survey 2019-21).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • To know whether the rich are getting richer and the poor getting poorer, it is necessary to compare:the distribution of income of an identical set of income recepients in different periods of time

                                                                                                                                                                                              To know if the rich get richer and the poor poorer → compare income distribution of an identical set of income receivers over different periods.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following is not responsible for poverty?Increasing rate of investment

                                                                                                                                                                                              Causes of poverty → inadequate growth rate, high population growth, unemployment; an increasing rate of investment reduces poverty, so it is not a cause.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following is not considered as social indicator of poverty?Less number of means of transport

                                                                                                                                                                                              Social indicators of poverty → illiteracy, lack of healthcare, lack of jobs, malnutrition, no safe water or sanitation; fewer means of transport is not one.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The aim of Differential Interest Scheme was to provide concessional loans to:Weaker Section of Society

                                                                                                                                                                                              Differential Interest Rate Scheme (1972) → concessional loans to weaker sections of society.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Recently Govemment of India has approved the proposal of providing loans to Women Self Health Groups (SHG) at a lower interest rate to eradicatepoverty through women empowerment. The interest rate is:7.00%

                                                                                                                                                                                              May 2013 Cabinet decision (under NRLM): women SHGs get loans up to Rs. 3 lakh at 7% interest (interest subvention).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who among the following has been chosen for ‘Hoover Medal’ in March 2009 for his contribution to the upliftment of the poor and the rural people?A.P.J. Abdul Kalam

                                                                                                                                                                                              2008 Hoover Medal (announced 27 March 2009, New York) → Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, for upliftment of the poor and rural people.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Who among the following has given the idea of Self-Help Groups as an effective tool for poverty alleviation?Md. Yunus

                                                                                                                                                                                              Self-Help Groups and microfinance as a poverty tool → Muhammad Yunus (Bangladesh), founder of Grameen Bank, Nobel Peace Prize 2006.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The SAARC Ministerial Conference on Poverty Alleviation was held in:Islamabad

                                                                                                                                                                                              SAARC Ministerial Conference on Poverty Alleviation → Islamabad, April 2002; 13th SAARC Summit (Dhaka 2005) declared 2006-2015 the SAARC Decade of Poverty Alleviation.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Main features of Indian social structure are:(i), (ii) and (iii)

                                                                                                                                                                                              Main features of Indian social structure → excess rural population, many religions, many castes; poverty belongs to the socio-economic structure, not the social one.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • With reference to the Indian economy after the 1991 economic liberalization, consider the following statements:3 and 4 only

                                                                                                                                                                                              Post-1991 rural economy (NITI Aayog, 2017): non-farm growth rose and rural employment growth fell; worker productivity rose in rural and urban areas; rural workforce share fell.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The rate of growth of employment in India has generally been of the order of:2 percent per annum

                                                                                                                                                                                              Growth rate of employment in India (question period) → about 2 percent per annum.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Unemployment problem leads to poverty because:People living below poverty line increase

                                                                                                                                                                                              Unemployment → loss of income, so people near the poverty line fall below it; more people below poverty line means more poverty.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Name the Indian State which has the maximum percentage of educated unemployed persons?Kerala

                                                                                                                                                                                              Highest level of educated unemployment in India → Kerala (people cannot find jobs matching their qualifications).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer using the code given below:Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

                                                                                                                                                                                              Educated unemployment rises with high growth when professional or skilled education is lacking; book: A and R true, R explains A. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • In the following question, a statement followed by two assumptions numbered I and II are given. You have to consider the statement and the assumptions and decide which of the assumptions follows from the statement. Statement: Unemployment allowance should be given to all uemployed Indian youth above 18 years of age. Assumptions: I. Unemployed youth in India need monetary support. II. The government has sufficient funds to provide allowance to all unemployed youth.Only I follows

                                                                                                                                                                                              Statement: unemployment allowance for all unemployed youth above 18 → only assumption I (youth need monetary support) follows; enough government funds is not implied.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Assertion (A): Roots of urban poverty lies in rural areas. Assertion (B): Level of education is normally low in rural areas. Consider the above statements and find out the correct answer from the code given below:Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Roots of urban poverty lie in rural areas: low rural education → migrants get poor urban jobs and stay poor; A and R true, R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • As per the number of employed males per thousand in urban areas in year 1999-2000, put the name offollowing States in descending order: A. Meghalaya B. Nagaland C. Assam D. West Bengal Select the correct answer from the codes given below:D, C, B, A

                                                                                                                                                                                              Employed urban males per thousand, 1999-2000 (descending) → West Bengal, Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya; same order in PLFS 2022-23 male LFPR. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid W-A-N-M: West Bengal > Assam > Nagaland > Meghalaya.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Employment growth in the organized sector in India during the period between 1994 and 2007 has:declined

                                                                                                                                                                                              Organised sector employment growth declined in 1994-2007: from 1.2% a year (1983-94) to –0.03% a year (Economic Survey 2009-10).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Most of the unemployment in India is:Structural

                                                                                                                                                                                              Most unemployment in India → Structural: mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs, due to poor education and training.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Disguised unemployment means:Marginal productivity of labour is zero

                                                                                                                                                                                              Disguised (hidden) unemployment → marginal productivity of labour is zero; more persons employed in a job than needed, so removing them does not cut output. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Disguised = in disguise: looks employed, adds nothing (marginal product zero).

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • In India disguised unemployment is main characteristic of:Primary Sector

                                                                                                                                                                                              Disguised unemployment in India → mainly in the primary sector (agriculture and allied), due to heavy population pressure on land. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Disguised unemployment in India is mainly related to: I. Agricultural sector II. Rural Area III. Manufacturing sector IV. Urban area Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:I and II

                                                                                                                                                                                              Disguised unemployment in India → mainly agricultural sector in rural areas (I and II), not manufacturing or urban areas.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The number of persons who remained unemployed for a major part of the year is called:Usual status unemployment

                                                                                                                                                                                              Unemployed for a major part of the year → Usual Status unemployment (reference period 365 days, NSSO, now NSO); captures long-term open unemployment.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which of the following method is not used by N.S.S.O. for the measurement of unemployment in India?Current Monthly Status

                                                                                                                                                                                              NSSO unemployment measures: Usual Principal Status (one year), Current Weekly Status (one week), Current Daily Status (each day of the week); no 'Current Monthly Status'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Year, Week, Day: never Month.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • In India which one of the following collects and publishes the unemployment Index?N.S.S.O.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Unemployment data in India → collected and published by NSSO (Employment-Unemployment Surveys); NSSO merged with CSO to form NSO in 2019.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • The growth rate of which one of the following sectors has very low employment elasticity?Mixed Farming

                                                                                                                                                                                              Lowest employment elasticity → agriculture/mixed farming (0.04, 1999-2000 to 2009-2010); construction highest (1.13); finance 0.66; manufacturing 0.09.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Which one of the following is not responsible for unemployment?Growth of per capita income

                                                                                                                                                                                              Causes of unemployment → rapid population growth, lack of skill, lack of manpower planning; growth of per capita income is not a cause.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Labour Force Participation Rate is defined as the:ratio of employed and willing to work to working age population

                                                                                                                                                                                              Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) → % of persons in the labour force (working, or seeking/available for work) in the working-age population.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A)

                                                                                                                                                                                              Female LFPR fell (31.1% in 2013-2014 to 23.3% in 2017-18) due to rising education of young women and rising household income; A and R true, R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • What was the Current Daily Status (CDS) unemployment rate in India as per National Sample Survey 2011-12?5.6 percent

                                                                                                                                                                                              NSS 68th round (2011-12) unemployment rate: Current Daily Status 5.6%, Current Weekly Status 3.7%, Usual Status 2.7%.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Memory aid Daily > Weekly > Usual: the shorter the reference period, the higher the rate here.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to NSS 61st round data, unemployment at current daily status in rural as well as urban areas is nearly:8 %

                                                                                                                                                                                              NSS 61st round → CDS unemployment about 8% in both rural (8.3%) and urban (8.2%) areas; 68th round (2011-12) → 5.6% all-India.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
