                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Foreign Exchange, FDI & External Debt · part 1 of 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      47 facts · 65 questions · 8 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • One of the important goals of the economic liberalization policy is to achieve full convertibility of the Indian rupee. This is being advocated because:it will attract more foreign capital inflow in India.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full rupee convertibility advocated to attract more foreign capital; LERMS from March 1992; rupee fully convertible on current account in August 1994 (IMF Article VIII). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 8 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In which budget did the Finance Minister announce the Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System?Union Budget, 1992-1993

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) → announced in Union Budget 1992-93; partial convertibility with dual rate (market interbank rate + RBI official rate).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements: Full convertibility of the rupee may mean –1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full convertibility of rupee → free float with other currencies and direct exchange anywhere inside or outside India; it does not make rupee an international currency.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements: The Indian rupee is fully convertible –1 alone

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Rupee is fully convertible only on current account (since August 1994); capital account convertibility is partial; not convertible into gold.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid Current = Complete; Capital = Partial.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following constitute Capital Account?1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Capital account → foreign loans, FDI, portfolio investment; private remittances belong to the current account.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Tarapore Committee was associated with which one of the following?Fuller capital account convertibility

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      S.S. Tarapore Committees (RBI) → capital account convertibility: first report May 1997; second on fuller CAC, report 31 July 2006. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Devaluation of a currency means:reduction in the value of a currency vis-a-vis major internationally traded currencies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Devaluation → official lowering of a currency's value against major international currencies (fixed exchange rate); rupee devalued in 1949, 1966 and 1991. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Devalued in three years but four times: 1991 had two steps (July 1 and July 3).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Rupee was devalued by what percent in July, 1991?18

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      July 1991 rupee devaluation → about 18% in two steps (1 and 3 July); 17.38% against pound sterling, about 18.7% in US dollar terms; financial year 1991-92. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements: The effect of devaluation of a currency is that it necessarily1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Devaluation necessarily makes exports more competitive only; it lowers the currency's foreign value and need not improve trade balance (costly essential imports like crude).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Devaluation → country's goods become cheaper abroad, so exports rise and imports become costly: A and R true, R explains A. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not the effect of devaluation of currency?This causes deflation in the importing country.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Devaluation does not cause deflation in the importing country; it raises the prices of imported goods and the domestic price level.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Assertion (A): The rate of growth of India's exports has shown an appreciable increase after 1991.Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India's export growth rose after 1991 because of devaluation (about 18% on 1 and 3 July 1991) and export promotion: A and R true, R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The problem of International liquidity is related to the non-availability of:Dollars and other hard currencies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      International liquidity problem → shortage of dollars and other hard currencies (resources to finance BoP deficits: gold, SDRs, foreign currencies).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The economic crisis in the later half of 1990s most seriously affected Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and South Korea. The cause of the crisis was:the prolonged over-valuation of local currencies vis-avis the western currencies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Late-1990s East Asian crisis (Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, South Korea) → prolonged over-valuation of local currencies; began in Thailand, July 1997.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • What has been the impact of the heavy devaluation of currencies in South-East Asian countries in the recent months on Indian exports?Unfavourable

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      South-East Asian currency devaluations (1997-98) → unfavourable for Indian exports, which compete with theirs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • If another global financial crisis happens in the near future, which of the following actions/policies are most likely to give some immunity to India?1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Immunity from a global financial crisis → avoid short-term foreign borrowings; more foreign banks and full capital account convertibility would increase risk.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the context of India, which of the following factors is/ are contributor/contributors to reducing the risk of a currency crisis?1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reduce currency crisis risk → IT sector forex earnings and remittances from Indians abroad; more government expenditure does not help.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not the most likely measure the Government/RBI takes to stop the slide of Indian rupee?Following an expansionary monetary policy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      To stop rupee slide: curb non-essential imports, promote exports, Masala Bonds, easier ECB rules; not expansionary monetary policy (it raises rupee supply).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following measures is not likely to aid in improving India’s Balance of Payment position?Levying of higher duties on exports

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Higher duties on exports cut exports, so they do not help BoP; import substitution, devaluation and higher import tariffs can help.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following actions which the Government can take:1 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reduce current account deficit → devalue currency and attract FDI/FII funds; cutting export subsidy would reduce exports, so it does not help.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the last one decade, which one among the following sectors has attracted the highest Foreign Direct Investment inflows into India?Services sector

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Highest FDI inflows: Telecommunication in the question period (per explanation); Services sector leads April 2000 to March 2024 (16.13%). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which sector in India attracts the highest FDI equity flow?Service Sector

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Sector attracting the highest FDI equity inflow in India → Service sector.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Largest inflow of foreign direct investment in India in 2007-08 took place in which sector?Services

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Largest FDI inflow in 2007-08 (and over the last decade) → services sector. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The largest share of Foreign Direct Investment (1997- 2000) went to:Services sector

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Largest FDI share in 1997-2000 → services sector; in the last 3 years (2021-2024) Computer Software and Hardware led, then services.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • India in recent past has succeeded in attracting large foreign investment in:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India attracted large foreign investment in life insurance, banking and automobiles; services (incl. banking, insurance) got 16.13% of FDI, April 2000 to March 2024.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The opportunities available in the Indian market for foreign exchange earnings are in the fields of:All the four

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Foreign exchange earning opportunities in India → tourism, medical care, garments and leather goods: all four.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following States of India received the highest Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) equity flow during April to September 2022?Karnataka

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FDI equity inflow April-September 2022 → Karnataka highest among options (5329 million USD); Maharashtra highest overall (8000 million USD).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In Bihar, during April-June 2018, which sector attracted the highest FDI equity inflow?Service sector

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Bihar, April-June 2018 → service sector attracted the highest FDI equity inflow.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The maximum foreign exchange inflow came to India in the year 2005-06 through which of the following sources:Portfolio investment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Largest foreign exchange inflow to India in 2005-06 (among options) → portfolio investment.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The flow of foreign exchange in which of the following forms can be said to be most volatile in the Indian context?Both (b) and (c) above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Most volatile foreign exchange flows → NRI deposits and foreign portfolio investment; they chase interest rate gaps and leave when rates turn unfavourable.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Foreign currency which has a tendency of quick migration is called:Hot currency

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Hot currency (hot money) → foreign currency that moves quickly between markets chasing the highest short-term interest rates.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:1 and 2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Tight US Fed policy can cause capital flight; capital flight can raise interest cost of firms with ECBs; devaluation increases (not decreases) ECB currency risk.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • ‘Tobin Tax’is levied on:on foreign exchange transactions

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Tobin Tax (after economist James Tobin) → tax on foreign exchange (spot currency conversion) transactions to curb short-term currency speculation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • With reference to Foreign Direct Investment in India, which one of the following is considered its major characteristic?It is a largely non-debt creating capital flow.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FDI → largely non-debt creating capital flow; investment in an unlisted Indian company, or ten percent or more of a listed company's equity.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following would include Foreign Direct Investment in India?1, 2 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FDI includes subsidiaries of foreign companies, majority foreign equity in Indian firms and firms fully financed by foreign companies; portfolio investment is not FDI.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Counted as FDI → FCCBs, foreign institutional investment with conditions, GDRs/ADRs; non-resident external deposits are debt-creating inflows, not FDI.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • As part of the liberalization programme and with a view to attract foreign exchange, the Government and the RBI have, devised two schemes known as FCNR 'A' and FCNR 'B'. Which of the following is/are true regarding these two schemes?1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FCNR(A) → 1975, RBI bore exchange rate risk, withdrawn 1993; FCNR(B) from 15 May 1993, banks bear the risk; only scheme A withdrawn.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Global capital flows to developing countries increased significantly during the nineties. In view of the East Asian financial crisis and Latin American experience, which type of inflow is good for the host country?Foreign Direct Investment

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Lesson of East Asian and Latin American crises → FDI is the best inflow (stable); excess volatile portfolio investment caused the crises.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Both Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) are related to investment in a country. Which one of the following statements best represents an important difference between the two?FII helps in increasing capital availability in general, while FDI only targets specific sectors

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      FDI vs FII: FII raises capital availability in general (short-term, secondary market); FDI targets specific sectors, is more stable, brings technology and management.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is not an example offoreign direct investment?The purchase of bonds or stocks issued by Pharma Company overseas

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Buying bonds or stocks of an overseas pharma company → portfolio investment, not FDI; acquiring a mill, a wholly owned firm or a new plant abroad are FDI.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Participatory Notes (PNs) are associated with which one of the following?Foreign Institutional Investors

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Participatory Notes (P-Notes) → issued by registered FIIs to overseas investors who invest in Indian stocks without registering with SEBI (started 2000).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following is issued by registered foreign portfolio investors to overseas investors who want to be part of Indian stock market without registering themselves directly?Participatory Note

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Participatory Note → issued by SEBI-registered foreign portfolio investors to overseas investors wanting Indian stocks without direct registration (overseas derivative instrument).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Limit of investment for outstanding corporate bond for Foreign Portfolio Investment in Union Budget 2020-21 has been extended upto:15%

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Union Budget 2020-21 → FPI limit in outstanding corporate bonds raised from 9% to 15%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • India receives largest inflow of foreign capital in equity investment from:Singapore

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Largest FDI equity source: Mauritius in the question period and cumulative; Singapore in recent years (US$ 11,774 million in 2023-24), then Mauritius, USA. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • During 1991-95 the countries which brought largest foreign direct investment to India are:USA and Japan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Largest FDI sources to India in 1991-95 → USA and Japan.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In terms of the share in Foreign Direct Investment Equity inflows in India during 2016-17, which of the following countries is on the top?Mauritius

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Top FDI equity sources in 2016-17 → Mauritius > Singapore > Japan; in 2023-24 → Singapore > Mauritius > USA > Netherlands > Japan.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A great deal of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) to India comes from Mauritius than frommany major and mature economies like UK and France. Why?India has double taxation avoidance agreement with Mauritius

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Large FDI from Mauritius → India's Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) with Mauritius; investors route capital via Mauritius to pay less tax.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
