                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Foreign Exchange, FDI & External Debt · part 2 of 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            64 facts · 71 questions · 4 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • As per the Economic Survey, 2023, which of the following statements describe(s) the trend of Foreign Direct Investment in India?Only 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Economic Survey 2022-23: FDI fell in the first half of FY23 due to weak global economy, though still above pre-pandemic levels; only statement 4.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) has been operationalized between India and the United States from:30 September, 2015

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FATCA (US law, 2010) → India-US IGA signed 9 July 2015, operational from 30 September 2015; shares offshore account information against tax evasion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • With reference to Government of India's decisions regarding Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) during the year 2001-2002, consider the following statements:Only 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FDI 2001-02: tea sector foreign firm to disinvest 26% (not 33%) within 5 years; print media foreign capital max 26%, largest Indian shareholder above 26%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In the calendar year 2005, the amount of capital invested by foreign institutional investors was approximately:US $ 10.7 bn.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Calendar year 2005 → foreign institutional investors invested about US$ 10.7 billion in Indian companies.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In India, Foreign Investment Promotion Boardnow works under:Ministry of Finance

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FIPB moved to Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance in January 2003; abolished in 2017 (approvals now by administrative ministries).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Most recently, FDI has now opened in which of the following sectors in India?Retail trade

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FDI opened in retail trade: single-brand 51% (2006), multi-brand 51% (2012); 100% single-brand with 30% local sourcing.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • With reference to foreign-owned e-commerce firms operating in India, which of the following statements is/are correct?2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Foreign-owned e-commerce: 100% FDI only in marketplace model; cannot sell own inventory; vendor deemed controlled if over 25% of its purchases come from the marketplace.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • On October 4,2012, the Government of India has proposed to change the limits of FDI in Insurance Sector. It is proposed to:raise the FDI limit from 26% to 49%

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FDI in insurance: proposal on 4 October 2012 to raise it from 26% to 49%; Budget 2021-22 raised it from 49% to 74% (effective 19 May 2021). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Foreign equity holding allowed in small scale sector in 1995-96 is:24%

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Foreign equity in small scale units, 1995-96 → up to 24%; above 24% of paid-up capital the unit lost its SSI status.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • A country is said to be in debt trap if:it has to borrow to make interest payments on outstanding loans

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Debt trap → a country must take new loans just to pay interest on old loans.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • At the end of 2010, India's external debt had cross the mark of:US $ 300 Billion

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India's external debt crossed US$ 300 billion by end-2010; US$ 624.7 billion at end-March 2023; US$ 648.2 billion at end-December 2023.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India's external debt is mostly non-government (US$ 506.0 billion of US$ 648.2 billion, end-December 2023) and not all in US dollars: both statements false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following continued to be the major component of India’s external credit till 2017?Commercial borrowing

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Major component of India's external debt → commercial borrowings (about 38% in 2017; 33.2% at end-December 2023).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • India's external debt increased from US$ 98,158 million as at the end of March 2000 to US $ 100,225 million as at the end of March 2001 due to increase in:commercial borrowings and NRI deposits

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India's external debt rose from US$ 98,158 million (March 2000) to US$ 100,225 million (March 2001) due to commercial borrowings and NRI deposits.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which among the following institutions regulates the external commercial borrowings?Reserve Bank of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) → regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (eligible borrowers, end use, maturity, all-in-cost ceiling).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • According to the World Bank’s Global Development Finance Report 2010, the correct descending order of the world’s five most indebted countries is:Russia, China, Turkey, Brazil, India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            World Bank Global Development Finance 2010 → most indebted: Russia, China, Turkey, Brazil, India; end-December 2022: China, Brazil, India, Mexico, Turkey.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • As on today, which one of the following countries has the largest external debt?USA

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Largest external debt → USA (US$ 24.5 trillion, 26.3% of global debt, end-December 2022), then UK, France, Germany, Japan.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • On the basis of size and composition of external debt, World Bank has classified India as:a less indebted country

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            World Bank classifies India as a less indebted country; external debt-to-GDP 18.7% at end-December 2023.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which country has highest loan from the World Bank after India till June, 2010?Mexico

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Largest World Bank borrower after India (till June 2010) → Mexico; in 2022 India had the highest IBRD/IDA debt stock (US$ 38.26 billion).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In the year 2001, India offered a grant of five million dollars to Tajikistan to:tackle the drought situation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            May 2001 → India gave Tajikistan a US$ 5 million grant to tackle drought.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In the year 2001, Germany approved a $ 32 million credit to India:for Tehri dam project

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            October 2001 → Germany granted a US$ 32 million credit for the Tehri dam project (Uttarakhand).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following statement about green bonds is NOT true?Green bonds are fixed interest loan with short date maturities

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Green bonds → fixed-income, low-cost loans with long (not short) maturities for climate projects; first issued by European Investment Bank in 2007; World Bank in 2008.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse The first green bond came from the European Investment Bank ('Climate Awareness Bond'), not a 'Fund' as option (b) says.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements for `India Millennium Deposit's Scheme:1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India Millennium Deposit scheme → launched 21 October 2000 by SBI for NRIs (not residents); five-year deposits at 8.5%; raised $ 5.5 billion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Resurgent India Bonds were issued in US dollar, Pound Sterling and:Deutsche Mark

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Resurgent India Bonds (SBI, 5 August 1998) → issued in US dollar, Pound Sterling and Deutsche Mark for five years.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Resurgent India Bonds → Deutsche Mark; India Millennium Deposits → euro.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is a bond through which Indian entities can raise money from foreign markets in rupees, and not in foreign currency?Masala Bonds

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Masala Bonds → rupee-denominated bonds issued abroad by Indian entities, so the issuer is shielded from currency risk; fund infrastructure and internationalise the rupee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • With reference to 'IFC Masala Bonds' sometimes seen in the news, which of the statements given below is/are correct?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            IFC (World Bank arm) issued the first Masala bond in November 2014; rupee-denominated debt for public and private sector; RBI allowed corporates on 29 September 2015.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Closure of Oil-Pool account effected from:1-4-2002

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Oil-Pool Account closed with abolition of the Administered Price Mechanism (APM) in oil on 1-4-2002 (Finance Minister Yashwant Sinha).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following best describes the term 'import cover', sometimes seen in the news?It is the number of months of imports that could be paid for by a country's international reserves

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Import cover → number of months of imports a country's international reserves can pay for; 11 months at end-December 2023.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In the fiscal year 2018-19, the total foreign exchange reserves are:Rs. 28,55,882 crore

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India's forex reserves, 2018-19 (end-March 2019) → Rs. 28,55,882 crore; 29 March 2024 → Rs. 53,84,281 crore (US$ 645.58 billion).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • According to the Reserve Bank of India, what was the total values of the foreign exchange reserves of India in 2018-19?412871 million US dollar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            RBI: forex reserves in 2018-19 (end-March 2019) → US$ 412871 million; on 29 March 2024 → US$ 645.58 billion.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following statements is not true in the context of foreign exchange reserves of India?Special Drawing Rights are not included in this

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India's forex reserves (held by RBI) → foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and reserve tranche position in IMF; so 'SDRs not included' is false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which among the following has largest share in the foreign exchange reserves of India?Foreign currency assets

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Largest share in India's forex reserves → foreign currency assets (US$ 570618 million on 29 March 2024), then gold, SDRs, IMF reserve position.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following groups of items is included in India's foreign exchange reserves?Foreign currency assets, gold holdings of the RBI and SDRs

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            India's forex reserves → foreign currency assets, RBI gold, SDRs and IMF reserve tranche; loans from World Bank or foreign countries are not included.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Memory aid FGSR: Foreign currency, Gold, SDRs, Reserve tranche.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements:2 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Forex reserves were US$ 129.7 billion on 10 December 2004 (above 125 billion); WPI series from April 2000 had base 1993-94; current base 2011-12.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            NEER rise → rupee appreciation; REER rise → loss (not gain) of trade competitiveness; higher domestic inflation than abroad widens the NEER–REER gap.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following statements, the price of any currency in international market is decided by the:2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A currency's price in the international market → set by demand for the country's goods/services and its government's stability; the World Bank has no role.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • According to new RBI Governor, which among the following factors determines the exchange value of money?All the three above factors

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Factors that determine exchange value of money (RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan) → high inflation, high fiscal deficit, high crude oil prices: all three.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following is the correct sequence of decreasing order of the given currencies in terms of their value in Indian Rupees?US dollar, Canadian dollar, New Zealand dollar, Hong Kong dollar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Value in rupees (descending) → US dollar > Canadian dollar > New Zealand dollar > Hong Kong dollar (14 June 2024: Rs. 83.54, 60.65, 51.16, 10.69).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Indian Rupee, in recent years, has gained strength against which of the following currency?Dollar

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Rupee kept appreciating against the US dollar (48.395 in 2002-03 to 44.273 in 2005-06); it fluctuated against euro, yen and pound.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • If the rupees per US Dollar exchange rate changes from Rs. 60 to Rs. 65 in a time period by the market forces, it implies:Depreciation of Rupee

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Rs. 60 → Rs. 65 per dollar through market forces → depreciation of rupee (its value fell); a rise in a currency's value is appreciation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Depreciation = market-driven fall (floating rate); Devaluation = official cut by government (fixed rate).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • When the exchange rate changes from 1$ = Rs. 60 to 1$ = Rs. 58, it means: I. Rupee value has appreciated II. Dollar value has depreciated III. Rupee value has depreciated IV. Dollar value has appreciatedI and II are correct

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            1$ = Rs. 60 → Rs. 58 → rupee appreciated and dollar depreciated (I and II).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Memory aid Fewer rupees per dollar = stronger rupee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which among the following currencies is the costliest?Pound Sterling

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Costliest among euro, pound and dollar → Pound Sterling (25 June 2024: Rs. 105.82; euro Rs. 89.38; dollar Rs. 83.43).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following is/are treated as artificial currency?SDR

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Artificial currency → Special Drawing Right (SDR), created by IMF and valued on a basket of currencies; ADR/GDR are financial instruments.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • What is the name of New Single European Currency:Euro

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            New single European currency (European Monetary Union) → Euro; now official currency of 20 of the 27 EU member states. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following is not true for ‘Euro’ in 1999:It is in circulation

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Euro introduced in 1999 as unit of account, means of deferred payment and mode of payment, but it was not yet in circulation then. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Euro is the national currency of:—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Euro → currency of only 12 EU states in the question period; now 20 of 27 EU members (not Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which country has not accepted Euro as its currency?All the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Britain, Denmark and Sweden → none of them uses the euro: all the above.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Eurodollars are:U.S. dollars circulating in Europe

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Eurodollars → US dollar deposits in banks outside the USA (mainly Europe), outside the US Federal Reserve's jurisdiction.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In which one of the following countries is Rupee its currency?Seychelles

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Rupee is the currency of Seychelles; Bhutan → Ngultrum; Malaysia → Ringgit; Maldives → Rufiyaa.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Don't pick Bhutan or Maldives: their currencies are Ngultrum and Rufiyaa, not rupee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Bangladesh's currency is:Taka

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Bangladesh → Taka; Indonesia → Rupiah; Italy → Lira (now Euro).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Baht is the currency of:Thailand

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Baht → Thailand; Turkiye → Turkish Lira; Vietnam → Dong; Iran → Rial.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Currency of China is:Yuan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            China → Yuan (unit of Renminbi); Japan → Yen; Italy → Lira (now Euro); India → Rupee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Dinar/New Dinar is not the currency of:U.A.E.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            UAE's currency is Dirham, not Dinar; Sudan, Yugoslavia and Tunisia had Dinar/New Dinar.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:4 3 1 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Ringgit → Malaysia; Baht → Thailand; Rupiah → Indonesia; Won → South Korea.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Match List 1 (Country) with List 2 (Currency) on the basis of given codes:2 4 1 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Mexico → Peso; Austria → Schilling (now Euro); Japan → Yen; Saudi Arabia → Riyal.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following statements is correct with reference to FEMA in India?Under FEMA, violation offoreign exchange rules has ceased to be a criminal offence.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FERA 1973 replaced by FEMA 1999 on 1 June 2000; under FEMA, foreign exchange violations are civil, not criminal, offences. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • FEMA(Foreign Exchange Management Act) was finally implemented in the year:2002

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            FEMA 1999 came into force on 1 June 2000 with a two-year sunset clause; fully implemented in 2002.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following authority sanctions foreign exchange for import of goods?Exchange Bank

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Foreign exchange for imports → sanctioned by Exchange Banks (Authorised Dealer Category-I banks) under FEMA 1999.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Assertion (A): Ceiling on foreign exchange for a host of current account transaction heads was lowered in the year 2000.A is true, but R is false

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Ceiling on foreign exchange for many current account heads was lowered in 2000 (A true); foreign currency assets rose (US$ 38036 million to 42281 million), so R false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • What is the correct chronological sequence of the following Indian Acts?4, 2, 1, 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Chronology: Minimum Wages Act 1948 → Industries (Development and Regulation) Act 1951 → MRTP Act 1969 → FERA 1973.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Hawala transactions relate to payments:received in rupees against overseas currencies and vice versa without going through the official channels

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Hawala → informal transfer of money (rupees against foreign currency and vice versa) outside official channels, without physical movement or records.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Prevention of Money LaunderingAct came into force in India during:2005

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) 2002 → Presidential assent 17 January 2003; came into force 1 July 2005.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Don't confuse Enacted in 2002, but in force only from 2005.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following economists propagated the Pure Monetary Theory of Trade Cycle?Hawtrey

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Pure Monetary Theory of Trade Cycle → R.G. Hawtrey (British): the trade cycle is a purely monetary phenomenon.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Correct pairs: rise in forex reserves → monetary expansion; low import growth → industrial recession; portfolio investment → FIIs; euro-issues are funds raised abroad, not shares held.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • With reference to Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), consider the following statements:1 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  AIIB (Beijing, operations from January 2016) → 96 members incl. many outside Asia (more than 80); China largest shareholder, India second.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Where was the first World Summit on Social Development under the aegis of UNESCO held?Copenhagen

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  First World Summit for Social Development (UNESCO aegis) → Copenhagen, March 1995; put people at the centre of development.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • How many countries are members of World Bank?189

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  World Bank (IBRD) → 189 member countries; created at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference along with the IMF.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The International Development Association, a lending agency, is administered by the:International Bank for Reconstruction and Development

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  International Development Association (IDA) → World Bank group agency administered by IBRD; concessional aid to the poorest countries.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Global Infrastructure Facility is a/an:World Bank collaboration that facilitates the preparation and structuring of complex infrastructure Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) to enable mobilization of private sector and institutional investor capital

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Global Infrastructure Facility (GIF) → World Bank platform to prepare and structure complex infrastructure PPPs and mobilise private and institutional capital.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • 'World Development Report' is an annual publication of:International Bank for Reconstruction and Development

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  World Development Report → annual publication of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The theme of the World Development Report 2001 is:Attacking Poverty

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  World Development Report 2001 theme → 'Attacking Poverty: Opportunity, Empowerment and Security'; WDR 2023 → 'Migrants, Refugees, and Societies'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to the World Development Report, low income economics are those for which the per capita GNP in 1994 was:US $ 725 or less

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  World Development Report: low income economies in 1994 → per capita GNP US$ 725 or less; FY25 low income → GNI US$ 1,145 or less.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • As per the World Development Report 2000, the highest Per Capita Income is in:Luxembourg

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  World Development Report 2000 → highest per capita income: Luxembourg ($44640); in 2022 (PPP per capita GNI) → Norway, then Qatar.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following is not a sub-index of the World Bank’s 'Ease of Doing Business Index'?Maintenance of law and order

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Ease of Doing Business had 10 sub-indicators (e.g. paying taxes, registering property, construction permits); maintenance of law and order was not one.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In ‘Ease of Doing Business Report’published by World Bank on 31th October, 2017, India has been placed at which rank?100

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  World Bank Doing Business (October 2017, DBR 2018) → India 100th of 190, up from 130th; DBR 2020 → 63rd.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • India’s ranking in the ‘Ease of Doing Business Index’ is sometimes, seen in the news. Which of the following has declared that ranking?World Bank

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Ease of Doing Business Index → published annually by the World Bank (Group).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • With reference to the World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Report, which of the following statement(s) is/ are correct?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Doing Business Report 2020 → India 63rd of 190 (up 14 places from 77th in 2019); top 3: New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which two States have been jointly ranked first in the ease of doing business ranking issued by the World Bank and DIPP in October 2016?Andhra Pradesh and Telangana

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  State ease of doing business ranking (World Bank-DIPP, October 2016) → Andhra Pradesh and Telangana jointly first; Gujarat (2015 topper) third.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following issues the ‘Global Economic Prospects’ report periodically?The World Bank

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  'Global Economic Prospects' → World Bank flagship report, issued twice a year (January and June).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one among the following countries has lowest GDP per capita?India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Lowest GDP per capita among China, India, Indonesia, Sri Lanka → India (9171.9 PPP $ in 2022).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The second largest economy in the world next to USA is:China

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Second largest economy after USA (nominal): Japan in 2005 per explanation; China now (2022 order: USA, China, Japan, Germany, India, UK).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following countries is the third largest economy of the world?Japan
