                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India : Population · part 1 of 6

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      40 facts · 57 questions · 9 Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Read the key facts and each question with its answer (30 min), then cover the answers and recall (10 min). Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Natural growth of population is the outcome of which of the following?A and B

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Natural growth of population = Crude Birth Rate minus Crude Death Rate; migration is not counted.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which arrangement offollowing would show sequence of demographic transition as typically associated with economic development?1, 3, 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Demographic transition (term by Frank W. Notestein) → high birth + high death → high birth + low death → low birth + low death. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Select one of the following set of processes leading to stable population structure:Constant birth and death rate

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Stable population → constant (low) birth and death rates, so growth is negligible.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • At present India's population growth is passing through the phase of which one of the following?High growth rate with definite signs of slowing down

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India's population growth now → high growth rate with definite signs of slowing down.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • What is the main reason in India for increasing population?Reduction in death rate

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Main reason for India's population growth → fall in death rate while birth rate stays high (2nd stage of demographic transition).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to Malthus, which one of the following is the most effective measure of population control?Birth control

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Malthus ('An Essay on the Principle of Population', 1798) → population grows geometrically, food arithmetically; best control: birth control through moral restraint. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid Population Grows Geometrically; food Adds Arithmetically.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Match list-I with list-II and select the correct answer using code given below the lists:3 4 1 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Optimum Population Theory → Edwin Cannan; Social Maladjustment → Henry George; Demographic Transition → Thompson; Population-Food Supply → Malthus.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R):(A) is true but (R) is false

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Population control is needed to protect the environment (A true); rapid population growth disturbs, not maintains, environmental balance (R false).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not a part of the demographic feature of a population?Standard of living

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Demographic features → density, sex-ratio, rural-urban population, literacy, age structure, life expectancy; standard of living is not one.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The highest density of population in India is associated with:Industrialized areas

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Highest population density in India (book) → industrialised areas such as Mumbai and Kolkata.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Some of the reasons for couples not willingly going for sterilization, which is a more reliable method for controlling population, are:All the four

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reasons couples avoid sterilisation → desire for male child, high child mortality, lack of understanding, economic compulsions (all four).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • From which year was regular and scientific Census started in India?1881

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      First synchronous, regular and scientific Census → 1881; earlier non-synchronous census 1865-1872; since then once every ten years. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • When was the Census work done for first time in India?In the year 1881

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      First census work in India → non-synchronous census of 1872; first synchronous census 1881 (book's answer).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • First Census in India was conducted in the year:1872

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      First modern Census → 1872, under Lord Mayo; first regular Census → 1881, under Lord Ripon. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid M before R: Mayo 1872, then Ripon 1881.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:(A) is true, but (R) is false

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Census → every ten years since 1881 (A true); population kept growing (fell only in 1921), so R false; 361.08 million (1951) → 1210.85 million (2011).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which among the following was used as the motto for Census of India 2011?Our Census, Our Future

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Census 2011 motto → 'Our Census, Our Future'; it was the 15th National Census.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • What is the minimum age of a person whose photographing, fingerprinting and iris mapping will be done for the Census of 2011?15 years

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Census 2011 / National Population Register → photograph, fingerprints and iris scan of persons aged 15 years and above.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Group of Ministers (GoM), who gave its approval for inclusion of Caste in Census 2011 was headed by:Pranab Mukherjee

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Group of Ministers that approved caste in Census 2011 → headed by then Finance Minister Pranab Mukherjee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • How many districts are in India?None of these

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Districts in India → 640 (Census 2011); 785 (June 2024).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • India's population growth during the 20th century can be classified into four distinct phases. Match List I (period) with List II (Phase) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:3 1 2 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Population phases → 1901-1921 stagnant; 1921-1951 steady; 1951-1981 rapid high growth; 1981-2001 high growth, slowing; lowest decadal growth 2001-2011 (17.7%, not 19.05). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to the Census of India 2011, the percentage growth of population in the country during the period of 2001-2011 was:17.70

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Census 2011 → decadal growth 2001-2011 was 17.7%; population 1028.74 million (2001) → 1210.85 million (2011). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The percentage of decadal growth of population during 2001-2011 as per Census 2011 is:None of the above/More than one of the above th nd

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Decadal growth 2001-2011 → 17.7% (final Census 2011 data); 17.64% was the provisional figure.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In which of the following Census year in India was recorded the highest percentage change in population?1971

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Highest decadal growth → 1961-71 (24.80%, Census 1971); 1981 → 24.66%, 1991 → 23.87%, 2001 → 21.54%, 2011 → 17.7%. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the context of population, which one of the following years has been termed as the year of 'Great Divide', after which population of India gradually registered accelerated growth?1921

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1921 → 'Great Divide' / 'Demographic Divide' year: the only Census with negative decadal growth (-0.31%); after it population grew at an accelerating pace. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid 1921: the one Census when India's population fell.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Assertion (A): India has experienced a phenomenal growth of population since 1951.A is true, but R is false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India's population grew phenomenally after 1951 (about 36 crore → over 102 crore by 2001) (A true); the 'Great Divide' year is 1921, not 1951 (R false).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The highest average annual exponential growth rate in India's population hasbeen recorded during the decade of:1971-81

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Highest average annual exponential growth → 1971-81 (2.22%); 1961-71 → 2.20%; 2001-11 → 1.64%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to the Census of2001, the annual exponential growth rate of the population in India during the last decade was:1.9 percent

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Average annual exponential growth 1991-2001 (Census 2001) → 1.97% (about 1.9%); 2001-2011 → 1.64%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements:Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1951-2001: population density 117 → 325 per sq km (under three times); growth rate 1.25% → 1.97% (not doubled). Census 2011: density 382, growth 1.64%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:1, 2 and 3 are correct

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India (question period): high growth rate; likely to overtake China (done, per UN 2024); one in six people is Indian; BPL was below 40% (21.92% in 2011-12).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • What is the total population of India?None of these th nd

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India's population → 1,028,737,436 (Census 2001) and 1,21,08,54,977 (Census 2011), so none of the options fits.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Population of India according to 1991 Census was:84.6 crore

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India's population, Census 1991 → 84.6 crore (846421039); Census 2011 → 1210854977; 1441.7 million in 2024, now the most populous country.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code below:1 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      India (Census 2001, book) → 16% of world population on 2.4% of Earth's land; adds 18 million a year to world population vs China's 10 million.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Don't swap the figures: 16% is population share, 2.4% is land share.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which one of the following is not true according to Census 2011?India accounts for 18.5% of the World Population.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following points does not figure in the 10-years Action Plan formulated under the National Population Policy?Special reward for men who adopt terminal family planning methods

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    NPP 10-year action plan: self-help groups, free compulsory education (6 to 14 years), compulsory registration of marriages and pregnancies; special awards to women, not men.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Consider the following statements:2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    India → first (not second) country with a National Family Planning Programme; NPP 2000: replacement fertility 2.1 by 2010 at about 111 crore; Kerala first State at replacement fertility.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • As per India’s National Population Policy, 2000, by which one of the following years is it our long-term objective to achieve population stabilization?2045

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    NPP 2000 → long-term goal: population stabilization by 2045 (later moved to 2070); medium-term: TFR to replacement level 2.1 by 2010. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse 2045 is the original NPP target; 2070 is the revised one. Read which the question wants.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)
