Open the chapter in the full notes for explanations.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A city is different from a village:All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          City differs from village in social values, household composition, way of living and economic activities (all four).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Urban growth is indicative of:All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Urban growth indicates rise in urban population, in number of urban centres, in total population and in urban income (all four).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following is NOT an element of rural community?Cultural diversity

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Cultural diversity → element of urban, not rural, community; rural community has we-feeling, territory, self-sufficiency.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following is not a feature of urban life?Informal ties

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Informal ties → not urban; urban life has competition, impersonal and formal relations, anonymity, loss of humanistic values, heterogeneity, market economy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • T.K. Oommen distinguished urban families through:all of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          T.K. Oommen (Indian sociologist) distinguished urban families by income source and changing values, structure of authority, and urban social milieu and social ecology (all).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following in relation to causes of urbanization and select the correct answer from the codes given below:1, 2 and 3 are correct

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Causes of urbanization → rural-urban migration (push and pull), more educational institutions in cities, industrialization; not high rural living standards. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following segments of population is not included in the scheme of inclusive development?Persons living in semi-urban areas

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Inclusive development (Economic Survey 2015-16) centres on marginal farmers, landless agricultural labourers, SC/ST; not persons in semi-urban areas.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • At current rate of growth, the urban population of India by the year 2030 will reach:575 million

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          India's urban population → 575 million by 2030 at current growth ('India 2018'); UN-Habitat 2022: 675.5 million by 2035.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In terms of Urbanization India is a:Moderately-low urbanized country

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          India → moderately-low urbanized country: 27.8% urban (2001), 31.1% (2011).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below:(A) is false, but (R) is true

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          India is not over-urbanized (only 31.1% urban: 377.1 of 1210.85 million, 2011) → A false; big cities lack adequate infrastructure → R true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Assertion (A): India’s level of urbanization is much lower than that of China.Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of(A)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          China far more urbanized than India (2005: 41% vs 29%; in 1950 India 17%, China 13%); poor planning true but not the reason → R not explanation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following statements is correct according to the Census 2001?All

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Census 2001, all true then: urban population 285 million (28.6 crore, 27.78%), more than USA's total population (28.14 crore); urbanization largely self-reliant. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Assertion (A): India's urban population exceeds the total population of USA.Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          India's urban population (28.6 crore, 2001) exceeded USA's total (28.14 crore) due to spectacular urban growth → A and R true, R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The expansion of Urban India is a platform for:All of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Urban expansion → platform for industrial growth, modern service sector growth and better income opportunities (all); cities run on secondary and tertiary activities.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Urbanization rose fast after 2001 (million-plus cities 35 → 53 in 2011); mobile revolution also true (tele-density 3.58% → 78.13%) but does not explain it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following statements regarding urbanization in India is not true?Urbanization of all regions in India has taken place in uniform manner.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Not true: 'urbanization is uniform' → it is very uneven: Goa most urbanized (over half urban), Himachal Pradesh least (10%).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • With reference to 'birth rate' which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?Both 1 and 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Both true: urbanization lowers birth rate (better family planning and healthcare access); higher literacy goes with lower birth rate.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Urbanization in India has:reduced both birth rate and death rate

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Urbanization in India → reduced both birth rate (more education and work) and death rate (better medical facilities).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Read the following statements and choose the correct option: Statement - I: First All India Census was attempted in 1871. Statement -II: From 1881 onwards decennial censuses became a regular feature. Statement -III: In forty years from 1900 to 1940, urban population increased from 10% of total population to 18%.Only Statement-II is true

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          First Census attempted 1872 (not 1871); regular decennial Census from 1881; urban share 1901-1941 rose 10.8% → 13.9% (not 18%) → only II true.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following periods is characterized by the stage of moderate urbanization in India?1931-1961

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Moderate urbanization stage → 1931-1961: urban population up 45.46 million (135.86%), urban share 12.2% → 18.3%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In India, the largest percentage of decadal growth of urbanization has been witnessed during:1971-81

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Largest decadal urban growth → 1971-81 (46.1%); 1961-71 38.2%, 1981-91 36.4%, 1991-2001 31.5%, 2001-2011 31.8%. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following criteria is not accepted to define any domicile in India as an urban center?Physical expansion

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Census urban criteria: statutory town, or population at least 5,000, 75% male workers non-agricultural, density 400/sq km. Physical expansion is not a criterion. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to 2011 Census, the total number of Census Towns in India is:3894

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Census Towns, Census 2011 → 3894 provisional, 3892 final (1362 in 2001); need 5000 people, 75% male non-farm workers, 400 persons/sq km.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • As per 2011 Census, the percentage of urban population to total population in India was:31.16

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          India's urban share, Census 2011 → 31.16% (provisional); final 31.1% (377106125 of 1210854977); rural 68.9%. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which religious group in India has its highest urban population?Jain

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Most urbanized religious group (Census 2011) → Jains (80% urban); Buddhists 43%, Muslims and Christians 40%, Hindus 29%, Sikhs 28%.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • More than one-fourth of India’s urban population lives in the two States of:Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Over one-fourth of India's urban population lives in Maharashtra (50818259) and Uttar Pradesh (44495063), Census 2011 (true in 2001 too).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           • The State with lowest urban population in India is:Sikkim

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Which of the following metros has the highest sex-ratio?Chennai

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest growth rate of urban population during:1971-81

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to the provisional figures of Census 2011 of India, the density of population is the highest in which of the following cities of U.P.?Ghaziabad

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Most densely populated city of UP, Census 2011 → Ghaziabad (3971 persons per sq km).

True: about 28% urban (27.8%, 2001); 1921 = demographic divide; Mumbai most populous metropolis.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to the Philip M. Hauser, the migration of people from rural areas to urban areas is known by which one of the following names:Population Implosion

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Philip M. Hauser → rural-to-urban migration and urban concentration = 'Population Implosion'; rapid population increase = 'Population Explosion'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Implosion = people pulled into cities; Explosion = rapid growth in numbers.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Migration theory with push and pull factors → Lee.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Assertion (A): In India, the increase in crime has gone up with an increase in urbanization and industrialization.Both A and Rare true and R is the correct explanation of A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Increasing Urbanization generates:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Increasing urbanization → more slum population, concentration in big cities, decline in quantity and quality of urban services; not fast infrastructure upgrade.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Revise: Nature of Indian Economy to Agriculture and Allied Sectors

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  42 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Mixed economy means:Where public sector and private sector co-exist in the national economy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Mixed economy → public sector and private sector co-exist in the national economy; blends market economy with planned economy. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Indian Economy is:Mixed economy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Indian economy → mixed economy (its main characteristic); combines aspects of capitalism and socialism. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse With socialist or Gandhian socialist economy; India is a mixed economy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following features indicates that Indian economy is in a developing category? I. Occupation is mainly agriculture II. Disguised unemployment III. Poor quality of human capital IV. High per capita intake ofproteins Select the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:I, II & III

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Developing economy signs → occupation mainly agriculture, disguised unemployment, poor quality of human capital; high per capita protein intake is not one. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The term National Income represents:Gross National Product at market prices minus depreciation and indirect taxes plus subsidies

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  National Income = NNP at factor cost = GNP at market prices – depreciation – indirect taxes + subsidies; NNP at market price = GNP – depreciation. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Memory aid Market price → factor cost: subtract indirect taxes, add subsidies.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Hindu rate of growth refers to the growth rate of:National Income

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Hindu rate of growth → slow growth of National Income/GDP (about 3.5%, 1950s–1980s); term first used by Prof. Raj Krishna, 1981. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Most appropriate measure of economic growth and of standard of living → per capita real income (Per Capita Product / per capita NNP). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • As per the NSSO 70th Round ‘Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households’, consider the following statements:1 and 3 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  NSSO 70th Round → 90.2 million agricultural households (57.8% of rural households); Rajasthan highest share; Kerala statement true; OBCs 'over 60 percent' false. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Assertion (A): Near self -sufficiency has been achieved in India in the production offoodgrains.Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of(A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Near self-sufficiency in foodgrains after Green Revolution: 50.8 MT (1950-51) → 211.9 MT (2001-02); no bulk imports → A, R true; R explains A. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • According to the report of CAG published in the year 2000 on PDS, the government subsidy on foodgrains increased from 1992-93 to 1998-99 by:more than three times

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  CAG report 2000 on PDS → food subsidy rose from Rs. 2800 crore (1992-93) to Rs. 8700 crore (1998-99), 3.1 times (more than three times). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which one of the following agricultural products fetches the largest foreign exchange for the country from its export?Basmati Rice

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Largest forex earner among options → Basmati rice; rice is the most valuable item in India's agricultural exports. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Preferred variety of Mango for export is:Alphonso

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Most preferred and most exported mango variety → Alphonso (Western India; Maharashtra main producer). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following is not the reason for low productivity in Indian agriculture?Co-operative farming

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Low farm productivity causes → population pressure, small holdings, disguised unemployment, uncertain monsoon; co-operative farming is not (it raises productivity). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Consider following statements about Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana and state which one of them is incorrect?Additional Central Assistance under the scheme would be available as 80% grant to the States

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana → launched August 2007; Rs. 25000 crore for 11th Plan; given as 100% central assistance (ACA), not 80% grant. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • National Horticulture Mission was launched in which of the following Five Year Plans?Tenth Five Year Plan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  National Horticulture Mission → started May 2005, in the 10th Five Year Plan; now a sub-scheme of MIDH (launched 2014-15). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following crops is not covered under the National Food Security Mission?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  NFSM → October 2007 (from Rabi 2007-08); target rice +10, wheat +8, pulses +2 million tons by 2011-12; coarse cereals not covered then. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 9 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Operation Flood is related to which of the following –Milk production

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Operation Flood (1970, NDDB) → milk production / White Revolution; Dr. Verghese Kurien → father of White Revolution. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The ‘blue revolution’is related with:fish production

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Blue Revolution → fish production (pisciculture); National Fisheries Development Board set up 2006, HQ Hyderabad. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Yellow Revolution is concerned with the production ofOilseeds

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Yellow Revolution → oilseeds (rapeseed-mustard); began 1986 with the Technology Mission on Oilseeds. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • National Agricultural Insurance Scheme replacing Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme was introduced in the year:1999

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  National Agricultural Insurance Scheme → from Rabi 1999-2000, replacing Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme (April 1, 1985); covers crop failure from calamities, pests, diseases. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Hariyali Yojana is related to:Water Management

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Hariyali scheme (January 2003, PM Vajpayee; Rs. 2000 crore) → water harvesting / watershed management; under Ministry of Rural Development. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • 'Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana' is related to:Thrust in export of agricultural products

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana → boost export of fruits, vegetables, flowers, minor forest produce, dairy, poultry; exporters get duty credit scrip (5 percent of FOB). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In which of the following States, the area under Tube-well irrigation is the highest?Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Largest area under tube-well irrigation → Uttar Pradesh. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • NAFED is mainly connected with:Agricultural marketing

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  NAFED (2 October 1958) → apex body of agricultural marketing cooperatives; under Ministry of Agriculture. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Which of the following organizations approves the Fair and Remunerative Price (F.R.P.) of the sugarcane?Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  FRP of sugarcane approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), on CACP's recommendation, after consulting States and sugar industry. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Don't confuse CACP only recommends the FRP; the CCEA approves it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Who determines the minimum support price in India?The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MSP recommended by Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP): set up January 1965 as Agricultural Prices Commission, renamed CACP in 1985. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The price at which the Government purchases foodgrains, is:Procurement Price

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Government buys foodgrains (for PDS and buffer stock) at Procurement Price, generally higher than MSP. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Must-know questions: 40

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Hour 56 →

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Hour 56 of 72 · Revise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Revise: Agriculture and Allied Sectors to Fiscal Policy & Revenue

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    42 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the followings is the largest source of agricultural credit in India in recent years?Commercial Banks

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Largest source of farm credit → Commercial Banks (about three-fourth; 53.7% in 1999-2000 → 76.86% in 2022-23); co-operatives fell from 39.5% to 10.80%. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Under the Kisan Credit Card scheme, short-term credit support is given to farmers for which of the following purposes?1, 3 and 4 only

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Kisan Credit Card (1998; NABARD model, R.V. Gupta Committee) → short-term credit for farm-asset working capital, household consumption, post-harvest expenses; not tractors, houses, cold storage. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order:4, 1, 2, 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Chronology → Regional Rural Banks (1975), NABARD (1982), SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (1992-93), Kisan Credit Card (1998). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • According to Fortune India List of 500 Companies/ Corporations, the biggest Company/Corporation in 2019 was:Reliance Industries Ltd.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Biggest company in Fortune India 500 list (2019 to 2023) → Reliance Industries; 2023: Indian Oil 2nd, LIC 3rd. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • With reference to the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), which of the statements is/are correct?Neither 1 nor 2

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    CSR made mandatory from April 1, 2014 (India first in world) by Section 135, Companies Act 2013 → two percent of average net profit of past three years. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Don't confuse Both statements wrong: the Act is of 2013 (not 2014) and the spend is two percent (not one).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • When was the National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) released by the Government of India?4 November, 2011

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    National Manufacturing Policy → 4 November 2011; manufacturing to 25% of GDP within a decade, 100 million jobs, 12-14% sector growth. Must know
