                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Who is the Chairman of the 10th Finance Commission?K.C. Pant

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Finance Commission chairmen: 1st K.C. Neogy (1951); 9th N.K.P. Salve; 10th K.C. Pant; 11th A.M. Khusro; 12th C. Rangarajan; Thirteenth Kelkar; Fourteenth Y.V. Reddy; 15th N.K. Singh. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 8 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The extent of money transfer to the States out ofsharable pool of tax collection according to the 12th Finance Commission has been fixed at:30.5 percent

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      12th Finance Commission (Dr. C. Rangarajan, 1st November 2002) → States' share 30.5% of net Union taxes (11th FC: 29.5%). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Committee which has recommended abolition of Tax Rebates under Section 88 of Income Tax Act of India, is:Kelkar Committee

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Kelkar Task Force on Direct Taxes → recommended removing tax rebate under Section 88 (also 80L and Section 10 interest income); final report December 2002. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Kelkar (direct-tax task force, 2002) with Chelliah, Shome or Rangarajan committees.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Recent tax reforms in India have been undertaken on the recommendations of the committee headed by:R. J. Chelliah

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1990s tax reforms → Tax Reforms Committee under Raja J. Chelliah (1991), covering direct and indirect taxes; made direct taxes the major tax revenue component. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Under the Constitution of India, Economic Planning is a subject:In the Concurrent List

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Economic and Social Planning → Concurrent List (List-3), Seventh Schedule; both Union and States can legislate. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Development, Monitoring and Evaluation Office, which monitors the progress of long term policies in an attached office under:NITI Aayog

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      DMEO → attached office of NITI Aayog, set up 18 September 2015 by merging PEO and IEO; monitors and evaluates government programmes. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • National Development Council:Reviews the National Plans

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      National Development Council (6 August 1952), chaired by Prime Minister → reviewed and approved Five Year Plans drafted by Planning Commission. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse Planning Commission drafted the Plan; NDC approved it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 11 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In which year was the 'Planning Commission' set up in India?1950

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Planning Commission → set up March 1950 by Cabinet Resolution; advisory, non-constitutional body (also called quasi-political). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • NITI Aayog came into existence on:1st January, 2015

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) → 1 January 2015, by Cabinet Resolution, replacing Planning Commission; a public policy think tank. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid NITI Aayog was born on New Year's Day 2015.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Who was the first Vice-Chairman of the NITI Aayog?Arvind Panagariya

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      First Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog → Arvind Panagariya (January 2015 to August 2017); Suman Bery since 1 May 2022. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Planning was considered Prerequisite:All the four

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Planning needed for → balanced socio-economic development, even spread of benefits, removing regional disparities, maximum use of resources (all four). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Gandhian Plan was expounded in 1944 by:Shriman Narayan Agarwal

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Gandhian Plan (1944) → Shriman Narayan Agarwal; small-unit production, agriculture, decentralisation, self-contained villages, cottage industries. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Consider the following about the 'Rolling Plan': I. A plan for the current year which includes the annual budget II. A plan for a fixed number of years, say 3, 4 or 5 III. It is revised every year as per requirements of the economy IV. A perspective plan for 10, 15 or 20 years Which of the above are correct?I, II, III and IV

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Rolling Plan (Gunnar Myrdal) → three plans: current-year plan with budget; plan of 3-5 years revised every year; perspective plan of 10-20 years. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid A Rolling Plan 'rolls forward' one year at a time.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The 'Rolling Plan' concept in National Planning was introduced by:The Janata Government

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Rolling Plan in India → Janata Party Government, 1978-79, after rejecting Fifth Five Year Plan; flexible, revised yearly. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The period of the 12th Five-Year Plan is:2012-2017

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      12th Five Year Plan → 2012-2017; theme 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'; 2016-17 was its last year. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • During the 12th Five Year Plan, the growth rate of agriculture, forestry and fish farming has been estimated to be:4.0%

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      12th Plan target growth for agriculture, forestry and fisheries → 4.0 percent a year. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the 12th Five Year Plan, which among the following has largest allocation of funds?Social Services

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      12th Plan largest allocation → Social Services (2664843 crore, about 34.7 percent of outlay); Energy 18.8 percent. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In India, which of the following Five Year Plans was launched with a focus on sustainable growth?12th

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      12th Plan (2012-17) → 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'; 11th Plan (2007-12) → 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Memory aid 12th Plan adds 'Sustainable' to the 11th Plan's theme.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Eleventh Five Year Plan emphasized on:Faster and more inclusive growth

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      11th Five Year Plan (2007-12) → 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Don't confuse With 12th Plan's 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • In the Eleventh Five Year Plan highest allocation has been made for:Energy sector

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      11th Plan highest allocation → social services, then energy sector; among the options, energy. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Hour 58 →

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Hour 58 of 72 · Revise

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Revise: Planning to Money and Banking

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        42 Must-know facts. Say each one aloud before you read it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Cover each line, recall it, then check. Answer the questions below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The rate fixed for industrial development in the Eleventh Plan is:10.5 percent

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        11th Plan targets → GDP 9%; agriculture 4% (double the 10th Plan's 2%); industry 10.5 percent (10% to 11%, up from 9.2%). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The annual growth rate of the economy as envisaged in the mid-term appraisal of the 10th plan is:7.0 percent

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        10th Plan (2002-07) → growth target 8 percent; cut to 7 percent in mid-term appraisal; actual 7.6 percent. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Original target (8%) with mid-term appraisal figure (7%).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Tenth Five Year Plan targets the highest growth rate in:Communication

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Tenth Plan highest target growth → communication (15%); financial services 11.69%; manufacturing 9.82%; trade 9.44%; agriculture 3.97%. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The growth rate percentage for the 9th Five Year Plan has been targeted:6.5%

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        9th Plan → growth target 6.5 percent; actual 5.4 percent; theme 'Growth with Social Justice and Equity'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Seventh Five Year Plan ended in March 1990, the Eighth Five Year Plan started in:April 1992

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        7th Plan ended 31 March 1990; 1990-91 and 1991-92 were Annual Plans; 8th Plan ran April 1992 to March 1997. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following Five Year Plans of India recognized human development as the core of developmental efforts?Eighth Five Year Plan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        8th Plan → recognised 'human development' as core of all development efforts; aimed at near-full employment. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • What is the annual growth rate aimed at in the Eighth Five Year Plan?5.6%

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        8th Plan (1992-97), delayed two years → target growth 5.6 percent; actual 6.8 percent. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which Plan among the following declared its objective of self-reliance and zero net foreign aid?Fifth five Year Plan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Fifth Plan → twin aims: removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance (zero net foreign aid). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The slogan of‘Poverty abolition’ was given in which Five Year Plan?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        'Garibi Hatao' → Indira Gandhi's 1971 election slogan, during 4th Plan (1969-74); poverty removal became main objective of 5th Plan (UPPSC answer: 5th Plan). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Under which Five Year Plan was the decision to establish a socialistic pattern of society taken?Second Five Year Plan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Socialistic pattern of society → 2nd Plan (1956-61), on P.C. Mahalanobis model; rapid industrialisation with heavy and basic industries. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid Second Plan is also called the 'Mahalanobis Plan'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Mahalanobis Plan Model adopted in India in the midfifties aimed at:Setting up heavy industries which were capital intensive

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Mahalanobis model (2nd Plan, 1956-61) → rapid industrialisation through capital-intensive heavy and basic industries; agriculture lower priority. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid Mahalanobis = Machines (heavy industry).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • During the planning periods, the highest growth rate was achieved during the:Tenth plan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Highest growth among Seventh to Tenth Plans → Tenth Plan; across all Plans, the Eleventh Plan recorded the highest growth. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 'Twenty Point Economic Programme' was first launched in the year:1975

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Twenty Point Programme → launched 1975; revised 1982 and 1986; restructured 2006; aim: poverty eradication and better quality of life. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Consider the following:1, 2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Broad Money (M3) = currency with public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with RBI + time deposits with banks. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid M3 = M1 + time deposits with banks.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Money multiplier in India is defined as:Base Money Reserve Money Reserve Money Base Money

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Money multiplier in India = Broad Money (M3) ÷ Reserve Money (high-powered money, M0 or R). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • When did the ‘Naya paisa’ introduced with the decimal system of coinage become, paisa?June 1, 1964

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Decimal coinage → 1 April 1957 ('Naya paisa'); 'Naya' dropped from 1 June 1964, becoming just 'paisa'. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Note issuing department of RBI should always possess the minimum gold stock of worth:Rs 115 crore

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Note issue → Minimum Reserve System (1956, amended 1957): gold plus foreign securities at least Rs. 200 crore, gold at least Rs. 115 crore. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who is authorized to issue coins in India?Ministry of Finance

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Coins issued by Government of India (Ministry of Finance), circulated by RBI; four mints: Mumbai, Noida, Kolkata, Hyderabad. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse RBI issues notes; Ministry of Finance issues coins.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Inflation is beneficial to which of the following section of economy?Debtors

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Inflation helps debtors (repay with cheaper money); creditors, fixed-interest bond investors, consumers and pensioners lose in real terms. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid Inflation is the borrower's friend, the lender's enemy.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The most common measure of estimating inflation in India is:Consumer Price Index

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Headline inflation → CPI (Combined), base 2012 = 100; RBI adopted it as key measure in April 2014, replacing WPI. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse Old answers say WPI; since April 2014 the answer is CPI-Combined.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 6 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The base of Consumer Price Index for industrial workers has been shifted from 1982 to:2001

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        CPI-IW base years → 1960 → 1982 (from 1988) → 2001 (from 2006) → 2016 (from September 2020); compiled by Labour Bureau. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The basis of determining dearness allowances to employees of India is:Consumer Price Index

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Dearness allowance of employees fixed using Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • With reference to the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), consider the following statements:2 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        WPI base 1993-94 = 100 came in April 2000, not 1998; it cut primary articles' weight, raised electricity's. Base 2011-12: manufactured 64.23%, primary 22.62%, fuel 13.15%. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The new WPI series was introduced on:14 September, 2010

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        WPI with base 2004-05 → released 14 September 2010; base revised to 2011-12 on 12 May 2017 (effective April 2017). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • In the context of independent India’s economy, which one of the following was the earliest event to take place?Enactment of Banking Regulation Act

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Earliest → Banking Regulation Act (10 March 1949); then First Plan (1951), SBI (July 1955), life insurance nationalised (1956), general insurance (1972). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Government of India has nationalized 14 banks of the country in:July, 1969

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Bank nationalisation → 14 major banks (assets above Rs. 50 crore) in July 1969; six more on 15 April 1980. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The largest commercial bank of India is:State Bank of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Largest commercial bank in India → State Bank of India (HQ Mumbai; 22,406 branches, 65,627 ATMs/CRMs as on 31 March 2023). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following bank has formed ‘farmers clubs’ to reach out to the farmers easily?State Bank of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SBI with NABARD formed 'Farmers Club' (Kishan club) in Uttar Pradesh to reach farmers and raise their bargaining power. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Since April, 2011, the SBI’s Chairman has been:Pratip Chaudhuri

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SBI Chairman from 7 April 2011 → Pratip Chaudhuri (till 30 September 2013); Dinesh Kumar Khara from October 2020; Challa Sreenivasulu Setty selected 29 June 2024. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which bank became the first bank to open its branch in China?State Bank of India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        First Indian bank to open a branch in China → State Bank of India (2006). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse First Indian private bank branch in China → Axis Bank (Shanghai).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following four Foreign Banks operating in India, has the largest number of branches in the country?Standard Chartered Bank

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Foreign bank with most branches in India → Standard Chartered (UK, 100); HSBC 26, Deutsche 17, Citibank 14, BNP Paribas 5. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The 'Lead Bank' Scheme was launched in:December, 1969

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Lead Bank Scheme → RBI, December 1969, from Gadgil Study Group and Nariman Committee; a designated bank leads credit development in each district. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following banks operates mainly in relation to small industries?SIDBI

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SIDBI → set up 2 April 1990 by Act of Parliament; HQ Lucknow; principal institution for financing and developing MSME (small industries). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Memory aid SIDBI's head office is in Lucknow, UP.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 5 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who among the following was the Chairman of the ‘Committee on Financial Inclusion’ constituted in January 2005?C. Rangarajan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Committee on Financial Inclusion → Dr. C. Rangarajan (constituted June 26, 2006; final report January 4, 2008). Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which one of the following statements is not correct?RBI was established in 1949.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        RBI → established April 1, 1935 (RBI Act 1934), not 1949; nationalised 1949; HQ Kolkata, moved to Mumbai 1937; Governments' banker, forex custodian. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Don't confuse 1935 = founded; 1949 = nationalised. Don't swap them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 7 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the Reserve Bank of India?It issues all types of currency notes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        RBI does not issue all notes: one rupee note issued by Government of India, signed by Finance Secretary; other notes signed by RBI Governor. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 4 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Who formulates the monetary policy in India?—

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Monetary policy → formulated by RBI till 2016; now Monetary Policy Committee sets policy rate, aided by RBI's Monetary Policy Department; RBI keeps price stability. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)
